codex-t1-c8.title: Chapter 8 — Nothing More Ordinary Than a Planetary Road Trip
codex-t1-c8.html:
The trip lasted barely a few minutes — just long enough to cross distances that, in any human ship, would have taken months. The ship touched down with a slight jolt in front of a massive door carved right into the red rock, and they had barely stepped off before it took off again instantly, vanishing into the dusty sky without a word of goodbye.

Fifteen guards sprang up immediately, surrounding the little group, their rifles — of a strange shape, their barrels gleaming with an unsettling bluish light — trained on them with flawless military precision.

— State the reason for your visit! one of them barked, his finger on the trigger. Immediately!

Takeshi instinctively raised his hands, his heart pounding wildly, while Isidora simply put her phone away calmly, a smile still hanging on her lips in the face of the barrels aimed at her.

— We have an appointment with your boss, she said with perfect nonchalance. Red point, ring a bell?

The guards stepped aside, lowering their weapons in an almost mechanical, synchronized movement, and the massive door opened onto an interior that contrasted violently with the reddish aridity of the Martian surface. Metal corridors stretched as far as the eye could see, lit by a cold white light. Dozens of soldiers stood at attention along the walls, some visibly human, others clearly modified — overdeveloped muscles, skin almost translucent in places. Robots patrolled among them, silent, their joints making barely a mechanical hiss. Farther off, stooped, gaunt figures pushed carts or dragged crates without ever raising their eyes — slaves, Takeshi understood with a shiver.

At the center of this organized ballet, a figure was already waiting for them, motionless, as if time itself had stopped around him.

Agent 47.

A perfectly tailored black suit, a blood-red tie, immaculate white gloves in stark contrast with the silenced pistol he held casually in one hand, barrel pointed at the floor. His face betrayed absolutely nothing — no surprise, no suspicion, not the slightest trace of emotion at the arrival of a king of Hell, a witch of the Void, an ancient demon, and a visibly terrified human.

— Follow me, he said in a perfectly neutral, almost monotone voice. The Boss is in the laboratory.

He turned on his heel without waiting for an answer, his footsteps echoing with almost hypnotic regularity on the metal floor. Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, unable to tear his eyes from this figure who, he now knew, had once survived a shot from the White Death himself.

— That's... that's him, he murmured to Alastor. The God of Death.

— Yup, Alastor confirmed in a low voice, his usual smile completely gone for the first time since they had met. And believe me, little human, now's the time to shut your mouth and walk.

Isidora put her phone away for good, her offhand air fading in turn, an unusual seriousness settling on her features as she fell into step behind Agent 47, followed closely by Lucifer, whose usual smile had also disappeared.

The group went deeper into the corridors of the base in silence, every guard, every robot, every slave they passed instinctively stepping aside as they went by — not out of respect, Takeshi understood, but out of a learned caution, the kind you reserve for what was walking in front: a man who had never missed a target.

The corridors stretched on, deeper and deeper, the air gradually filling with an acrid smell — chemical, almost burned. Screams rang out intermittently behind some closed doors, muffled, long, sometimes punctuated by an even more unsettling silence. Takeshi kept his eyes fixed straight ahead, no longer even daring to glance at the doors those sounds came from, his throat too tight to ask a single question.

Agent 47 guided them without a word, his stride always perfectly even, until they finally came out into a vast room lit by a harsh white light, packed with machines, holographic screens and tanks filled with liquids of improbable colors.

Grand Patron Luigi stood in the middle of the room, a phone in his hand, taking photos of various installations with almost childish enthusiasm, while two men in white coats — the famous German scientists — directed a dozen technicians busily working at several stations at once, trading technical terms at a speed and in a jargon Takeshi didn't understand at all.

— No, no, put the stabilizer on the left, one of the scientists was saying urgently, otherwise the resonance frequency will throw the whole quantum field out of sync again.

— We said seventeen point three, not eighteen, the other barked at a technician who was hastily adjusting a dial.

Agent 47 stopped a few meters from Grand Patron Luigi, standing back, silent, visibly waiting for his boss to notice their presence on his own rather than interrupting him.

Takeshi watched the scene, completely overwhelmed by the scale of what he was seeing — technology beyond anything he could have imagined possible, machines softly humming around them, and at the center of it all, this seemingly ordinary man who, with a single word, could wipe entire realities out of existence.

Grand Patron Luigi raised a finger without even turning around, his eyes still riveted on his screen.

— Hold on, 47, I'm posting on Insta, then we can get started, he said, his thumb rapidly scrolling through a series of hashtags.

He tapped the screen one last time, a faint beep confirming the post, before finally putting the phone in his pocket with visible satisfaction.

Isidora, for her part, had already moved closer, a sudden interest replacing her outward seriousness.

— Wait, what's your account? she asked, pulling her own phone out again. I've gotta follow, no question.

Grand Patron Luigi finally turned toward them, a perfectly rehearsed salesman's smile spreading across his face, as if he had been waiting for that question from the start.

— @GrandPatronLuigiOfficiel, he said proudly. Six billion followers on every platform, you can't miss it.

— Oh yeah, I didn't recognize you without the filter, Isidora answered, already typing the name, a little laugh escaping her.

He burst out laughing in turn, a loud and strangely warm laugh for someone whose cosmic reputation came down to an incalculable body count, before finally turning his attention to the whole group, his gaze lingering a moment longer on Takeshi, a glint of curiosity passing through his eyes.

— Well, he said, spreading his arms, satisfied, so we've got some fine company coming all the way to my place. What can I do for you, my little ones?

Isidora stepped forward, regaining her usual composure despite the heavy aura reigning in the room.

— Actually, she said, we need your help to go to a weird dimension where everything that doesn't exist exists. Like Lucifer's fashion sense. But even there, that's probably nonexistent.

— Hey, Lucifer protested without much conviction, clearly used to that kind of jab.

Grand Patron Luigi let out a little smirk, his arms slowly crossing, a calculating interest gradually replacing his salesman's smile.

— I suppose you want to find something, he said, besides the king of Hell's charisma, which is indeed nonexistent. What do you want?

Isidora exchanged a brief look with Lucifer, then with Alastor, before answering, her tone becoming a little more serious.

— The Dimension of Shadows, she said. We know 81 is locked up there. And maybe also my nephew's father, here, she added, nodding toward Takeshi.

Grand Patron Luigi's smile vanished instantly at the mention of the name, a heavy silence settling over the laboratory, the scientists themselves pausing their work, as if the air had suddenly become charged with a palpable tension.

— 81, he repeated slowly, his gaze hardening. Do you even know what you're asking?

Agent 47, who had stayed silent in the background until then, turned his head slightly toward his boss, the only perceptible reaction from him since their arrival.

Grand Patron Luigi's smirk reappeared at once, as quickly as it had vanished, an amused glint crossing his eyes.

— Nah, just kidding, relax, he said, waving a casual hand. I can give you something to get there if you want. Well, give you a solution. So I'll keep it short: basically, I own a star that I created. Actually it's a black star, and it's a portal to that very dimension. So you just have to go inside it.

A stunned silence greeted this announcement, Isidora herself left speechless for a moment before regaining her composure.

— Wait, seriously? she said. I spent months looking for a way into that dimension, and you're just telling me "yeah, I've got a star for that, no biggie"?

— Well, yeah, Grand Patron Luigi answered with a shrug, as if the remark made no sense. I've got stuff everywhere. Keep up.

Lucifer, who had stayed silent until then, frowned, suspicion clearly showing in his voice.

— And why would you help us, just like that, for free? he asked. That's not exactly your style.

Grand Patron Luigi's smile grew even wider, almost delighted to finally be asked the question he had been waiting for.

— Ah, he said, pointing at Lucifer. Now that's a good question. Because no, obviously, it's not free.

He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his announcement, before going on, his gaze sliding toward Takeshi with renewed interest.

— I have a little favor to ask of you in return. Nothing too nasty. Well, depends who you ask.

Grand Patron Luigi spread his arms, a radiant smile spreading across his face, as if he were about to announce the most important revelation of the day.

— All I want, he said, is for each of you to follow my accounts. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X. All four. That's not much to ask, is it?

A stunned silence once again greeted this statement, Takeshi blinking, unable to tell whether the man was serious.

— That's... that's your condition? he asked finally. To access a cosmic dimension that erases everything forgotten? An Instagram follow?

— And TikTok, Grand Patron Luigi specified, raising a finger. And YouTube. And X. All four, I said.

Isidora already had her phone in hand, typing frantically.

— Oh, that's been done for like ten minutes, she said with a satisfied smile, turning the screen toward him to prove it.

Lucifer sighed long and hard, pulling out his own phone with a clearly reluctant slowness.

— I have never hated my life as much as I do right now, he muttered, looking for the app.

Alastor, for his part, burst out laughing, a sincere sound that contrasted with the tension built up since their arrival on Mars.

— Honestly, he said, complying in turn, it's the simplest deal we've ever gotten from a cosmic lunatic. I'm not gonna complain.

Grand Patron Luigi watched the scene with obvious satisfaction, almost counting out loud the new follower notifications popping up on his own phone.

— And there we go, he said at last, putting the phone away. Follow 47, he'll show you the star. And be careful going in there, okay — I've never tested it on living beings, so you're the guinea pigs.

Agent 47 started moving again without a word, turning on his heel with that same mechanical regularity that never seemed to leave him. The group followed him through a new series of corridors, deeper still, the white lighting gradually giving way to a dimmer, almost bluish light, while the hum of the machines grew louder the farther they went.

Takeshi, walking at the back, glanced at Alastor.

— "I've never tested it on living beings," he repeated in a low voice, a hint of panic in his voice. He really said that, right? I didn't dream it?

— No, you didn't dream it, Alastor confirmed with a smile that was anything but reassuring.

— And nobody finds that worrying? Takeshi pressed, glancing at Isidora and Lucifer walking ahead, apparently not the least bit bothered.

— Little human, Alastor answered, you've already died once today. At this point, a second time wouldn't change much about your day.

They finally came out into an immense circular hall, its center occupied by a massive structure, a metal ring surrounding a control point where several technicians were already at work, alerted by their arrival. Agent 47 stopped dead in front of the ring, finally turning toward them, his face still devoid of the slightest expression.

— The black star is stored inside this ring, in compressed form, he said, his voice as neutral as if he were reciting a technical manual. Once activated, it will generate a direct access. You will have thirty seconds to enter before the contact point closes.

Isidora walked up to the ring, whistling softly in admiration as she looked over the structure.

— Thirty seconds, she repeated. Nice margin for error.

— It's already more than the Boss originally planned, 47 answered without the slightest perceptible trace of irony.

Lucifer stepped forward in turn, his eyes scanning the ring with obvious suspicion.

— And once we're on the other side, he said, do we have any idea what's waiting for us?

— No, 47 answered simply. No data exists on the interior of the Dimension of Shadows.

The silence that followed this answer weighed heavily on the little group, everyone exchanging a look that betrayed, for the first time since their arrival on Mars, a shared worry.
codex-t1-c8.text: The trip lasted barely a few minutes — just long enough to cross distances that, in any human ship, would have taken months. The ship touched down with a slight jolt in front of a massive door carved right into the red rock, and they had barely stepped off before it took off again instantly, vanishing into the dusty sky without a word of goodbye. Fifteen guards sprang up immediately, surrounding the little group, their rifles — of a strange shape, their barrels gleaming with an unsettling bluish light — trained on them with flawless military precision. — State the reason for your visit! one of them barked, his finger on the trigger. Immediately! Takeshi instinctively raised his hands, his heart pounding wildly, while Isidora simply put her phone away calmly, a smile still hanging on her lips in the face of the barrels aimed at her. — We have an appointment with your boss, she said with perfect nonchalance. Red point, ring a bell? The guards stepped aside, lowering their weapons in an almost mechanical, synchronized movement, and the massive door opened onto an interior that contrasted violently with the reddish aridity of the Martian surface. Metal corridors stretched as far as the eye could see, lit by a cold white light. Dozens of soldiers stood at attention along the walls, some visibly human, others clearly modified — overdeveloped muscles, skin almost translucent in places. Robots patrolled among them, silent, their joints making barely a mechanical hiss. Farther off, stooped, gaunt figures pushed carts or dragged crates without ever raising their eyes — slaves, Takeshi understood with a shiver. At the center of this organized ballet, a figure was already waiting for them, motionless, as if time itself had stopped around him. Agent 47. A perfectly tailored black suit, a blood-red tie, immaculate white gloves in stark contrast with the silenced pistol he held casually in one hand, barrel pointed at the floor. His face betrayed absolutely nothing — no surprise, no suspicion, not the slightest trace of emotion at the arrival of a king of Hell, a witch of the Void, an ancient demon, and a visibly terrified human. — Follow me, he said in a perfectly neutral, almost monotone voice. The Boss is in the laboratory. He turned on his heel without waiting for an answer, his footsteps echoing with almost hypnotic regularity on the metal floor. Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, unable to tear his eyes from this figure who, he now knew, had once survived a shot from the White Death himself. — That's... that's him, he murmured to Alastor. The God of Death. — Yup, Alastor confirmed in a low voice, his usual smile completely gone for the first time since they had met. And believe me, little human, now's the time to shut your mouth and walk. Isidora put her phone away for good, her offhand air fading in turn, an unusual seriousness settling on her features as she fell into step behind Agent 47, followed closely by Lucifer, whose usual smile had also disappeared. The group went deeper into the corridors of the base in silence, every guard, every robot, every slave they passed instinctively stepping aside as they went by — not out of respect, Takeshi understood, but out of a learned caution, the kind you reserve for what was walking in front: a man who had never missed a target. The corridors stretched on, deeper and deeper, the air gradually filling with an acrid smell — chemical, almost burned. Screams rang out intermittently behind some closed doors, muffled, long, sometimes punctuated by an even more unsettling silence. Takeshi kept his eyes fixed straight ahead, no longer even daring to glance at the doors those sounds came from, his throat too tight to ask a single question. Agent 47 guided them without a word, his stride always perfectly even, until they finally came out into a vast room lit by a harsh white light, packed with machines, holographic screens and tanks filled with liquids of improbable colors. Grand Patron Luigi stood in the middle of the room, a phone in his hand, taking photos of various installations with almost childish enthusiasm, while two men in white coats — the famous German scientists — directed a dozen technicians busily working at several stations at once, trading technical terms at a speed and in a jargon Takeshi didn't understand at all. — No, no, put the stabilizer on the left, one of the scientists was saying urgently, otherwise the resonance frequency will throw the whole quantum field out of sync again. — We said seventeen point three, not eighteen, the other barked at a technician who was hastily adjusting a dial. Agent 47 stopped a few meters from Grand Patron Luigi, standing back, silent, visibly waiting for his boss to notice their presence on his own rather than interrupting him. Takeshi watched the scene, completely overwhelmed by the scale of what he was seeing — technology beyond anything he could have imagined possible, machines softly humming around them, and at the center of it all, this seemingly ordinary man who, with a single word, could wipe entire realities out of existence. Grand Patron Luigi raised a finger without even turning around, his eyes still riveted on his screen. — Hold on, 47, I'm posting on Insta, then we can get started, he said, his thumb rapidly scrolling through a series of hashtags. He tapped the screen one last time, a faint beep confirming the post, before finally putting the phone in his pocket with visible satisfaction. Isidora, for her part, had already moved closer, a sudden interest replacing her outward seriousness. — Wait, what's your account? she asked, pulling her own phone out again. I've gotta follow, no question. Grand Patron Luigi finally turned toward them, a perfectly rehearsed salesman's smile spreading across his face, as if he had been waiting for that question from the start. — @GrandPatronLuigiOfficiel , he said proudly. Six billion followers on every platform, you can't miss it. — Oh yeah, I didn't recognize you without the filter, Isidora answered, already typing the name, a little laugh escaping her. He burst out laughing in turn, a loud and strangely warm laugh for someone whose cosmic reputation came down to an incalculable body count, before finally turning his attention to the whole group, his gaze lingering a moment longer on Takeshi, a glint of curiosity passing through his eyes. — Well, he said, spreading his arms, satisfied, so we've got some fine company coming all the way to my place. What can I do for you, my little ones? Isidora stepped forward, regaining her usual composure despite the heavy aura reigning in the room. — Actually, she said, we need your help to go to a weird dimension where everything that doesn't exist exists. Like Lucifer's fashion sense. But even there, that's probably nonexistent. — Hey, Lucifer protested without much conviction, clearly used to that kind of jab. Grand Patron Luigi let out a little smirk, his arms slowly crossing, a calculating interest gradually replacing his salesman's smile. — I suppose you want to find something, he said, besides the king of Hell's charisma, which is indeed nonexistent. What do you want? Isidora exchanged a brief look with Lucifer, then with Alastor, before answering, her tone becoming a little more serious. — The Dimension of Shadows, she said. We know 81 is locked up there. And maybe also my nephew's father, here, she added, nodding toward Takeshi. Grand Patron Luigi's smile vanished instantly at the mention of the name, a heavy silence settling over the laboratory, the scientists themselves pausing their work, as if the air had suddenly become charged with a palpable tension. — 81, he repeated slowly, his gaze hardening. Do you even know what you're asking? Agent 47, who had stayed silent in the background until then, turned his head slightly toward his boss, the only perceptible reaction from him since their arrival. Grand Patron Luigi's smirk reappeared at once, as quickly as it had vanished, an amused glint crossing his eyes. — Nah, just kidding, relax, he said, waving a casual hand. I can give you something to get there if you want. Well, give you a solution. So I'll keep it short: basically, I own a star that I created. I've got stuff everywhere. Keep up. Lucifer, who had stayed silent until then, frowned, suspicion clearly showing in his voice. — And why would you help us, just like that, for free? he asked. That's not exactly your style. Grand Patron Luigi's smile grew even wider, almost delighted to finally be asked the question he had been waiting for. — Ah, he said, pointing at Lucifer. Now that's a good question. Because no, obviously, it's not free. He let the silence hang for a moment, visibly savoring the effect of his announcement, before going on, his gaze sliding toward Takeshi with renewed interest. — I have a little favor to ask of you in return. Nothing too nasty. Well, depends who you ask. Grand Patron Luigi spread his arms, a radiant smile spreading across his face, as if he were about to announce the most important revelation of the day. — All I want, he said, is for each of you to follow my accounts. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X. All four. That's not much to ask, is it? A stunned silence once again greeted this statement, Takeshi blinking, unable to tell whether the man was serious. — That's... that's your condition? he asked finally. To access a cosmic dimension that erases everything forgotten? An Instagram follow? — And TikTok, Grand Patron Luigi specified, raising a finger. And YouTube. And X. All four, I said. At this point, a second time wouldn't change much about your day. codex-t1-c9.title: Chapter 9 — Full of Bullshit!
codex-t1-c9.html:
Agent 47 activated a mechanism on the control panel, and the metal ring began to vibrate, a deep hum rapidly intensifying until it became almost unbearable. At its center, the air tore open, revealing a sphere so deeply black that it seemed to suck in the light of the entire room.

— Thirty seconds, 47 repeated. Now.

Without another word, Isidora was the first to leap in, followed closely by Lucifer, then Alastor, dragging Takeshi along with a firm grip. The sensation of crossing over was different from all the previous ones — an absolute void, with no direction, no up or down, as if their very existence had been momentarily suspended between two realities.

Then, as abruptly as the passage had begun, they emerged on the other side.

Takeshi immediately felt his feet sink into something cold and liquid — a thin film of water, barely a few centimeters deep, covering a ground he couldn't clearly identify, neither stone nor earth, something in between, that almost rippled under his steps as if it weren't entirely solid.

Above them, the sky — if you could still call it a sky — was nothing but a black gloom, without stars, without clouds, without the slightest identifiable source of light, and yet they could see everything clearly, as if light itself no longer really made sense here. Shapes crossed that darkness intermittently — blurry, indescribable silhouettes, some vaguely resembling objects, others creatures, still others nothing recognizable at all, gliding silently through the void without ever seeming to have any particular direction.

Takeshi turned in place, desperately searching for a horizon, a boundary, anything that would show where this place ended — but there was nothing. No beginning, no end. Just that expanse of shallow water stretching as far as the eye could see in every direction, under that sky of darkness peopled with forgotten things.

— What... what is all this? he murmured, his voice echoing strangely, as if absorbed by the surrounding void before it even fully reached his own ears.

Isidora, for her part, stood motionless, watching the shapes float above them with an expression he had never seen on her before — something that looked, for the first time, like sincere worry.

— The Dimension of Shadows, she said softly. We're here.

Isidora took out her phone, the screen lighting up in the surrounding darkness — then her face fell slightly.

— Wait, there's no signal here?! she exclaimed, waving the phone around as if that would magically make a signal bar appear. Like, I got signal IN HELL, but not here?!

She tapped frantically at the screen, turning in circles in search of a phantom signal, her look of utter disaster contrasting violently with the gravity of the place.

— This is a joke, she said. How am I supposed to post a story if there's no signal? That's the worst part of this dimension. NO SIGNAL!

Lucifer, standing back, rolled his eyes up to the sky — well, to what passed for one.

— We've just entered a dimension where everything the entire universe has forgotten ends up disappearing, he said, and your one concern is your Instagram account.

— My priorities are clear, yes, Isidora answered without the slightest embarrassment, finally tucking the phone into a fold of her cape with a disappointed sigh. Fine. Whatever. I'll catch up later. "Sorry guys, I was stuck in the absolute void, milk milk lemonade."

Alastor let out a dry little laugh, while Takeshi stayed frozen, his eyes relentlessly sweeping the infinite expanse around them, a chilling certainty gradually settling in him that here, in this place with no beginning and no end, finding anything at all — 81, his father, or even simply the way back — was going to prove much harder than expected.

Isidora slowly turned in place, scanning the shifting darkness around them, her tone gradually becoming serious again.

— Okay, now we need to figure out where you find a god killer in an infinite dimension, she said. Because right now, look as I might, I don't really see any signposts.

— Didn't you have a little idea before coming? Lucifer asked, one eyebrow raised. Like, a plan that went further than "we go in and improvise"?

— I found the dimension, Isidora answered curtly. That was already something. What else did you want, a GPS?

Alastor, who had stayed silent until then, was carefully watching the shapes drifting above them, his eyes narrowed in concentration.

— Maybe we shouldn't try to see, he said slowly. Maybe we should try to feel. Something like 81, with all the power he's absorbed, can't just be floating in the void like everything else. It must... weigh on this place, one way or another.

Takeshi, still unsettled by the vastness of the place, ventured to speak up.

— Weigh how? he asked. Like, physically?

— Like gravity, Alastor answered. If this place keeps everything that's been forgotten, then a being as enormous as him must create some kind of point of attraction. We just need to find the direction where everything seems to... converge.

Isidora froze for a moment, a slow smile stretching across her lips.

— That, she said, is the first intelligent idea you've had since we left, Al. I'm almost proud of you.

— Almost, Alastor repeated with an ironic smile.

Lucifer closed his eyes for a moment, a focused expression crossing his face, before opening them again and slowly pointing in a direction in the darkness — a point that, at first glance, was in no way different from the rest of the surrounding void.

— There, he said. I feel something, that way. A heaviness. Like a debt that hasn't been fully paid.

The group turned toward the indicated direction, the water lapping gently around their feet as a heavy silence settled, each of them aware that the next step they took would bring them, one way or another, closer to the most dangerous being ever recorded in the two Codices.

Isidora suddenly froze, a smile lighting up her face as if a light bulb had just switched on above her head.

— Oh fuck, I know! she exclaimed. We just have to ask the magic chair!

A confused silence greeted this declaration, every eye turning to her.

— The what? asked Lucifer, one eyebrow raised so high it threatened to disappear into his hair.

— The Answer, Isidora clarified, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. That omniscient entity stashed somewhere in this dimension, that answers every question except two. It's supposed to be here, right? That's exactly what we need!

Alastor frowned, a new caution crossing his eyes.

— You sure that's a good idea? he said. Every soul only gets three questions in its entire existence. And if you ask a forbidden question — like how to defeat KJ or Grand Patron Luigi — it self-destructs on the spot.

— Well, that's exactly why we'll be careful, Isidora answered with a shrug. We just ask where 81 is. It's not exactly a trick question.

Takeshi, who had followed the exchange with growing apprehension, raised a hesitant hand.

— Wait, he said, but how do we find her? Nobody's ever managed to reach her, have they?

— No known method, Isidora confirmed, a predatory smile reappearing on her lips. But hey, we're already in a dimension that's supposed to be impossible to enter. So we might as well give it a shot.

Lucifer sighed long and hard, running a hand over his face.

— Great, he said. Yet another plan that relies entirely on total improvisation.

— Got a better idea? Isidora shot back.

The silence that followed was her only answer.

They walked in silence across the liquid expanse, the water lapping faintly around their steps, while above them shapes kept drifting through the darkness — some resembling broken objects, others fragments of words, sometimes entire sentences, vanishing as soon as they seemed to take shape.

— Look, Lulu, it's full of bullshit, kind of like your big dickhead skull, Isidora called out, pointing at a shapeless mass floating lazily above them.

— Your humor is always a pleasure, Lucifer answered without even looking up.

They kept going, the atmosphere gradually growing denser, heavier, as if the air itself — if it could still be called that here — were slowly tightening around them. Then, in the distance, a strange silhouette began to take shape: a heap of furniture, dozens, maybe hundreds of pieces, piled on top of each other, floating a few meters above the liquid ground — chairs, tables, wardrobes, some familiar, others in a style Takeshi had never seen.

— What's all this crap? asked Lucifer, slowing down.

Isidora had stopped dead, her eyes fixed on the pile of furniture with a new, almost religious intensity.

— It's here, she said simply.

— How can you be so sure? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised. It's literally a pile of forgotten furniture. It could be anything.

Isidora didn't answer right away, her eyes still riveted on the floating heap, something in her attitude having completely changed — no more sarcasm, no more nonchalance, just a quiet, inexplicable certainty.

— I don't know how to explain it to you, Al, she said finally, her voice lower than usual. But I feel it. Like something pulling at the back of my skull. It's here. The chair is here.

Takeshi, uncomfortable with this sudden change of tone in her, moved a little closer to the group.

— And how do we find it in there? he asked, gesturing at the chaotic pile of suspended furniture.

Isidora took a deep breath and stepped toward the floating heap, the water lapping gently around her feet.

— We search, she answered simply. And we pray it isn't the wrong chair.

They spread out among the heap, methodically searching through dozens of suspended pieces of furniture, pushing aside ordinary chairs, busted armchairs, wobbly tables — until Alastor, pulling on a half-collapsed chest of drawers, uncovered, nestled behind a stack of wardrobes, a chair decidedly different from all the others.

Its wood seemed both ancient and intact, without a trace of wear or dust, and on top of its backrest sat a small crystal sphere, translucent, inside which a faint, almost hypnotic glow was dancing.

— That's her, Isidora breathed, rushing forward.

She took hold of it with a care unusual for her, carrying it at arm's length to a clearer patch of the liquid ground, where she set it down delicately, then stepped back a few paces, as if the object might shatter at the slightest sudden movement.

A tense silence settled, every eye fixed on the empty chair, no one daring to make the first move.

— Well, Lucifer said finally, who asks the first question?

— Not me, Isidora answered immediately, stepping back even further. I already used my three questions centuries ago. I'm not allowed anymore.

Every eye then turned to Alastor, who immediately raised his hands in refusal.

— Oh no, count me out, he said. If I ask a lousy question and this thing blows up before we get the answer we want, I don't want it to be my fault.

Lucifer sighed, glancing resignedly at the sphere.

— And if I'm the one asking, and I make a mistake, he said, it's the king of Hell himself who burns a question. A bit more symbolic weight, isn't it?

Every eye inevitably ended up converging on Takeshi, who felt his stomach knot all at once.

— Wait, no, he said, backing away instinctively. Why me?

— You've never asked anybody a question, Isidora answered with a shrug. You've still got your three chances intact. And incidentally, it's kind of your father and your Poppy problem that got us all the way here, so...

— So what? Takeshi insisted, panic clearly showing in his voice.

— So it's kind of logical that you're the one who asks, Alastor concluded with a smile that was anything but reassuring.

Takeshi stood frozen for a moment, his eyes moving from the empty chair to the faces around him, all silent, all waiting. Then, with an almost painful slowness, he stepped toward the crystal sphere, his voice hesitant when he finally broke the silence.

— And... and what do I ask first? Where 81 is, or where my father is?

A voice suddenly rang out, calm, composed, coming from no visible mouth — seeming to emanate directly from the crystal sphere resting on the chair's backrest, vibrating in the air with a clarity strangely at odds with the heavy silence of the surrounding dimension.

— Hello, visitors, said the voice. So, you managed to come here. Not everyone can. But I believe I recognize Isidora, who came here several centuries ago.

Isidora stiffened slightly, a tense smile replacing her usual confidence.

— Yeah, it's been a while, she answered, her voice losing a little of its customary composure.

— But for the others, the voice went on, let me introduce myself. I am The Answer.

A silence settled, everyone holding their breath before this invisible entity that nevertheless seemed to be watching them all, with a precision that gave them goosebumps.

Takeshi, still motionless in front of the chair, felt his throat tighten even more.

— Do you... do you know why we're here? he asked, his voice trembling.

— I know everything there is to know, The Answer replied, in a perfectly neutral tone, neither warm nor cold. But I only answer questions asked directly. So, young Mystic — for that is indeed what you are, isn't it — ask your question. Just remember: three questions per soul, not one more. And two questions in particular will cause my immediate destruction if you ask them. Think carefully.

Takeshi took a deep breath, his hands trembling slightly as he stared at the crystal sphere.

— How do we free 81, oh great omniscient chair?

— Could you please stop sucking up to it, Isidora called from the back, a sardonic smile on her lips despite the tension in the air.

A silence followed, longer than the previous one, as if The Answer were taking the time to weigh each word before replying.

— This crystal sphere resting on me is not something that belongs to me, it said finally, its voice as neutral as ever. It was placed there. And I do believe that a soul has been training for a long time, here, in this dimension.

The group exchanged confused looks, Lucifer frowning first.

— Wait, he said, are you telling us someone else is already here? For how long?

— I do not have the answer to that precise question, The Answer replied. But the energy of this sphere does not come from me. It was placed deliberately, by a consciousness present in this dimension, capable of interacting with my structure without directly summoning me.

Takeshi felt his heart race, a lightning-fast thought crossing his mind.

— My father, he murmured. Could it be my father?

— I can neither confirm nor deny that hypothesis unless you ask the question formally, The Answer replied. Remember: your first question — how to free 81 — remains pending. Do you wish me to answer it, or would you rather rephrase it to ask instead about the identity of this presence?

Isidora stepped forward, a new urgency in her voice.

— Wait, kid, think carefully, she said. You've only got three questions. If you change your mind now, it doesn't count as used, but if you phrase it badly, you might lose your chance for good.

Takeshi clenched his fists, his decision made.

— Yes, I want to know where 81 is, he said, his voice firm despite the trembling still in his hands.

A silence settled, heavier than the previous ones, before The Answer spoke again, its voice as neutral as ever but charged with a new weight.

— This crystal sphere, it said, is the God Killer's prison.

A stunned silence fell over the entire group. Takeshi took a step back, his gaze settling with growing horror on the small translucent sphere that had been resting just above his head from the start, that faint glow dancing peacefully inside it.

— Wait, said Lucifer, his voice strangled. Are you telling us that 81 — THE 81, the one who destroyed Heaven, who devoured a billion years of gods — is stashed away in this little thing the size of a golf ball?

— The physical size of a container has no bearing on the power or the entity it holds, The Answer replied. A consciousness as vast as 81's was compressed, fragment by fragment, into this enclosed space, by the ten beings responsible for his sealing. It is not an ordinary prison. It is a prison on the scale of his soul.

Isidora had frozen, her eyes riveted on the sphere with a new intensity, a mixture of fascination and pure terror crossing her usually so offhand features.

— And that famous consciousness that's been "training" here for a while, she said slowly, you're telling me it might be the one that put this chair here. On purpose. Right next to 81's prison.

— That is a possibility I can neither confirm nor deny without a direct question, The Answer repeated.

Takeshi, still in shock, looked up at the sphere he had almost literally been holding in his hands a few moments earlier without knowing it, a chilling thought gradually forcing itself on him.

— He said it had to be put somewhere else, he murmured, turning to Isidora. You moved that chair yourself, with that thing on it. We... we literally carried his prison without knowing it.

Takeshi hesitated a split second before asking his second question, his voice more confident than before.

— How can we free him?

— To free 81, The Answer replied without the slightest delay, you just need to take this crystal sphere and break it, by throwing it on the ground, for example. But I advise you to do so on physical ground.

A stunned silence greeted this answer of almost comical simplicity, in total contrast with the cosmic scale of the entity in question.

— This is a joke, said Lucifer, his voice incredulous. Like, we've got ten super-powerful beings — including an Incarnation of Death and five Archdragons — who joined forces to seal away the most dangerous threat ever known... and all it takes is dropping it on the floor to screw everything up?

— The complexity of a seal does not necessarily lie in the fragility of its breaking point, The Answer replied, but in the difficulty of reaching it. No one before you had located this dimension, let alone this specific sphere. The simplicity of the final act in no way diminishes the difficulty of the road traveled to get there.

Isidora was already backing away instinctively, her hands raised as if to push Takeshi away from the sphere he was still holding between his fingers.

— Wait, wait, wait, she said hastily. Put that fucking ball down right now, kid. Like, right now, right now.

Takeshi looked down at the sphere he hadn't even noticed he had picked up again, a cold sweat instantly running down his spine.

— Wait, he said, his voice going up a notch, you were telling me that while I was holding it in my hands?!

— Technically, The Answer specified, as long as it is not broken on a surface dense enough to release the pressure contained inside, it remains stable. You were safe. Probably.

— "Probably"?! Takeshi repeated, panic completely overwhelming him as he knelt with exaggerated slowness to set the sphere back down on the liquid ground with the delicacy of a bomb technician defusing a bomb.

Takeshi, still shaken, slowly straightened up, taking a trembling breath before asking his last question.

— Where is my father?

— Your father is... IN THAILAND! Isidora yelled, cutting off the voice that was starting to answer.

— I will start again, The Answer said in a perfectly even tone, as if the interruption had never even happened.

— So your father is... AN ASSHOLE! Isidora shouted again, grinning from ear to ear.

— I will start again, The Answer repeated, unruffled.

— Your father... ABANDONED YOU! Isidora bellowed once more, punctuating every word with a theatrical sweep of her arm.

— SHUT UP! I WANT TO TALK! The Answer finally shouted, its voice losing every trace of neutrality for the first time since their arrival.

— SO I'M STARTING AGAAAAAIN! The Answer yelled over Isidora, visibly delighted by the chaos it was causing. YOUR FATHER IS LOCKED UP IN THE CULT OF... XAVIER DUPONT DE LIGONNÈS!

— WILL YOU SHUT YOUR MOUTH!!! The Answer retorted, the crystal sphere vibrating violently under the sudden intensity of its voice, an irritated light pulsing inside it.

A shocked silence abruptly fell again, Lucifer and Alastor doubled over, unable to hold back their laughter, while Takeshi stood open-mouthed, torn between hilarity and total dismay.

— Your father, The Answer finally went on, its voice gradually regaining its usual calm, though still tinged with perceptible annoyance, is being held by the Cult of KJ. He is still alive.

Takeshi froze, the words taking several seconds to truly sink into his mind, every trace of amusement evaporating instantly.

— He... he's alive, he murmured, his voice trembling. Are you sure?

— I am never wrong, The Answer replied. Your father is being held somewhere within the Cult of KJ, since the War of the Estrangement. That was your last question. You have now used your three questions. I can no longer answer any other, for this life.

Isidora, a smile still hanging on her lips, crossed her arms with perfect nonchalance.

— Then again, it's true he could've been in Thailand, getting his ass kneaded by some Thai girl, huh. We don't know. We don't judge.

A brief silence preceded The Answer's reply, its voice returning to an icy calm, almost threatening in its recovered neutrality.

— Isidora, it said, if I had arms, legs, charisma, strength, solidity — and not just someone else's prison to show off with — I would come and knead that bitch skull of yours.

A stunned silence greeted this retort, before Lucifer burst out laughing once again, even louder than before, almost doubling over.

— Now that, he said between hiccups, is the best thing I've heard in centuries. An ancient omniscient entity threatening to knead Isidora's skull.

Isidora, for her part, stayed open-mouthed for a moment, before a delighted smile spread across her face, visibly more impressed than insulted.

— Okay, she said, respect. I didn't think you had that in you, chair.

— I am not a chair, The Answer replied curtly. I am an omniscient consciousness forced to reside in a piece of furniture for lack of options. There is a difference.

— Yeah, yeah, said Isidora, waving a casual hand, the chair. Well, thanks for the info, anyway. Even if you nearly fried twice because of me.

Takeshi, still shaken by the revelation about his father, stayed silent, his gaze lost in the dark immensity of the dimension, a new and fragile determination slowly beginning to form behind the persistent worry that filled him.
codex-t1-c9.text: Agent 47 activated a mechanism on the control panel, and the metal ring began to vibrate, a deep hum rapidly intensifying until it became almost unbearable. At its center, the air tore open, revealing a sphere so deeply black that it seemed to suck in the light of the entire room. — Thirty seconds, 47 repeated. Now. Without another word, Isidora was the first to leap in, followed closely by Lucifer, then Alastor, dragging Takeshi along with a firm grip. The sensation of crossing over was different from all the previous ones — an absolute void, with no direction, no up or down, as if their very existence had been momentarily suspended between two realities. Then, as abruptly as the passage had begun, they emerged on the other side. Takeshi immediately felt his feet sink into something cold and liquid — a thin film of water, barely a few centimeters deep, covering a ground he couldn't clearly identify, neither stone nor earth, something in between, that almost rippled under his steps as if it weren't entirely solid. Above them, the sky — if you could still call it a sky — was nothing but a black gloom, without stars, without clouds, without the slightest identifiable source of light, and yet they could see everything clearly, as if light itself no longer really made sense here. Shapes crossed that darkness intermittently — blurry, indescribable silhouettes, some vaguely resembling objects, others creatures, still others nothing recognizable at all, gliding silently through the void without ever seeming to have any particular direction. Takeshi turned in place, desperately searching for a horizon, a boundary, anything that would show where this place ended — but there was nothing. No beginning, no end. Just that expanse of shallow water stretching as far as the eye could see in every direction, under that sky of darkness peopled with forgotten things. — What... what is all this? he murmured, his voice echoing strangely, as if absorbed by the surrounding void before it even fully reached his own ears. Isidora, for her part, stood motionless, watching the shapes float above them with an expression he had never seen on her before — something that looked, for the first time, like sincere worry. — The Dimension of Shadows, she said softly. We're here. Isidora took out her phone, the screen lighting up in the surrounding darkness — then her face fell slightly. — Wait, there's no signal here?! she exclaimed, waving the phone around as if that would magically make a signal bar appear. Like, I got signal IN HELL, but not here?! She tapped frantically at the screen, turning in circles in search of a phantom signal, her look of utter disaster contrasting violently with the gravity of the place. — This is a joke, she said. How am I supposed to post a story if there's no signal? That's the worst part of this dimension. NO SIGNAL! Lucifer, standing back, rolled his eyes up to the sky — well, to what passed for one. — We've just entered a dimension where everything the entire universe has forgotten ends up disappearing, he said, and your one concern is your Instagram account. — My priorities are clear, yes, Isidora answered without the slightest embarrassment, finally tucking the phone into a fold of her cape with a disappointed sigh. Fine. Whatever. I'll catch up later. "Sorry guys, I was stuck in the absolute void, milk milk lemonade." Alastor let out a dry little laugh, while Takeshi stayed frozen, his eyes relentlessly sweeping the infinite expanse around them, a chilling certainty gradually settling in him that here, in this place with no beginning and no end, finding anything at all — 81, his father, or even simply the way back — was going to prove much harder than expected. Isidora slowly turned in place, scanning the shifting darkness around them, her tone gradually becoming serious again. — Okay, now we need to figure out where you find a god killer in an infinite dimension, she said. Because right now, look as I might, I don't really see any signposts. — Didn't you have a little idea before coming? Lucifer asked, one eyebrow raised. Like, a plan that went further than "we go in and improvise"? — I found the dimension, Isidora answered curtly. That was already something. What else did you want, a GPS? Alastor, who had stayed silent until then, was carefully watching the shapes drifting above them, his eyes narrowed in concentration. — Maybe we shouldn't try to see, he said slowly. Maybe we should try to feel. Something like 81, with all the power he's absorbed, can't just be floating in the void like everything else. It must... weigh on this place, one way or another. Takeshi, still unsettled by the vastness of the place, ventured to speak up. — Weigh how? he asked. Like, physically? — Like gravity, Alastor answered. If this place keeps everything that's been forgotten, then a being as enormous as him must create some kind of point of attraction. We just need to find the direction where everything seems to... converge. Isidora froze for a moment, a slow smile stretching across her lips. — That, she said, is the first intelligent idea you've had since we left, Al. I'm almost proud of you. — Almost, Alastor repeated with an ironic smile. Lucifer closed his eyes for a moment, a focused expression crossing his face, before opening them again and slowly pointing in a direction in the darkness — a point that, at first glance, was in no way different from the rest of the surrounding void. — There, he said. I feel something, that way. A heaviness. Like a debt that hasn't been fully paid. The group turned toward the indicated direction, the water lapping gently around their feet as a heavy silence settled, each of them aware that the next step they took would bring them, one way or another, closer to the most dangerous being ever recorded in the two Codices. Isidora suddenly froze, a smile lighting up her face as if a light bulb had just switched on above her head. — Oh fuck, I know! she exclaimed. We just have to ask the magic chair! A confused silence greeted this declaration, every eye turning to her. — The what? asked Lucifer, one eyebrow raised so high it threatened to disappear into his hair. — The Answer, Isidora clarified, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. That omniscient entity stashed somewhere in this dimension, that answers every question except two. It's supposed to be here, right? That's exactly what we need! Alastor frowned, a new caution crossing his eyes. — You sure that's a good idea? he said. Every soul only gets three questions in its entire existence. And if you ask a forbidden question — like how to defeat KJ or Grand Patron Luigi — it self-destructs on the spot. — Well, that's exactly why we'll be careful, Isidora answered with a shrug. We just ask where 81 is. It's not exactly a trick question. Takeshi, who had followed the exchange with growing apprehension, raised a hesitant hand. — Wait, he said, but how do we find her? Nobody's ever managed to reach her, have they? — No known method, Isidora confirmed, a predatory smile reappearing on her lips. But hey, we're already in a dimension that's supposed to be impossible to enter. So we might as well give it a shot. Lucifer sighed long and hard, running a hand over his face. — Great, he said. Yet another plan that relies entirely on total improvisation. — Got a better idea? Isidora shot back. The silence that followed was her only answer. They walked in silence across the liquid expanse, the water lapping faintly around their steps, while above them shapes kept drifting through the darkness — some resembling broken objects, others fragments of words, sometimes entire sentences, vanishing as soon as they seemed to take shape. — Look, Lulu, it's full of bullshit, kind of like your big dickhead skull, Isidora called out, pointing at a shapeless mass floating lazily above them. — Your humor is always a pleasure, Lucifer answered without even looking up. They kept going, the atmosphere gradually growing denser, heavier, as if the air itself — if it could still be called that here — were slowly tightening around them. Then, in the distance, a strange silhouette began to take shape: a heap of furniture, dozens, maybe hundreds of pieces, piled on top of each other, floating a few meters above the liquid ground — chairs, tables, wardrobes, some familiar, others in a style Takeshi had never seen. — What's all this crap? asked Lucifer, slowing down. Isidora had stopped dead, her eyes fixed on the pile of furniture with a new, almost religious intensity. — It's here, she said simply. — How can you be so sure? asked Alastor, one eyebrow raised. It's literally a pile of forgotten furniture. It could be anything. Isidora didn't answer right away, her eyes still riveted on the floating heap, something in her attitude having completely changed — no more sarcasm, no more nonchalance, just a quiet, inexplicable certainty. — I don't know how to explain it to you, Al, she said finally, her voice lower than usual. But I feel it. Like something pulling at the back of my skull. It's here. The chair is here. Takeshi, uncomfortable with this sudden change of tone in her, moved a little closer to the group. — And how do we find it in there? he asked, gesturing at the chaotic pile of suspended furniture. Isidora took a deep breath and stepped toward the floating heap, the water lapping gently around her feet. — We search, she answered simply. And we pray it isn't the wrong chair. They spread out among the heap, methodically searching through dozens of suspended pieces of furniture, pushing aside ordinary chairs, busted armchairs, wobbly tables — until Alastor, pulling on a half-collapsed chest of drawers, uncovered, nestled behind a stack of wardrobes, a chair decidedly different from all the others. Its wood seemed both ancient and intact, without a trace of wear or dust, and on top of its backrest sat a small crystal sphere, translucent, inside which a faint, almost hypnotic glow was dancing. — That's her, Isidora breathed, rushing forward. She took hold of it with a care unusual for her, carrying it at arm's length to a clearer patch of the liquid ground, where she set it down delicately, then stepped back a few paces, as if the object might shatter at the slightest sudden movement. Takeshi insisted, panic clearly showing in his voice. — So it's kind of logical that you're the one who asks, Alastor concluded with a smile that was anything but reassuring. A voice suddenly rang out, calm, composed, coming from no visible mouth — seeming to emanate directly from the crystal sphere resting on the chair's backrest, vibrating in the air with a clarity strangely at odds with the heavy silence of the surrounding dimension. — Hello, visitors, said the voice. So, you managed to come here. Not everyone can. But I believe I recognize Isidora, who came here several centuries ago. Isidora stiffened slightly, a tense smile replacing her usual confidence. — Yeah, it's been a while, she answered, her voice losing a little of its customary composure. — But for the others, the voice went on, let me introduce myself. I am The Answer. A silence settled, everyone holding their breath before this invisible entity that nevertheless seemed to be watching them all, with a precision that gave them goosebumps. Takeshi, still motionless in front of the chair, felt his throat tighten even more. — Do you... do you know why we're here? he asked, his voice trembling. — I know everything there is to know, The Answer replied, in a perfectly neutral tone, neither warm nor cold. But I only answer questions asked directly. So, young Mystic — for that is indeed what you are, isn't it — ask your question. Just remember: three questions per soul, not one more. And two questions in particular will cause my immediate destruction if you ask them. Think carefully. It was placed there. And I do believe that a soul has been training for a long time, here, in this dimension. For how long? — I do not have the answer to that precise question, The Answer replied. But the energy of this sphere does not come from me. It was placed deliberately, by a consciousness present in this dimension, capable of interacting with my structure without directly summoning me. Takeshi felt his heart race, a lightning-fast thought crossing his mind. — My father, he murmured. Could it be my father? — I can neither confirm nor deny that hypothesis unless you ask the question formally, The Answer replied. Remember: your first question — how to free 81 — remains pending. codex-t2-c1.title: Chapter 1 — Justice Came Out of My Ass
codex-t2-c1.html:
Isidora turned her phone back on without a word, resuming her live with disconcerting ease — a gesture no one around her even bothered to comment on, all of them visibly too used to the reflex to pay it the slightest attention.

— Okay, people, here we go again, she announced simply, positioning the camera to capture the imminent takeoff.

Agent 47, unfazed, spoke up again, his synthetic-sounding voice as neutral as ever despite the implicit gravity of the information being passed on.

— Reaper confirms: Justice Man has an estimated one percent chance of survival. Probability of victory against 81: zero.

81 let out a short, dry laugh, adjusting the swords on his back with growing nonchalance.

— One percent, he repeated. That's already better than Rex Stella had, at least.

— He may have a chance to escape, Reaper specified. His imprisonment ability could theoretically protect him temporarily, with no guarantee of long-term success.

Takeshi, climbing aboard the ship that had just gently landed on the white stone of the sanctuary, cast a worried glance at 81.

— Are you really planning to kill him too? he asked. Even though his power is precisely about not killing the people he captures?

81 settled heavily into the ship, his massive body making the structure creak under his weight.

— Doesn't change what he did to me, he answered, an icy coldness returning to his voice. He took part in sealing me. Never mind his fine values of justice. He'll pay like the others.

A heavy silence settled, Isidora herself momentarily pausing her live commentary, sensing the new tension that had just settled in the cabin.

Lucifer, climbing in in turn, laid a hand on Takeshi's shoulder, his tone more serious than usual.

— Drop it, kid, he murmured. You can't reason with a vengeance several millennia old. Just stay out of his way, and you'll be fine.

The ship took off, shooting through space toward Earth, while inside everyone stayed silent, aware that the next confrontation would be very different from the last.

The ship touched down discreetly in a dark alley not far from downtown Washington, its hull blending almost instantly into the surrounding darkness thanks to an optical camouflage Agent 47 had activated even before the landing was complete.

They got off one by one, Takeshi blinking in the glare of the streetlights and at the familiar noise of city traffic — a striking contrast after the cosmic landscapes he had just crossed.

— Welcome back to Earth, kid, Lucifer remarked, adjusting his jacket, an amused smile on his lips. Feels weird, huh, seeing normal stuff again.

— You call that normal? Takeshi answered, nodding toward Isidora, who was already filming the facades of the surrounding buildings for her live, visibly delighted with the change of scenery.

They made their way through the streets, Agent 47 in the lead, his earpiece crackling regularly as Reaper analyzed police reports in real time, looking for the slightest sign of an unusual intervention.

— Activity detected, 47 finally announced, stopping dead at an intersection. Police report: several assaults stopped within ten minutes, within a three-block radius. No suspects apprehended on site. Victims report a swift intervention followed by the immediate disappearance of the attackers.

81 gave a satisfied smile, his eyes — well, his single eye — narrowing with growing anticipation.

— That's him, he said. Still saving little shopkeepers and random passersby. He never changed.

They followed the indicated direction, walking past several shop fronts, until they spotted, at the end of the street, a figure in a dark suit, standing motionless in front of a small grocery store, seeming to watch over the surroundings with an almost fatherly vigilance.

— There, Isidora murmured, finally lowering her phone, her usual excitement giving way to a new tension. That's him.

Justice Man, instantly sensing a presence approaching, slowly turned his head toward them, his gaze freezing as he recognized, among the little group, the massive and familiar figure of 81.

Justice Man slowly straightened up, his gaze moving from 81 to Isidora, an immediate tension hardening his features.

— You, he said, his voice heavy with calm gravity. I knew you'd get out. But it's a little premature.

— You can say that again, he's probably premature about so many things, Isidora called out with a mocking smile, her phone already raised toward the scene.

— You, shut up, Justice Man shot back without even looking at her, don't start busting my balls.

Isidora raised her hands in innocence, a smile still on her lips, but didn't turn off her live for all that, continuing to film with obvious pleasure.

— Okay, okay, I'll shut up, she said. But I'm still filming, just so you know.

81 took a step forward, his two swords still sheathed, a fierce smile slowly stretching across his scarred face.

— Premature, you say, he repeated. I've been waiting for this for millennia, Justice Man. Premature isn't really the word I'd use.

Justice Man didn't back down, his posture firming up, a golden glow slowly beginning to emanate from his hands, the energy of his power already gathering.

— I always knew this day would come, he said. But know one thing, 81: even if I know I can't beat you, I won't surrender without a fight.

— I expected nothing less from you, 81 answered, slowly drawing one of his two swords, his smile widening as the excitement of the imminent fight rose in him.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47 and Lucifer, felt a lump form in his throat, a dull worry growing at what was about to unfold right in the middle of a Washington street, under the potential eyes of dozens of passersby still unaware of the danger looming over them.

— Shouldn't we, like, evacuate the civilians before it starts? he asked, his voice hesitant.

— Too late for that, Agent 47 answered simply, glancing at the few passersby who were already starting to stop, intrigued by the palpable tension of the scene.

With a sweeping gesture, Justice Man summoned a massive hammer, its metal handle engraved with glowing symbols, the head of the weapon as wide as a human torso, and took up a defensive stance, legs slightly bent, ready to absorb the first assault.

81, for his part, simply kept his sword in hand, his single eye never leaving his opponent, an almost amused patience crossing his scarred face.

That was when a police officer, alerted by the passersby who had gathered at a distance, stepped toward them, one hand resting on his service weapon, his tone resolutely professional despite the rather unusual scene unfolding before him.

— Excuse me, gentlemen, he said, but those weapons are prohibited. Surrender and come with me to the station.

— STAND BACK! Justice Man shouted, without taking his eyes off 81. This man is dangerous, you need to evacuate the city at the very least!

The officer, visibly unimpressed by the warning, frowned, his hand tightening on his weapon.

— Sir, he retorted curtly, stop resisting, or you'll be considered noncompliant with the law.

Isidora, still filming the scene with undisguised pleasure, couldn't help bursting out laughing.

— People, I swear, this is the best moment of my evening, she commented. The poor cop trying to arrest a god killer and the Incarnation of Justice for illegal possession of weapons.

81, also amused by the intervention, turned his head slightly toward the officer, a predatory smile stretching across his face.

— He's right, you know, he said to the officer, a hint of irony in his voice. You really should evacuate the city. It's good advice.

The officer, suddenly hesitant before the icy self-assurance of that answer, took a step back, his hand trembling slightly on the grip of his weapon, while around them the first passersby were finally beginning to understand that something far more serious than a simple altercation was about to happen.

The officer, panic definitively taking over, drew his weapon and fired without waiting any longer — the bullet hit 81 square in the chest, ricocheting off his skin without leaving the slightest mark, dropping to the ground with a pathetic clink.

81 looked down at the point of impact, a barely annoyed smile stretching across his face, before turning to the officer with chilling murderous intent.

— Mistake, he said simply, lunging toward the man with lightning speed.

But Justice Man reacted instantly, his hammer striking the ground with such force that a shockwave hurled the officer out of reach, sending him crashing against the wall of a nearby building, dazed but alive.

— RUN! Justice Man roared at the man, without even turning toward him, his whole body tensed facing 81. Evacuate the city, the state if you have to, but get out!

The officer, still shaken, got up as best he could and immediately bolted, shouting confused orders into his radio, his trembling voice betraying pure terror.

Around them, the crowd that had gathered was already starting to panic, screams rising from all sides as the first witnesses finally grasped the scale of the danger, a general stampede beginning in the adjacent streets.

In the distance, police sirens wailed, approaching fast, their shrill sound adding to the growing chaos.

Justice Man, while keeping his guard up against 81, cast a quick glance at the panicking crowd, a visible dilemma crossing his features — protect the civilians still pouring into the area, or focus entirely on the fight that seemed inevitable.

— See your problem, Justice Man? said 81, visibly savoring this hesitation. You've always been too busy saving everyone to focus on what really matters.

— Saving people matters, Justice Man retorted, his hammer tightening in his hand as he made a quick gesture toward the surrounding streets, a golden glow briefly sweeping the area, forming an invisible barrier that gently pushed the crowd back. Even if it costs me dearly in this fight.

Isidora, still live, zoomed in on the scene with growing excitement.

— People, it's officially total chaos, she commented. I hope you've got popcorn, because this is going to be one hell of a show.

The fight exploded without warning, 81 and Justice Man lunging at each other in an outburst of raw power — their first blows colliding with such violence that the resulting shockwave literally swept away several surrounding blocks, entire facades collapsing with a deafening roar, glass and rubble raining down on the already deserted streets.

Justice Man absorbed each impact with impressive resilience, his hammer rising every time to block or deflect 81's assaults, but the difference in power remained glaring, visible without even trying to analyze it — each exchange left Justice Man pushed back a little further, a little more out of breath, while 81 seemed to barely bother putting in any effort.

But it was neither of them who broke the tense silence that followed each titanic clash.

— Could you move over to fight, please? Isidora called from the side, her phone perfectly steady despite the surrounding chaos. The lighting's better on the right.

The two fighters froze for a fraction of a second, a stunned silence settling despite the surrounding destruction, before 81 turned his head slightly toward her, one eyebrow — well, the brow ridge above his single eye — raised.

— Are you serious right now? he said.

— Completely, Isidora confirmed with a radiant smile. The setting sun hits badly on this side, it makes crappy shadows on your faces. Whereas over there, she added, pointing to an intersection a little farther on, it'd be way more cinematic.

Justice Man, still panting, shot her an incredulous look, a hint of exasperation breaking through his concentration.

— We're in the middle of a fight for the survival of one of us, he said, and you're worried about the lighting?

— People have standards these days, Isidora answered with a shrug, not the least bit shaken by the remark. You don't want your epic fight to look like a bad found-footage movie, do you?

81, shaking his head with a mixture of amusement and exasperation, turned back to Justice Man, his sword still raised.

— She's not completely wrong, you know, he said. Okay, come on, let's keep going, but a little more to the right.

81 and Justice Man repositioned themselves a few meters farther on, in light that was indeed better...

Justice Man raised his hammer.

81 smiled.

— Let's resume.

The next clash shook the whole neighborhood. Justice Man took the hit, slid three meters across the cracked asphalt, his hammer raised just in time to parry a second blow.

— You feel the difference now...

— I've always felt it.

81 followed up, faster, heavier. Justice Man dodged the first blow, blocked the second, but the third hurled him against the facade of a building that half collapsed under the impact.

Isidora, phone still raised.

— Wow, the angle's perfect now, thanks for the decorating tips, guys.

Takeshi, standing back with Agent 47 and Lucifer, watched Justice Man painfully get back up, blood running down his temple.

— He's going to die.

Lucifer didn't answer right away.

— Yes.

Justice Man straightened up, his hammer back in position, his gaze still fixed on 81 despite his obvious exhaustion.

— I'll hold out as long as it takes for the civilians to get far away.

81 moved forward slowly, his sword dragging along the ground with a metallic screech.

— You've always been too noble for your own good, Justice Man.

Isidora, phone still aimed, not taking her eyes off the fight.

— Shut up and more action! The fans want a fight, not a date, so either you get a room or you fight!

81 turned his head slightly toward her.

— She's right.

Justice Man gripped his hammer.

— ...

81 lunged first, his blade tracing a perfect arc. Justice Man raised his weapon just in time, the impact sending out a wave that shattered the windows of the surrounding buildings for a hundred meters.

— YOUR PROBLEM, JUSTICE MAN, IS THAT YOU ALWAYS FIGHT FOR OTHER PEOPLE!

— AND YOURS IS THAT YOU ONLY FIGHT FOR YOURSELF!

81 struck again, faster, Justice Man backing up several meters, the asphalt cracking under his feet with every forced step.

Isidora, in the background.

— YES! FINALLY SOME PUNCH! KEEP IT UP!

Takeshi, motionless, watched Justice Man's hammer begin to crack under the repeated impacts.

— He's going to lose his weapon...

Agent 47, unfazed.

— Confirmed. Structural failure estimated within the next few seconds.

Justice Man raised his hammer one last time to block a blow. The handle snapped clean, the head of the weapon flying off with a metallic crash.

81 stopped, his sword hovering a few centimeters from the face of Justice Man, out of breath, disarmed, on his knees on the split asphalt.

— ...

81 smiled.

— So, Justice Man. Any last words?

A voice rang out from the sky, calm, charged with an ancient power.

— You're the one who should be saying your last words, 81.

A bright point appeared above them, a star hanging behind Justice Man, a beam of light slowly descending and settling on the cracked asphalt with almost theatrical gentleness.

A figure materialized out of the light.

81 looked up, his smile freezing into a grimace mixing amusement and old grudge.

— Aravos. Still here to piss me off, then.

Isidora, phone still in hand, tilted her head to the side.

— Ooh, smells like a throuple.

— SHUT UP! 81, Justice Man and Aravos shouted in a single voice.

Isidora raised her hands in surrender, a smile still on her lips, but obviously didn't cut her live.

Aravos stepped forward, his footsteps making no sound on the ground, his gaze fixed squarely on 81 with an ancient coldness.

— It's been a long time.

— Not long enough, 81 answered, his sword still raised above Justice Man, but his attention now entirely turned toward the newcomer. I was hoping to kill you last. You ruined the surprise.

— Likewise.

Justice Man, taking advantage of 81's momentary inattention, tried to back away, crawling a few meters before collapsing, exhausted, his gaze moving between the two figures now facing each other.

Takeshi, standing back, leaned toward Agent 47.

— Who's he?

— Aravos. The Star of Decline. One of the ten who sealed 81.

81 rolled his shoulder, his sword rising again, his fierce smile returning to his face.

— Right. Since you came all the way here for your daughter, might as well settle this now.

Aravos didn't answer right away.

— ...

Then his gaze hardened.

— Exactly.

A crackle in Agent 47's earpiece.

— According to my estimates, combined chance of survival for Aravos and Justice Man: one point twenty-five percent. Chance of definitive victory: zero.

Then screams. From the other side of the city.

Buildings were collapsing one after another in a continuous roar, cries of panic rising from everywhere at once. In the distance, an army was taking shape on the horizon, advancing in formation, and on the ruins of a gutted building stood an immense figure.

Two and a half meters tall. A mass of bulging muscles under skin stretched to the limit, two tattoos inked into each forearm.

DIE. Left arm.

MEMORIES OF DEFEAT. Right arm.

Aravos froze, his gaze instantly hardening.

— Kang.

Isidora, phone turned toward the horizon.

— OH FUCK, we've got a second surprise guest!

81, still motionless facing Aravos, a nasty smile slowly stretching across his face.

— Kang? The King of Kings? The one who never managed to meet me?

Aravos didn't answer, his eyes still fixed on the massive figure advancing through the rubble, every step making the ground shake under his titanic weight.

Justice Man, still on his knees, raised his head, blood still running from his temple.

— ...

— Another problem, he murmured.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed, took a step back.

— Are there many cosmic threats left that are going to show up today?

Lucifer, arms crossed, watched the scene with an almost weary calm.

— Given the day we're having... I wouldn't even dare bet on it.

Kang landed in the middle of the battlefield, his massive feet shattering the asphalt on impact, placing himself directly between 81 and the Aravos–Justice Man duo.

— Aravos. Finally, there you are. Now I can get my revenge.

Aravos raised a hand.

— Listen, Kang. You wanted to fight 81 today? There he is. Right in front of you. Help us, and we'll all have gotten what we wanted.

Kang stood motionless.

— ...

A full minute went by, his gaze moving from 81 to Aravos, visible reflection crossing his weathered features.

— I accept.

He stepped forward, taking his place beside Aravos and Justice Man, then raised a massive arm toward the army still advancing in the distance, ravaging everything in its path.

— TO ME! JOIN THE FIGHT!

The entire army instantly veered, changing direction in a single movement, heading straight for them with a pounding of synchronized footsteps.

Isidora, her eyes shining, raised her phone with both hands.

— People, I hope you're sitting down, because what's coming next is going to be HUGE.

81, alone facing this growing gathering, didn't back away a centimeter, a fierce smile slowly stretching across his scarred face, his sword spinning once in his hand before steadying.

— A king, a star, a judge, and a whole army.

He cracked his neck.

— Perfect. This is going to be more interesting than expected.

Agent 47, standing back with Takeshi and Lucifer, discreetly activated a new function on his earpiece.

— Reaper. Full recalculation needed.

— Calculating.

Takeshi, short of breath, watched the army draw inexorably closer, the ground trembling under thousands of footsteps.

— Shouldn't we... step in?

Lucifer laid a firm hand on his shoulder.

— No. We watch. And we pray that 81 is in as good a mood as he looks.

Justice Man, still on his knees, picked up the broken head of his hammer, clutching it in his fist like an improvised weapon.

— ...

He got back up.
