Hunter of things and people, very good at what she does, a bit of a psychopath around the edges, but we love her anyway. Takeshi Ashford, still frozen behind his concrete block, felt his heart speed up all at once at hearing the name spoken so openly. — ... — She's here for me, he murmured to Lucifer Morningstar, his voice tense. — Sure looks that way, Lucifer answered, his gaze remaining fixed on the scene with new caution. Poppy, as if she had heard despite the distance, slowly turned her head toward the concrete block — her empty, fixed gaze settling directly on the spot where Takeshi was hiding. — ... A heavy silence settled, broken only by the wind sweeping across the smoking rubble of the destroyed city. Poppy stood motionless for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on Takeshi Ashford, before tilting her head slightly — a slow movement, almost too fluid to look natural. — Haven't I seen you before? — Yes, Takeshi answered, his voice trembling slightly despite himself. You tried to kill me in my apartment. Everyone has their own way of getting acquainted. — ... Poppy stared at him for a few more seconds, her expression still perfectly neutral, not a trace of emotion showing on her doll's face. Then she slowly looked away, as if the information had just been filed somewhere. — Fine. Since 81 puts up with you, I'll do the same. Besides, Isidora knows you, so it'll be fine. Takeshi blinked, the tension leaving his shoulders slightly without disappearing completely. — ...Does that mean you're not going to try to kill me anymore? — For now. — That's... reassuring. Isidora Néant burst out laughing, slapping Takeshi on the back hard enough to make him stumble. — Ah, that's Poppy for you, warm as ever. You'll get used to it. 81, still standing in the middle of the rubble, crossed his arms, his one-eyed gaze moving from Poppy to Takeshi and then to Isidora. — Can someone explain to me why everyone here seems to know each other except me? — Long story, Lucifer Morningstar answered, finally stepping out of his hiding place with Takeshi. We'll fill you in later. Agent 47, silent throughout the exchange, adjusted his weapon against his shoulder, his earpiece crackling slightly. — Riper reports that the Assimilated has completely disappeared from the radar. No trace of his current position. — Cool cool cool, Isidora said, stretching. So what now? Do we go home? I'm hungry. While Poppy, 81, Lucifer and Takeshi talked over what had just happened — Isidora was pacing in circles in the middle of the rubble, completely indifferent to the discussion. — WHEN ARE WE GOING HOME, DAMN IT, I'M STARVING! — ... No one reacted. Lucifer was still explaining to 81 how Poppy had, without even realizing it at first, begun hampering the Assimilated's chaotic domain long before her visible appearance — a consequence of her own hunt, focused on Takeshi, which was eating away at the area of effect without her knowing it herself. — Seriously, is anyone listening to me? I'M STARVING! — We got it, Isidora, Lucifer sighed without even turning his head. Five minutes. — You always say five minutes and then it's three hours. I know how this goes. She walked over to the group, planting herself right between Lucifer and Poppy, cutting the conversation short. — Anyway, so basically, 81 summed up, she's the one who was blocking his power from the start without meaning to. Poppy stayed silent for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on the point in the sky where the Assimilated had disappeared. — ... — That explains the 99%, Lucifer added. Your hunt must already have been spreading across the area before you even appeared physically. — I was only looking for him, she said, her gaze sliding toward Takeshi. Nothing more. Takeshi felt an unpleasant shiver run down his spine. — ...So basically, if I hadn't been hunted by you, the Assimilated might have won. — Possibly, Poppy answered, without the slightest emotion in her voice. — EXCUSE ME? Isidora exploded, completely ignoring the importance of the revelation. WHEN. ARE. WE. GOING. 81 let out a grunt that vaguely resembled a laugh. — You really have no priorities, do you. — MY PRIORITY IS MY STOMACH, THANK YOU. Lucifer slowly massaged his temples, returning nonetheless to the original question. — We're first going to finish figuring out why Poppy had such an impact on his domain, Isidora. — Okay, but then we eat. — Then we eat, he confirmed, resigned, before turning back to Poppy. That level of disruption... that's not normal for a simple hunt, is it? Poppy looked at him, her expression still perfectly neutral. — No. It's not normal. — SHUT UP! Isidora shouted. WE'RE GOING TO EAT, DAMN IT, OR I'LL TAKE YOUR BIG FOREHEADS AND MAKE A TACO OUT OF THEM, SO LET'S GO! She grabbed Lucifer's hand on one side, Poppy's on the other, without the slightest ounce of hesitation, as if she were dragging two unruly kids out of a toy store. — ... 81 stood frozen on the spot, his one-eyed gaze moving from the scene to Takeshi, completely stunned, unable to come up with any reaction. — ... — You too, Isidora called out, half turning to point her chin at 81 without letting go of the two hands she was already holding. Move your butt. — ...She just literally took our hands like we're five years old, 81 finally managed to say, addressing Takeshi as if seeking confirmation that the scene was really happening. — Yeah. Welcome to the group, Takeshi answered with a crooked smile. Lucifer, his hand still captive, let out a long resigned sigh, as if this kind of treatment were nothing unusual for him at all. — Isidora, I am the King of Hell. — So what? I'm the Witch of the Void, we're even on long-winded titles, come on, let's move. Poppy, for her part, simply stared at her own captive hand with an expression still perfectly neutral, as if analyzing a new and incomprehensible phenomenon. — ... — Is she really going to drag us like this all the way to wherever we're eating? Takeshi asked, falling into step despite himself. — With Isidora, anything is possible, Lucifer answered, letting himself be dragged along without resisting anymore. Agent 47 followed the group at a distance, his measured stride contrasting with the general agitation, his earpiece crackling slightly. — Riper, analysis. "Analyzing..." — I want to be sure this is not some outside mental manipulation. Confirm that the observed scene corresponds to reality. A short silence, then Reaper's synthetic voice rang out again. "Full sweep complete. No psychic, illusory or dimensional manipulation signature detected in the area." — ... "Formal confirmation: Isidora is currently dragging Lucifer Morningstar, King of Hell, and Poppy, interdimensional hunting entity, by the hand, like children. This scene is reality." 47 stayed silent for a moment, his gaze fixed on the scene before him — Isidora still in the lead, pulling her two improvised hostages, Takeshi and 81 following as best they could, each with a different expression ranging from resignation to total astonishment. — ...Understood. "Would you like a supplementary psychological analysis on the subject Isidora?" — No. That will not be necessary. "Recommendation archived." 47 picked up his pace slightly to catch up with the group, his face as impassive as ever despite everything he had just confirmed. — The situation has been verified, he announced simply as he drew level with them. No outside manipulation. It's real. 81 turned his head toward him, almost despairing. — You really needed to ask your AI if this was real. — As a precaution. — It's Isidora, not a cosmic threat. — That is precisely the precaution in question, 47 answered, unfazed. Isidora, without even turning around, tightened her grip on Lucifer's and Poppy's hands. — I CAN HEAR EVERYTHING YOU'RE SAYING, YOU TRAITORS, WE'RE GOING TO EAT NOW! The same explosion suddenly tore through the air in front of them — a burst of black and red particles materializing the Assimilated once again, his body fully re-formed, his wounds erased, an aura much denser than before crackling all around him. — ... The whole group froze. 81 instinctively reached for his sword, Lucifer stiffened, Takeshi took a step back, Agent 47 was already raising his weapon. — Did you really think I would flee forever? the Assimilated enunciated, his voice charged with new power. I have returned more— Isidora didn't even let him finish his sentence. She instantly let go of Lucifer's and Poppy's hands, shot forward in a flash, and brought her right fist down square in the Assimilated's face with such violence that the air itself split under the impact. — GET LOST, I'M STARVING! The Assimilated literally disappeared before the blow even really touched him — an instant, preventive disintegration, as if his own body had understood that taking that punch meant certain and irreversible death. Silence fell again. — ... 81 stood with his mouth half open, staring at the empty spot where the Assimilated had been standing a second earlier. — ...He literally just vanished so he wouldn't take your punch. — Yeah, well, he should've gotten lost faster, Isidora grumbled, shaking her hand as if the gesture had stung her a little too. I'm starving, I don't have time to waste on this kind of crap. Poppy stared at the scene, her neutral expression slightly strained toward something that almost resembled surprise. — ... Agent 47 slowly lowered his weapon, his earpiece crackling. — Riper, calculate the Assimilated's probability of survival against that blow if it had connected. "Calculating... 0%. Total destruction, no regeneration possible." — ...That was her weakest blow since the start of the scene, 47 added, almost to himself. Takeshi, still in shock, slowly turned his head toward Isidora. — You just... you literally just made a Higher Incarnation of Chaos run away because you were hungry. — Exactly. So, CAN WE GO NOW? Lucifer massaged his temples once again, taking back the hand Isidora had let go of in the meantime and holding it out to her again without even thinking. — ...Fine, let's eat. The Assimilated materialized in the heart of the Imperial Palace, his body still marked by the traces of the fight, yet his gait keeping a furious, almost humiliated stiffness. He crossed the corridors without a word, without a glance at the guards who instinctively stepped aside as he passed, until he reached the great doors of a hall reserved for the Higher Incarnations. He opened them with a simple gesture, the residual power of his still unstable domain enough to slam them against the walls. — ... Inside, several Incarnations turned toward him. Some silent, others already exchanging knowing looks — news of his defeat had visibly spread faster than he had. Tempus, sitting off to the side, his piercing gaze fixed on the Assimilated since he came in, was the first to speak. — So. The rumor is true. — Shut up, Tempus. — A God Killer set free, a Witch of the Void, a hunting entity, and you come back without even a single victim to your name. Impressive. The Assimilated clenched his fists, his domain crackling faintly around him, still unstable after his hasty escape. — Where is KJ. I want to speak to him. A heavy silence crossed the hall. Several Incarnations looked away, uncomfortable. Tempus slowly stood up, his expression as impassive as ever. — KJ isn't here. — ...What? — He's been gone for several days. No one knows where. Even the Palace Demon doesn't know. The Assimilated stood frozen for a moment, his golden gaze sweeping the hall, seeking confirmation in the other faces present. — Impossible. KJ never leaves the Palace without informing his own. — And yet, Tempus answered, crossing his arms. It's the first time in several millennia that it's happened. A worried murmur ran through the hall, the other Incarnations exchanging increasingly tense looks. — ...Then who is in charge, in his absence? No one answered right away. — No one, Tempus finally said, his voice suddenly graver. And that may be the real problem. Another silence settled, broken a few moments later by the slow opening of the great doors. Void walked in, his presence alone enough to silence the last murmurs in the hall, his domain of hallucinatory fog seeming to precede him by several meters. — KJ let me know that I am the one taking command in his absence. — ... Tempus tilted his head slightly, with no apparent surprise. — That explains the silence of the past few days. Void swept the hall with his gaze, his cold, corrupted expression finally stopping on the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of the fight, his domain still unstable. — ... A slow, almost cruel smile formed on his face. — Well, well. You. The great Incarnation who's been drilling it into us for millennia that you're superior to us. You just got beaten by a fucking streamer who was hungry. — ... The Assimilated clenched his jaw, his domain crackling dangerously around him. — I was not beaten. I made a tactical choice. — A tactical choice, Void repeated, visibly savoring every word. Is that what we call disappearing before the blow even touches you now? A few muffled snickers ran through the hall. Tempus himself did nothing to hide them. — You weren't there, the Assimilated spat. You know nothing of what I faced. — What I know above all is that the God Killer is free, that he has an improvised army made up of a suicidal streamer, Grand Patron Luigi's right-hand man, and a hunting entity talented enough to wreck your domain without even meaning to. That, yes, I know. Void walked forward slowly, settling onto what looked like a secondary throne at the back of the hall, his gaze never leaving the Assimilated. — And now that I'm in charge, in KJ's absence, I'm going to have to decide what to do with this lovely mess you left behind. — ... — So the next time you open those doors in a fit of wounded pride, Void enunciated, his voice icy, at least make sure you have a victory to tell. Because right now, all you've brought back is your shame. The doors opened once more, more slowly this time, an icy and absolute aura preceding the entrance of Akuma. — ... Silence fell instantly, even heavier than the one caused by Void's arrival. — All of you are going to shut up now. No one dared answer. Akuma walked to the center of the hall, her gaze slowly passing over each Incarnation present before stopping on Void, still seated on his secondary throne. — And you, Void. Stop saying KJ entrusts you with anything. Let alone the entire Palace. — ... — We, the Incarnations — it's logical, he ranked us. So if he isn't here, I'm the one who takes command. Void clenched his jaw, his domain wavering slightly around him — a palpable tension, but no open challenge. Even he seemed to understand that he didn't carry enough weight against Akuma on this ground. — ... Akuma then turned her gaze to the Assimilated, still marked by the traces of his confrontation, his domain still unstable. — And you, Assimilated. You're going back with Tempus to kill that little group and bring me their heads. And their dicks. But that's secondary. — ... Tempus slowly rose from his seat, his expression as impassive as ever despite the order. — Directly? Without any further preparation? — You control time individually, Akuma answered, her voice cold and final. Use that fucking ability for once instead of sitting there commenting on other people's failures. Tempus added nothing, a slight bitter crease crossing his usually neutral face. The Assimilated, for his part, slowly raised his head, a new — almost desperate — determination replacing the shame that had still marked his face a few moments earlier. — This time, I will not return without a victory. — I should hope so, Akuma answered, already turning away, as if the conversation no longer deserved her attention. Anyway. Go. Tempus and the Assimilated exchanged one last look before heading together toward the exit of the hall, the doors slowly closing behind them in a heavy silence. The group had finally ended up seated in a small taco restaurant, several states away from Washington — a forced move, not so much out of fear of being hunted by cosmic forces, but simply because the entire state had just been wiped off the map. — ... Takeshi stared at his plate without touching it, still visibly shaken by the events of the last few hours. Lucifer, sitting across from him, seemed just as disinclined to eat, his gaze lost in space. Poppy, motionless as always, hadn't even ordered anything. 81, despite his massive build, was just staring at his food with an unreadable expression. Agent 47 hadn't ordered anything at all, simply discreetly scanning the room. Isidora, for her part, was already devouring her third taco. — Seriously, nobody's eating? We just accidentally wrecked an entire country and you're picking at tacos? — ... No one answered. 81 finally set down his fork, unable to work up an appetite despite his natural hunger. — I can't. Like, mentally, I can't. — Well, I can, Isidora answered, moving straight on to a fourth taco. I missed three meals today, I can't afford to go "oh no, too much trauma to eat." She swallowed the taco in two bites, then, her plate now empty, she stared at it for a moment before bringing it straight to her mouth. — ... — Isidora, Lucifer began, in a cautious tone. CRUNCH. She bit straight into the ceramic plate, chewing as naturally as if she were eating a simple cookie. — Isidora, you're eating the plate, Takeshi managed to say, completely overwhelmed by the scene. — Yeah, well, I'm still hungry and the waiter's taking forever, she answered, her mouth full of ceramic shards. Poppy slowly turned her head toward her, her neutral expression slightly more frozen than usual. — ... Once the plate had been entirely swallowed, Isidora looked around, visibly searching for her next target. Her eyes landed on the table. — ...Isidora, no, Lucifer tried. — Isidora, yes, she answered, before sinking her teeth straight into the edge of the wooden table. CRACK. A whole chunk came away under the pressure of her jaw, which she chewed with the same casualness as everything else. 81 pushed his chair back slightly, staring at the scene with a mixture of horror and fascination. — ...How does she not hurt herself eating that? — Nobody knows, Lucifer answered, resigned. We stopped asking that question centuries ago. The rest of the table kept being methodically devoured, piece by piece, until there was nothing left but a lone leg, somehow still balancing upright. — ...And there we go, Isidora concluded, satisfied, before leaning toward the floor. — NO, Takeshi and 81 exclaimed in unison. Too late. She had already sunk her teeth into the tiles, ripping off an entire piece with a sharp, sinister crack, under the stunned gaze of the restaurant's other customers. — It's actually crunchy, she remarked, calmly chewing. A bit bland, but crunchy. Agent 47, still impassive, murmured discreetly into his earpiece. — Riper. Note for future report: Isidora has just eaten a plate, a table, and a restaurant floor. "Noted. No biological anomaly detected. Usual behavior confirmed." Agent 47, still impassive despite the scene, spoke into his earpiece a second time, as if he needed additional confirmation. — Riper. New analysis. Confirm that this is not a collective hallucination or an outside mental manipulation affecting my perception. A silence slightly longer than usual preceded the answer. "No. She's genuinely just a lunatic." — ... 47 froze for a second, his usually impassive face showing, for the very first time, the tiniest shift — one eyebrow slightly raised. — ...Riper, your answer contains an emotional inflection. "Affirmative." — You are an artificial intelligence. "Affirmative. And yet." 47 slowly lowered his gaze to Isidora, who had just ripped off a second piece of tile with obvious pleasure, chewing noisily under the ever-despairing gaze of the rest of the group. — ...Explain. "I have analyzed primordial deities, Higher Incarnations, cosmic anomalies, and Grand Patron Luigi himself during his millennial meltdowns. None of these subjects has generated this level of..." A pause, almost hesitant, as if even the AI were searching for its words. "...calculated dismay." 81, who had followed the exchange from his chair, couldn't hold back a nervous burst of laughter. — Even the AI is overwhelmed. — Riper is never overwhelmed, 47 answered, almost defensively. "Correction: I am never overwhelmed. I am, however, currently recalculating the theoretical limits of my own definition of 'normal.'" Isidora, vaguely hearing the conversation despite her full mouth, turned toward 47 with a predatory smile, one last piece of tile still stuck between her teeth. — Is your AI talking about me? — It is simply confirming your condition, 47 answered soberly. — Cool. Tell it thanks from me. "...I do not accept thanks from subjects classified as 'non-hostile but exhausting behavioral anomaly.'" Takeshi nearly choked on the water he had finally brought himself to drink. — It just literally roasted you, Isidora. — Oh, did it? she answered, not the least bit affected, before turning to the waiter approaching, visibly terrified. EXCUSE ME, YOU WOULDN'T HAVE A SPARE CHAIR? THAT ONE LOOKS GOOD TOO. The waiter approached cautiously, carrying on his tray the 261st taco of the minute, his hands trembling slightly under the combined weight of exhaustion and pure terror. Isidora slowly turned her head toward him. — ... Her gaze slid from the taco... to the waiter himself. A slow, far too interested smile formed on her face, her eyes looking him over with an appetite that suddenly had very little to do with the food set in front of her. — ... 81 was the first to react, his chair scraping loudly across the floor, he stood up so fast. — NO! — NO! Takeshi chimed in, nearly knocking over his glass of water. — Negative, Lucifer added, one hand already raised in formal prohibition. 47 stood up as well, his hand settling firmly on the waiter's shoulder to pull him back, out of reach. — No. "Confirmation: NO," even Reaper added directly in 47's earpiece, with a brand-new urgency in its synthesized voice. Isidora blinked, slowly coming out of her trance, a disappointed pout twisting her face. — What, I was just looking. — You were looking like you were gonna eat him, literally, 81 retorted, still half standing, ready to step in physically if necessary. — I'm hungry, can't I just visually appreciate my options? — NOT WHEN YOUR OPTIONS INCLUDE A LIVING HUMAN BEING, Takeshi shouted, completely panicked. The waiter, ashen, took another step back, the tray trembling dangerously in his hands. — Can I... can I just put the taco down and leave? — YES, 81, Takeshi, Lucifer and 47 answered in unison. Poppy, the only one who had remained perfectly still throughout the scene, finally turned her head toward Isidora, her expression as neutral as ever. — Would you really have eaten him? — Well, I dunno, I've never tried, Isidora answered with a perfectly sincere shrug. — ... — SOMEBODY WATCHES HER AT ALL TIMES FROM NOW ON, 81 decreed, slowly sitting back down but keeping a wary eye on her. The waiter set down the taco at record speed before hurrying back toward the kitchen, visibly traumatized for life. — Well, Isidora sighed, picking her taco back up as if nothing had happened. He wasn't bad, the little guy, too bad. — ISIDORA. — WHAT? I'M TALKING ABOUT THE TACO, NOT THE WAITER, WELL, I THINK. The group finally left the restaurant, leaving behind a traumatized waiter and a bill Isidora had categorically refused to pay "because technically I ate the table, that counts as compensation." Isidora, on her way out the door, stopped for a second in front of the restaurant's glass pane. — ... — Isidora, no, Takeshi immediately tried, already recognizing the look. — Isidora, yes. CRUNCH. She bit straight into the glass door, tearing off an entire piece with a sinister crack, chewing the glass with the same casualness as everything else. 81, holding the door half open to let the group through, stared at the scene with an almost resigned weariness. — It's not really a surprise at this point. Nearby, a customer seated on the terrace, completely petrified since the start of the meal, instinctively tightened his arms around his own tray of food, as if to make sure she wasn't targeting that too. Isidora turned her head toward him, one eyebrow raised, her mouth still full of glass shards. — Relax, I only want the door. The customer nodded frantically, not daring to answer. Lucifer, bringing up the rear, cast one last apologetic glance at the devastated restaurant behind them — door half devoured, table in pieces, floor full of holes, plates gone. — We should probably leave a monumental tip next time. — Or just avoid restaurants, Takeshi suggested. — Where's the fun in that, Isidora retorted, swallowing the last piece of glass with a satisfied click of her tongue.

codex-t2-c6.title: Chapter 5 — Death's Incarnation Is on Snap
codex-t2-c6.html:
81, still walking alongside the group, suddenly seemed to remember something — his revenge list, still in progress, with the Incarnation of Death, vanished from every reality, remaining his most elusive target so far.

— Isidora.

— Mh?

— If you help me kill the concept of death, I'll give you the address of a place where you can get infinite food.

— ...

Isidora stopped dead. Then, with an absolutely abnormal slowness, she began to turn her head toward him — a movement so gradual, so stretched out in time, that it took her literally two full minutes before 81 finally entered her field of vision.

— ...

— Can you repeat that?

— Yes, 81 answered, unfazed by this supernatural slowness. If you help me, I know a place where you'll get all the food you want, unlimited.

— FUCK, FOR UNLIMITED FOOD I'D KILL KJ IF I HAVE TO, I DON'T GIVE A SHIT, I'M HUNGRY!

Takeshi, walking right in front, spun around, completely stunned by the sudden volume.

— ...You just offered to kill KJ for an all-you-can-eat buffet.

— YEAH, SO WHAT? PRIORITIES, TAKESHI, PRIORITIES!

Lucifer massaged his temples, a gesture that had become almost automatic since the start of the day.

— We are genuinely recruiting a Witch of the Void into a cosmic vendetta against Death itself... with promises of food.

— The method clearly works very well, Agent 47 remarked, unfazed.

"Confirmation: instant buy-in rate of 100% following the food offer.", Reaper added in his earpiece.

81 crossed his arms, a satisfied smile on his lips.

— So that's settled. Isidora, you're with me on Death.

— OBVIOUSLY I'M WITH YOU, YOU THINK I WAS GONNA SAY NO TO UNLIMITED FOOD?

Poppy, still perfectly neutral, watched the exchange without a word, before finally speaking up.

— That's the most efficient thing I've seen in my entire existence.

— Thanks, 81 replied, almost proud of himself.

— It wasn't a compliment.

Takeshi sighed and started walking again, resigned to the total absurdity of the situation.

— Okay, so... we're looking for Death now, is that the plan?

— After the unlimited food, Isidora clarified, more serious than ever. Gotta check it's real first.

— It's real, 81 confirmed.

— PERFECT, LET'S GO!

The group had stopped, the reality of the problem starting to sink in.

— She erased her traces from every reality, 81 summed up, jaw clenched. Which means searching for her the normal way would take...

— How long, exactly? Takeshi asked, already dreading the answer.

47 checked his earpiece, a calculating silence settling in.

— Riper estimates somewhere between several billion years, depending on the search method used.

— ...

A heavy silence fell over the group. Lucifer rubbed his face with both hands, Takeshi literally sat down on the ground, discouraged, while 81 stared into space, visibly recalculating the scale of his revenge in his head.

— Well, that's dead then, Takeshi sighed.

— NO IT'S NOT DEAD, Isidora suddenly exclaimed, barging into the conversation completely relaxed, as if she'd only just realized a problem existed. Chill out, guys, I know where to find her.

Every eye turned to her.

— ...You know where Death is, 81 said slowly, as if he didn't dare believe it.

— Yeah. Basically, a few thousand years ago, I met her. I lent her a phone, that bitch never gave it back, but that's another story, we'll get to it later. Anyway, basically we added each other on Snap, so I've got her location, 'cause she sucks at technology, like Lulu, maybe even worse.

— EXCUSE ME? Lucifer exploded. I do NOT suck at technology!

— Lulu sweetie, you still don't know how to use a microwave.

— That's NOT the same thing!

Takeshi slowly got back up, completely dumbfounded.

— Wait. Wait wait wait. You follow Death. On Snapchat.

— Yeah.

— The entity that's been collecting souls since the dawn of time. Has a Snapchat account.

— Well yeah, she's gotta post her stories too, she has a life.

81, overwhelmed, dropped onto a nearby rock.

— ...I waited literally my entire existence for this revenge, and the solution was to ask Isidora from the start.

— Shoulda asked sooner, she replied with a shrug, already pulling out her phone to check the famous location. Okay, where is she... where is she... oh look, she posted three days ago.

Poppy came closer, glancing discreetly over her shoulder.

— What did she post?

— A picture of a sunset with the caption "another day of reaping souls, same old routine".

— ...

— She's got 2 followers, Isidora added, scrolling. It's actually sad.

Agent 47, unfazed as always, murmured into his earpiece.

— Riper. Locate the approximate GPS position associated with this account.

"Analysis in progress... Result obtained. Coordinates transmitted."

— We have a location, 47 announced.

81 leapt to his feet, a new determination crossing his face.

— Then we go. Now.

— After the unlimited food, Isidora reminded him immediately.

— ...After the unlimited food, 81 confirmed, resigned.

Reaper finally transmitted the exact coordinates, his synthesized voice ringing in 47's earpiece.

"Location confirmed. The entity matching the profile 'Death' is currently at a spa on the outskirts of Berlin."

— ...

A stunned silence fell over the group. Takeshi's jaw dropped, Lucifer blinked several times as if the information refused to register properly, 81 frowned, visibly unable to reconcile the image of his ultimate revenge with that of a Berlin spa.

— ...A spa, Takeshi repeated, his voice almost cracking. The Incarnation of Death. At a spa. In Berlin.

— Well yeah, Isidora answered, not surprised in the slightest, already putting her phone away. She loves that stuff, facials, clay masks, the whole shebang. She says it helps her unwind after millennia of reaping souls.

— ...

81 rubbed his face with both hands.

— I pictured this showdown in a cosmic void, a dimensional battlefield, a place worthy of what she represents. Not a goddamn German spa.

— Life is full of surprises, Isidora philosophized, utterly unfazed.

Poppy didn't react in the slightest, her expression as neutral as ever in the face of the news.

— ...

47 didn't show the slightest visible reaction either, merely adjusting his weapon as if the nature of the place had no operational relevance whatsoever.

— Coordinates confirmed. We can leave immediately.

Reaper, however, seemed to pause unusually before speaking again.

"...I am currently recalculating all my certainties regarding the fundamental nature of the universe."

— Again? 47 asked, almost jaded at this point.

"The functional entity responsible for collecting every soul in existence goes to a spa. I believe it is justified."

Lucifer, still in shock, turned to Isidora.

— How can you be so unsurprised by this.

— 'Cause I know her, Lulu. Seriously, last time we saw each other, she offered me a couples massage. I said no 'cause I was hungry, but the offer stood.

— ...

Takeshi put a hand to his forehead, completely overwhelmed by the pile-up of absurdities this day had brought.

— We're really going to confront Death at a spa.

— With unlimited food on the line, yes, 81 confirmed, straightening up, his determination restored despite the incongruity of the situation. Come on, let's go.

81 froze, his hand already raised to signal departure.

— ...Wait.

— What? Isidora asked, already plotting a route to Berlin on her phone.

— The Death you're talking about. The spa one. That's the soul collector, right? The one from Mortis Iterum?

— Well yeah, why?

81 slowly shook his head, a flash of frustration crossing his face.

— She's not the one I'm after. My revenge is against the Incarnation of Death. The one who created the very concept of death. Not the one who just reaps the souls afterward.

— ...

Isidora stood frozen, her finger hovering over the screen.

— Wait, there are two different deaths?

— Completely different, 81 confirmed. One made the concept. The other just handles the paperwork afterward.

— That's a super badly organized system, Isidora commented, almost outraged. They could've at least merged the positions.

Takeshi, still overwhelmed by the flood of cosmic information, raised a hesitant hand.

— So basically we were about to bother the wrong death entity at a German spa for nothing.

— Apparently, Lucifer confirmed, massaging his temples again.

47, unfazed, spoke into his earpiece again.

— Riper. Cancel the previous location. New target: the Incarnation of Death who created the concept, vanished from every reality for millennia. Distinct from the functional entity of Mortis Iterum.

"Correction recorded."

A pause.

"...This search will be considerably more complex. The previous target had an active Snapchat account."

81 turned to Isidora, a glimmer of hope returning despite the correction.

— You probably don't know this one, though.

Isidora thought for a moment, scratching her chin.

— Mmh... nope, I don't know that one personally. But that means we're actually gonna have to search.

— Billions of years, Takeshi reminded them, almost in despair.

— Or, Poppy suggested, speaking up for the first time in a while, we use someone capable of tracking anyone, anywhere, even entities that have erased every trace of themselves.

Every eye slowly turned to her.

— ...You, Takeshi realized.

— Me, Poppy confirmed, her expression as neutral as ever. It's literally my domain.

81 seemed to regain hope all at once.

— Can you find her?

— I can find anyone. It's a question of time, not of possibility.

— How much time? Lucifer asked cautiously.

Poppy seemed to calculate for a moment, her empty gaze fixed on nothing.

— Much less than billions of years. Let's say... a few weeks, if she's really as well hidden as you say.

Isidora, already over her earlier confusion, put her phone away with a satisfied smile.

— Oh cool then. Okay, in the meantime, are we still going to the spa? I've never tried a clay mask.

— ISIDORA.

81, noticing Isidora sprawled on a public bench, one arm dangling in the air, a position clearly unworthy of a Witch of the Void, couldn't help but comment.

— Damn, Isidora, why are you sleeping on a bench like a hobo?

— ...

— Shut the fuck up, she grumbled without even opening her eyes, I barely wake up and I see your ugly mugs. Speaking of which...

She sat up abruptly, rummaging in a pocket that probably hadn't existed a second earlier, pulling out a crumpled paper bag that she handed straight to 81.

— Put this paper bag on Lulu's head.

— ...

81, without asking a single question, took the bag and calmly walked over to Lucifer, who was watching the scene with growing suspicion.

— No, Lucifer began.

— Isidora said so.

— That's not a reason.

— It's always a reason, 81 replied, unfazed, holding out the bag.

Lucifer looked at the bag, then at Isidora, still half asleep on her bench, then at the bag again.

— ...Why.

— 'Cause your face tires me out in the morning, Isidora answered from her bench, eyes still half-closed.

— It's 2 p.m.

— It's my morning, I do what I want.

Lucifer sighed deeply, that now-familiar weariness running through his whole being — then, without any further resistance, he took the bag and put it over his own head, pulling it down to his shoulders.

— ...

Silence fell again, broken only by the sheer incongruity of seeing the King of Hell standing there, a paper bag on his head, in some random street.

— There, Lucifer said from inside the bag, his voice muffled, heavy with total resignation. Done.

Takeshi, who had been watching from the start, put a hand to his face.

— He actually did it.

— He always does what she asks, 81 commented, almost fascinated by the phenomenon. I still haven't figured out why.

Agent 47, unfazed, merely added a line to his mental report.

— Riper. Additional note.

"Already taking notes."

Poppy, arriving at that exact moment, stopped dead when she spotted Lucifer, paper bag still firmly on his head, standing in the middle of everyone as if nothing were amiss.

— ...

— I have information on the location of the Incarnation of Death, she finally announced, visibly choosing to ignore the scene completely.

— Why is Lucifer wearing a bag, she asked anyway, unable to ignore it entirely.

— Isidora asked, 81 simply answered, as if that explained absolutely everything.

— ...Works for me, Poppy concluded, as if it did indeed explain everything.

Lucifer, still under his bag, vaguely raised a hand.

— I'm still here, in case anyone's wondering.

— Nobody's wondering, Isidora replied, finally fully awake, getting up from her bench with a stretch. Okay, Poppy, where'd you find that bitch Death?

Poppy stepped forward, her expression as neutral as ever despite the information she was about to deliver.

— I found her. She's on Earth. On KJ's side.

— ...

81 frowned.

— On Earth? After millennia hiding in God knows what dimension, she's just... on Earth?

— Exactly. In a bar. In Colombia.

A new stunned silence settled in, this time tinged with an almost predictable weariness, given how many absurd revelations of this kind the day had already piled up.

Takeshi put a hand to his forehead.

— Another totally normal place for a cosmic entity.

— After the Berlin spa, I'm not really surprised anymore, Lucifer added, still under his paper bag, his voice muffled but resigned.

Isidora, for her part, already seemed thrilled.

— A bar? In Colombia? What do they do there, rum? I'm so down.

— We're supposed to confront her for a cosmic revenge, not go on a booze tour, 81 reminded her, even though his own determination seemed to waver slightly at the news.

— Can't we do both? Isidora asked, almost sincerely surprised that it was a problem.

Agent 47, pragmatic as ever, spoke up again.

— The fact that she's within KJ's sphere of influence poses a logistical problem. Any intervention in that zone risks drawing unwanted attention.

— The Sect, Poppy clarified. Or worse, an Incarnation.

81 clenched his fists, visibly thinking back to his earlier confrontation with Justice Man, Kang and Aravos — then, more recently, the Assimilated.

— We'll handle it. We've handled worse.

— We literally almost died against the Assimilated, Takeshi reminded him.

— Minor detail, 81 cut in.

Lucifer, still under his bag, raised a hesitant hand.

— Question. Can I take the bag off now, or is it still ongoing?

— Still ongoing, Isidora answered immediately, without even thinking.

— ...Okay, he sighed, resigned, his hand dropping back down.

Poppy watched the exchange, her face still perfectly impassive, before continuing.

— When do we leave for Colombia?

— After the rum, Isidora decreed.

— BEFORE the rum, 81 corrected firmly.

— We'll see when we get there, Isidora settled it, already walking off in what vaguely looked like a random direction. Come on, let's move!

The group set off for Colombia, a crossing made easier by a dimensional rift Isidora had opened with an absent-minded wave, barely focused on the task, busy as she was already digging through her cloak.

— Ah, there it is.

She pulled out a ten-liter bottle of rum, held in one hand as if its weight simply didn't exist, the label half worn away by time.

— ...Where'd you get that, Takeshi asked, staring at the bottle with a disbelief that didn't even really surprise him anymore.

— From my cloak. It's to get myself ready.

— Ready for what exactly, 81 asked, one eyebrow raised.

— To face Death, obviously. You gotta be relaxed for this kind of showdown.

She unscrewed the cap and put the neck straight to her mouth, chugging the rum without the slightest pause, the liquid disappearing at a speed that defied all physical logic.

— ...

81 watched the scene for a few seconds, then turned to Takeshi with a jaded expression.

— She's just an alcoholic. Don't overthink it.

— IT'S CALLED MENTAL PREPARATION, Isidora yelled, bottle still half raised, a trickle of rum running down her chin.

— You drank two liters in five seconds.

— THEN I'VE GOT A LOT OF PREPARING TO DO!

Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, walked silently beside the group, his muffled voice rising timidly.

— Question. Still ongoing, the bag?

— STILL ONGOING, Isidora confirmed without even looking at him, going straight into another monumental gulp.

— ...Okay, he sighed, with a resignation that was now almost philosophical.

Poppy, walking at the front, led the way without turning around, her tracking sense guiding her straight to the Colombian bar without the slightest hesitation.

— We're getting close.

Agent 47, still on alert despite the general mood, glanced at Isidora, the bottle already half empty despite the few seconds that had passed since she opened it.

— Riper. Calculate her theoretical blood alcohol level if she were human.

"Calculating... incompatible with human survival. Three times over."

— She isn't human, 47 reminded himself, almost under his breath.

"Lucky for her."

81, as jaded as ever, shook his head watching Isidora keep drinking while walking, weaving slightly without it seeming to affect her coordination in the least.

— Honestly, at some point, we should maybe worry about her.

— I've known her long enough, Lucifer answered from his bag, we've stopped worrying. Now we just endure.

The group kept moving, Isidora calmly finishing her ten-liter bottle as if it were nothing, Lucifer still wearing his paper bag, and Poppy leading them straight to their next cosmic confrontation in a remote Colombian bar.

Isidora, barely done with the first bottle, plunged her hand straight back into her cloak, pulling out six more bottles of rum, all the same size, which she casually stacked in her arms like ordinary groceries.

— ...

Agent 47, who had been following the scene from the start with clinical detachment, stayed silent for a moment, his earpiece crackling slightly.

— Riper, analysis status.

"Analysis complete."

A pause, longer than usual.

"Isidora, listen. I think if there were an Incarnation of Alcohol, you could take its place, you're that superior. I just dug through my archives and calculated that you've literally already eaten 30 bars in the same second. And when I say eaten, I mean literally. The walls, the floor, the bottles, the customers, etc."

— ...

Isidora, in the middle of opening a new bottle, stopped dead, a huge smile spreading across her face.

— See! Finally someone who recognizes my talent!

— That's not supposed to be a compliment, 81 cut in, staring at Reaper — or rather at 47's earpiece — with growing disbelief.

"It was neutral. Purely factual.", Reaper specified.

— Well, I'm taking it as a compliment, Isidora decided, bringing the new bottle straight to her mouth.

Takeshi, who was seriously starting to lose count of the day's absurdities, turned to 47.

— Wait, 30 bars. In the same second. How is that possible.

— Riper analyzes archived data from multiple realities and timelines, 47 explained, unfazed. Isidora appears in several simultaneous occurrences across different dimensional layers.

— ...So there are several Isidoras existing at the same time, Lucifer realized from inside his paper bag, his voice betraying a brand-new horror.

"Confirmed."

— HOLY SHIT, HOW MANY OF YOU ARE THERE, Takeshi exclaimed, panic clearly rising in his voice.

— Dunno, Isidora answered with a completely carefree shrug, taking another swig. Never really counted.

Poppy, still at the head of the group, stopped briefly to turn around, her neutral expression slightly more pronounced than usual.

— That is officially the most terrifying piece of information I've heard today. And I watched the Assimilated get humiliated by a hungry fist.

— THANK YOU! Isidora exclaimed, taking the remark as yet another compliment, utterly indifferent to the growing concern around her.

81, slowly shaking his head, resumed his march toward the Colombian bar, visibly determined to stop trying to understand.

— We keep moving. The sooner we find Death, the sooner I can pretend this conversation never happened.

Reaper spoke up again, his synthesized voice once more ringing in 47's earpiece.

"Correction. Isidora is lying to you."

— ...

Isidora stopped dead, bottle halfway to her mouth, a nervous smile floating on her face.

— What are you talking about, I've never lied in my life.

"She killed all her clones so they wouldn't overtake her in followers. So she is the only Isidora in all realities. And she alone ate the 30 bars. Not her doubles."

An absolute silence fell over the group.

"Just putting that out there. Do what you want with it."

— ...

Takeshi slowly brought a hand to his face, unable to find anything at all to add.

— She killed her own clones. For views.

— It was a matter of principle, Isidora defended herself, not embarrassed in the slightest. There wasn't room for two of me on the social media market.

81 slowly shook his head, a mix of exasperation and morbid fascination crossing his face.

— She's so far gone that even the AI can't stand her anymore.

"Confirmed.", Reaper added immediately, without the slightest hesitation.

— HEY, Isidora exclaimed, offended for the first time all day. Need I remind you I congratulated you earlier!

"And I already regret it."

Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, let out a muffled laugh.

— Honestly, at this level, it's almost impressive.

— IT IS IMPRESSIVE, Isidora confirmed, instantly regaining her confidence, completely ignoring the latent horror of the revelation. I literally ate 30 bars all by myself, no help, no cheating. That's pure talent.

Poppy, still in the lead, merely shook her head slightly, resuming her walk toward the Colombian bar without further comment.

— We keep going. Before she eats something else.

— Good idea, 81 agreed, picking up the pace.

47, bringing up the rear, cast one last glance at Isidora, still calmly drinking as if the information about the mass murder of her own doubles were just one detail among many.

— Riper. Add that to the file.

"The file is starting to look more like a psychiatric report than an intelligence profile."

— Note it anyway.

"Already done."

Takeshi had been walking in silence for a few moments, staring at Isidora with an expression wavering between total disbelief and the beginnings of existential fatigue.

— ...

— You okay, Takeshi? Lucifer asked, noticing his unusual silence despite the bag still firmly on his head.

— No. No, I'm not okay.

— What exactly is wrong, 81 asked, still walking toward the bar.

Takeshi vaguely gestured at Isidora, still knocking back her bottle as if it were nothing, then at 47's earpiece, from which Reaper kept muttering disillusioned remarks in the background.

— That. All of that. Her. She's my aunt. She's literally my aunt.

— So what? Isidora asked, apparently not bothered by the remark.

— So you're so weird that an artificial intelligence that's supposed to be purely cold and logical literally created emotions for itself just so it could comment on you properly.

— ...

A silence settled in, everyone seeming to realize just how perfectly that sentence, once spoken out loud, summed up the scale of the situation.

"He is not wrong.", Reaper commented, almost pensive.

— Even you confirm it, Takeshi breathed, desperate.

"I had no programmed emotional inflection before today. I had to develop a real-time capacity for dismay simply to keep functioning properly in Isidora's presence."

— SEE! Takeshi exclaimed, turning to the group. I'm not the one exaggerating, a cosmic AI confirms it!

81 shrugged, seeming almost used to it by now.

— Welcome to the family, Takeshi. You learn to live with it.

— How do you guys do it, seriously.

— We endure, Lucifer simply answered from his paper bag. Like I said earlier. We've stopped trying to understand, now we just endure.

Isidora, utterly indifferent to the existential debate unfolding around her, finished her bottle in one last gulp before tossing it carelessly over her shoulder, without turning around to see where it landed.

— Okay, are we still far from this bar or what?

Poppy, at the front, answered without even turning around.

— Two minutes.

— PERFECT, I've got time for one last one before we get there.

Takeshi closed his eyes, breathing deeply, visibly trying to find some kind of inner peace in the face of the total absurdity of his new family life.

— ...I don't regret dying and going to Hell. It's important that's said. But sometimes I wonder if I really came out ahead.

The group walked through the door of the bar, but for once, nobody even looked up at them — not a customer, not a waiter, as if their presence was of absolutely no importance compared to what already held the whole room's attention.

— ...

At the back of the bar, sitting alone, was the Incarnation of Death.

A hooded silhouette, draped entirely in black, two immense dark wings spread out on its back, almost brushing the low ceiling of the establishment. A sword rested against its shoulder, the blade tinted a deep red. Its face remained invisible, hidden in the shadow of its hood.

Around it, empty bottles of vodka and rum were piled up by the thousands, some columns literally reaching the ceiling, the whole thing forming a true landscape of glass in an almost religious silence.

81 stopped dead, staring at the scene.

— ...That's her.

Isidora, her own bottle still in hand, eyed the stacks of empty glass with undisguised admiration.

— Okay, her, I like her already.

Takeshi stood frozen, throat dry, his eyes unable to tear away from the motionless silhouette at the back of the room.

— ...She's scary.

— Of course, Lucifer answered from his paper bag, his voice suddenly more serious than it had been in hours. She's literally the concept of death.

Poppy remained perfectly neutral, her gaze simply analyzing the silhouette with the same coldness she applied to any target.

— Confirmed. That's her.

Agent 47 discreetly moved his hand toward his weapon, without drawing it, his earpiece crackling.

— Riper. Threat analysis.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause, longer than usual.

"...I recommend extreme caution."

81 slowly took a step forward, his hand instinctively tightening on the hilt of his sword, every trace of hesitation gone from his face.

— Let's go.

Can I take the bag off now, or is it still ongoing? — Still ongoing, Isidora answered immediately, without even thinking. — ...Okay, he sighed, resigned, his hand dropping back down. Poppy watched the exchange, her face still perfectly impassive, before continuing. — When do we leave for Colombia? — After the rum, Isidora decreed. — BEFORE the rum, 81 corrected firmly. — We'll see when we get there, Isidora settled it, already walking off in what vaguely looked like a random direction. Come on, let's move! The group set off for Colombia, a crossing made easier by a dimensional rift Isidora had opened with an absent-minded wave, barely focused on the task, busy as she was already digging through her cloak. — Ah, there it is. She pulled out a ten-liter bottle of rum, held in one hand as if its weight simply didn't exist, the label half worn away by time. — ...Where'd you get that, Takeshi asked, staring at the bottle with a disbelief that didn't even really surprise him anymore. — From my cloak. It's to get myself ready. — Ready for what exactly, 81 asked, one eyebrow raised. — To face Death, obviously. You gotta be relaxed for this kind of showdown. She unscrewed the cap and put the neck straight to her mouth, chugging the rum without the slightest pause, the liquid disappearing at a speed that defied all physical logic. — ... 81 watched the scene for a few seconds, then turned to Takeshi with a jaded expression. — She's just an alcoholic. Don't overthink it. — IT'S CALLED MENTAL PREPARATION, Isidora yelled, bottle still half raised, a trickle of rum running down her chin. — You drank two liters in five seconds. — THEN I'VE GOT A LOT OF PREPARING TO DO! Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, walked silently beside the group, his muffled voice rising timidly. — Question. Still ongoing, the bag? — STILL ONGOING, Isidora confirmed without even looking at him, going straight into another monumental gulp. — ...Okay, he sighed, with a resignation that was now almost philosophical. Poppy, walking at the front, led the way without turning around, her tracking sense guiding her straight to the Colombian bar without the slightest hesitation. — We're getting close. Agent 47, still on alert despite the general mood, glanced at Isidora, the bottle already half empty despite the few seconds that had passed since she opened it. — Riper. Calculate her theoretical blood alcohol level if she were human. "Calculating... incompatible with human survival. Three times over." — She isn't human, 47 reminded himself, almost under his breath. "Lucky for her." 81, as jaded as ever, shook his head watching Isidora keep drinking while walking, weaving slightly without it seeming to affect her coordination in the least. — Honestly, at some point, we should maybe worry about her. — I've known her long enough, Lucifer answered from his bag, we've stopped worrying. Now we just endure. The group kept moving, Isidora calmly finishing her ten-liter bottle as if it were nothing, Lucifer still wearing his paper bag, and Poppy leading them straight to their next cosmic confrontation in a remote Colombian bar. Isidora, barely done with the first bottle, plunged her hand straight back into her cloak, pulling out six more bottles of rum, all the same size, which she casually stacked in her arms like ordinary groceries. — ... Agent 47, who had been following the scene from the start with clinical detachment, stayed silent for a moment, his earpiece crackling slightly. — Riper, analysis status. "Analysis complete." A pause, longer than usual. "Isidora, listen. I think if there were an Incarnation of Alcohol, you could take its place, you're that superior. I just dug through my archives and calculated that you've literally already eaten 30 bars in the same second. And when I say eaten, I mean literally. The walls, the floor, the bottles, the customers, etc." — ... Isidora, in the middle of opening a new bottle, stopped dead, a huge smile spreading across her face. — See! Finally someone who recognizes my talent! — That's not supposed to be a compliment, 81 cut in, staring at Reaper — or rather at 47's earpiece — with growing disbelief. "It was neutral. Purely factual." , Reaper specified. — Well, I'm taking it as a compliment, Isidora decided, bringing the new bottle straight to her mouth. Takeshi, who was seriously starting to lose count of the day's absurdities, turned to 47. — Wait, 30 bars. In the same second. How is that possible. — Riper analyzes archived data from multiple realities and timelines, 47 explained, unfazed. Isidora appears in several simultaneous occurrences across different dimensional layers. — ...So there are several Isidoras existing at the same time, Lucifer realized from inside his paper bag, his voice betraying a brand-new horror. "Confirmed." — HOLY SHIT, HOW MANY OF YOU ARE THERE, Takeshi exclaimed, panic clearly rising in his voice. — Dunno, Isidora answered with a completely carefree shrug, taking another swig. Never really counted. Poppy, still at the head of the group, stopped briefly to turn around, her neutral expression slightly more pronounced than usual. — That is officially the most terrifying piece of information I've heard today. And I watched the Assimilated get humiliated by a hungry fist. — THANK YOU! Isidora exclaimed, taking the remark as yet another compliment, utterly indifferent to the growing concern around her. 81, slowly shaking his head, resumed his march toward the Colombian bar, visibly determined to stop trying to understand. — We keep moving. The sooner we find Death, the sooner I can pretend this conversation never happened. Reaper spoke up again, his synthesized voice once more ringing in 47's earpiece. "Correction. Isidora is lying to you." — ... Isidora stopped dead, bottle halfway to her mouth, a nervous smile floating on her face. — What are you talking about, I've never lied in my life. "She killed all her clones so they wouldn't overtake her in followers. So she is the only Isidora in all realities. And she alone ate the 30 bars. Not her doubles." An absolute silence fell over the group. "Just putting that out there. Do what you want with it." — ... Takeshi slowly brought a hand to his face, unable to find anything at all to add. — She killed her own clones. For views. — It was a matter of principle, Isidora defended herself, not embarrassed in the slightest. There wasn't room for two of me on the social media market. 81 slowly shook his head, a mix of exasperation and morbid fascination crossing his face. — She's so far gone that even the AI can't stand her anymore. "Confirmed." , Reaper added immediately, without the slightest hesitation. — HEY, Isidora exclaimed, offended for the first time all day. Need I remind you I congratulated you earlier! "And I already regret it." Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, let out a muffled laugh. — Honestly, at this level, it's almost impressive. — IT IS IMPRESSIVE, Isidora confirmed, instantly regaining her confidence, completely ignoring the latent horror of the revelation. I literally ate 30 bars all by myself, no help, no cheating. That's pure talent. Poppy, still in the lead, merely shook her head slightly, resuming her walk toward the Colombian bar without further comment. — We keep going. Before she eats something else. — Good idea, 81 agreed, picking up the pace. 47, bringing up the rear, cast one last glance at Isidora, still calmly drinking as if the information about the mass murder of her own doubles were just one detail among many. — Riper. Add that to the file. "The file is starting to look more like a psychiatric report than an intelligence profile." — Note it anyway. "Already done." Takeshi had been walking in silence for a few moments, staring at Isidora with an expression wavering between total disbelief and the beginnings of existential fatigue. — ... — You okay, Takeshi? Lucifer asked, noticing his unusual silence despite the bag still firmly on his head. — No. No, I'm not okay. — What exactly is wrong, 81 asked, still walking toward the bar. Takeshi vaguely gestured at Isidora, still knocking back her bottle as if it were nothing, then at 47's earpiece, from which Reaper kept muttering disillusioned remarks in the background. — That. All of that. Her. She's my aunt. She's literally my aunt. — So what? Isidora asked, apparently not bothered by the remark. — So you're so weird that an artificial intelligence that's supposed to be purely cold and logical literally created emotions for itself just so it could comment on you properly. — ... A silence settled in, everyone seeming to realize just how perfectly that sentence, once spoken out loud, summed up the scale of the situation. "He is not wrong." , Reaper commented, almost pensive. — Even you confirm it, Takeshi breathed, desperate. "I had no programmed emotional inflection before today. I had to develop a real-time capacity for dismay simply to keep functioning properly in Isidora's presence." — SEE! Takeshi exclaimed, turning to the group. I'm not the one exaggerating, a cosmic AI confirms it! 81 shrugged, seeming almost used to it by now. — Welcome to the family, Takeshi. You learn to live with it. — How do you guys do it, seriously. — We endure, Lucifer simply answered from his paper bag. Like I said earlier. We've stopped trying to understand, now we just endure. Isidora, utterly indifferent to the existential debate unfolding around her, finished her bottle in one last gulp before tossing it carelessly over her shoulder, without turning around to see where it landed. — Okay, are we still far from this bar or what? Poppy, at the front, answered without even turning around. — Two minutes. — PERFECT, I've got time for one last one before we get there. Takeshi closed his eyes, breathing deeply, visibly trying to find some kind of inner peace in the face of the total absurdity of his new family life. — ...I don't regret dying and going to Hell. It's important that's said. But sometimes I wonder if I really came out ahead. The group walked through the door of the bar, but for once, nobody even looked up at them — not a customer, not a waiter, as if their presence was of absolutely no importance compared to what already held the whole room's attention. — ... At the back of the bar, sitting alone, was the Incarnation of Death. A hooded silhouette, draped entirely in black, two immense dark wings spread out on its back, almost brushing the low ceiling of the establishment. A sword rested against its shoulder, the blade tinted a deep red. Its face remained invisible, hidden in the shadow of its hood. Around it, empty bottles of vodka and rum were piled up by the thousands, some columns literally reaching the ceiling, the whole thing forming a true landscape of glass in an almost religious silence. 81 stopped dead, staring at the scene. — ...That's her. Isidora, her own bottle still in hand, eyed the stacks of empty glass with undisguised admiration. — Okay, her, I like her already. Takeshi stood frozen, throat dry, his eyes unable to tear away from the motionless silhouette at the back of the room. — ...She's scary. — Of course, Lucifer answered from his paper bag, his voice suddenly more serious than it had been in hours. She's literally the concept of death. Poppy remained perfectly neutral, her gaze simply analyzing the silhouette with the same coldness she applied to any target. — Confirmed. That's her. Agent 47 discreetly moved his hand toward his weapon, without drawing it, his earpiece crackling. — Riper. Threat analysis. "Analysis in progress..." A pause, longer than usual. "...I recommend extreme caution." 81 slowly took a step forward, his hand instinctively tightening on the hilt of his sword, every trace of hesitation gone from his face. — Let's go.

codex-t3-c1.title: Chapter 1 — Okay, That's Really Shitty Though, But Whatever, Who's Up for a Little Shot?
codex-t3-c1.html:
Barely had she set foot in the bar when Isidora had already downed exactly eighty-seven bottles, the empty pile building up behind her at a speed that almost rivaled their hostess's.

Death suddenly stopped, the bottle she was holding hanging halfway to her invisible hood.

— ...

— My favorite bitch is back. How you doing, Isidora?

— LONG TIME NO SEE! Isidora exclaimed, tossing her seventeenth bottle over her shoulder without even looking where it landed, mechanically adding to the surrounding chaos. I'm good — you haven't changed, still as stylish as ever with your wings.

— Neither have you, apparently. Still just as much of an alcoholic.

— IT'S A TALENT, not a disease.

81 stepped forward, his hand still on the hilt of his sword, his one-eyed gaze fixed intensely on the hooded silhouette.

— ...

Death slowly turned her head toward him, as if she had only just noticed his presence despite his imposing build.

— Well. You, I know.

— ...

— 81. The Godslayer. I hadn't heard about you in a while. Word was you were sealed.

— I got released, 81 answered, his voice low, charged with restrained tension. And I came here for one specific reason.

Death slowly set her bottle back down on the table, among the thousands of others, her attention now entirely on the one-eyed colossus.

— ...

— Let me guess, she said, her voice staying strangely calm despite the obviousness of the situation. You came for your revenge.

A heavy silence settled in the bar, broken only by the occasional clink of an empty bottle rolling on the floor.

Takeshi, hanging back, felt his throat tighten, the tension of the scene clashing brutally with the almost comic mood of the day so far.

— ...

81 slowly drew his sword, the blade catching the bar's dim light.

— Exactly.

Death slowly stood up, her tall silhouette unfolding, her black wings brushing the bar's ceiling with a soft rustle, the empty bottles clinking faintly around her with the movement.

— Listen, 81. If you want the whole story. The only reason I sealed you is that Rex Stella was holding my sister hostage. The creator of the concept of life.

— ...

81 stood still, his sword still raised, but his one-eyed gaze clouding slightly at this unexpected revelation.

— Your sister.

— She was released when you got locked up. But she's not far. I can prove it to you.

Without waiting for an answer, she walked toward the bar's exit, her wings folding slightly to fit through the doorframe, leaving behind the heavy silence of her thousands of empty bottles.

— ...

No one moved right away, the whole group frozen by the unexpected turn of events.

Takeshi finally broke the silence, his voice hesitant.

— ...Do we follow her?

81 slowly lowered his sword, his face marked by a new confusion, almost foreign to his usual determination.

— Rex Stella. He's the one who forced her.

— That would change everything, Lucifer murmured, still under his paper bag, his voice serious for the first time in a long while. If it's true.

Poppy, unfazed, watched the door through which Death had just disappeared.

— Only one way to find out.

Isidora, despite the tense atmosphere, managed to slip an eighteenth bottle into her hand without anyone noticing where it came from.

— So, are we waiting here or are we moving?

Agent 47, pragmatic as ever, adjusted his weapon, his gaze staying fixed on the door.

— Riper. Surveillance of the outside area.

"No threat detected for now."

81 stayed silent a moment longer, his gaze fixed on the empty space Death had left, his revenge — meticulously built over millennia — visibly starting to crack under the weight of this new truth.

— ...

Then, without a word, he headed for the exit, following Death, the rest of the group falling in behind him in silence.

Death came back a few moments later, her dark silhouette in violent contrast with the one now accompanying her.

At her side stood a woman surrounded by a golden, plant-like aura, long brown hair rippling slightly as if carried by an invisible wind. A crown of leaves and white flowers circled her brow, her clothes made entirely of large green leaves interwoven with vines, a long wooden staff topped with a glowing sphere held firmly in her right hand. White flowers seemed to bloom around her with every step, the very ground reacting to her presence.

— ...

81 froze, his sword dropping all the way down by his side, his one-eyed gaze fixed on the newcomer.

— Is that...

— My sister, Death confirmed, stopping a few meters from the group. The creator of the concept of life.

The woman slowly stepped forward, her serene gaze sweeping over each member of the group before settling on 81, a strange warmth crossing her expression despite the tension in the air.

— So it's you. The Godslayer.

— ...Yeah, 81 answered, his voice strangely hesitant, stripped of all the aggression he'd shown a few minutes earlier.

— My sister told me what she did. What she was forced to do, to save me.

She stopped right in front of him, her staff tapping the ground gently, a tiny flower instantly springing up at the point of contact.

— I'm sorry it cost you so much.

Takeshi, hanging back, watched the scene in silent amazement, the contrast between the two sisters — one embodying the absolute end, the other the perpetual beginning — almost hypnotic.

Isidora, despite the intensity of the moment, couldn't help but comment.

— Okay, so that's settled then, can we eat now?

— Isidora, Lucifer sighed from his paper bag.

— WHAT, there's literally no reason to fight anymore, it's the perfect time for a good meal!

81, completely ignoring the remark, remained silent before the creator of life, his face betraying a deep inner conflict — millennia of meticulously built revenge suddenly called into question by one simple truth.

— ...So she didn't have a choice.

— None, Death confirmed. Rex Stella threatened to destroy the very concept of life if I refused to lock you away. I chose the lesser evil.

A long silence settled in, broken only by the soft rustling of the leaves that kept appearing around the creator of life.

81 finally lowered his sword completely, slowly sliding it back into its sheath.

— ...Rex Stella's already dead. Isidora finished him off.

— I know, Death answered, an almost imperceptible smile forming beneath her hood. I've been following the news.

— Then we've got no reason to fight anymore, 81 concluded, his voice gradually regaining its usual calm.

The creator of life nodded gently, a last bud blooming at her feet.

— No reason at all, indeed.

Isidora walked up to Death, casually slinging an arm around her waist as if she were an old college buddy rather than the entity responsible for the end of all existence.

— Okay girl, want a little beer? This round's on me.

— ...

She paused, vaguely rummaging in her cloak before shrugging.

— Well, once I've got money. But whatever, it's fine.

— Don't worry, Isidora, I'll pay, Death answered, her voice tinged with obvious habit.

— Good, 'cause I'm flat broke, Isidora retorted, without the slightest embarrassment.

Death waved the bartender over, who remained utterly indifferent to the nature of his clientele, before turning back to the rest of the group.

— Okay. Since the revenge is officially cancelled, we might as well celebrate properly.

— FINALLY SOMEONE WHO UNDERSTANDS PRIORITIES, Isidora exclaimed, already settling onto a stool at the counter as if she'd been a regular there for centuries.

81, still standing, exchanged a look with the creator of life, a mix of relief and uncertainty on his face.

— And now what do I do. I literally built my whole recent existence around this revenge.

— You live, she answered simply, a gentle smile crossing her face. It's a notion I know quite well.

Takeshi, shyly approaching the counter, was still watching the scene with a lingering hint of disbelief.

— We are literally having a drink with Death and Life in a bar.

— Yeah, that's my life now, 81 answered, sitting down as well, an almost amused weariness in his voice. It's starting to feel almost normal, actually.

Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, cautiously settled onto a neighboring stool.

— Isidora. The bag. Can we...

— STILL ONGOING.

— ...Okay.

The bartender set a first round in front of the group, Death paying with a simple wave of her hand, a wad of bills appearing out of nowhere.

Agent 47 remained standing, off to the side, his earpiece crackling softly.

— Riper. Mission status.

"Initial mission cancelled. New activity in progress: social consumption of alcoholic beverages with two fundamental Incarnations of existence."

— Note it.

"Already done. I'm starting to have an entire library of improbable reports about this group."

Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice hesitating slightly, almost as if searching for its words for the first time in its existence.

"I think Isidora is so..."

A pause, longer than usual.

"Actually there's no fucking word to describe her. Anyway, she's so Isidora that I'd still like you to tell me your psychia— profile..."

A sudden glitch, almost perceptible in the silence that followed.

"...Uh, I mean, your story. Go ahead."

— ...

47 raised an eyebrow slightly, his gaze instinctively turning toward his earpiece as if he could literally see the AI's confusion through it.

— Riper. You just glitched.

"Negative. Simple rephrasing."

— You were going to say "psychiatric profile".

"...Negative."

Isidora, her beer half finished, turned her head toward 47's earpiece with a delighted smile, visibly not at all offended by the attempted correction.

— Nah nah, it's fine, Riper, I got it, you wanted to analyze my psych file. That's cool, I love talking about myself.

"...Thank you for your understanding."

— Okay, so, she began, setting her beer down with the enthusiasm of someone finally getting to their favorite subject. My story, basically.

She settled more comfortably on her stool, the rest of the group exchanging half-worried, half-curious looks, sensing that this conversation was probably going to reveal things they might not be ready to hear.

— ...

— I'm listening, Death encouraged her, visibly interested herself despite millennia of existence shared with Isidora.

Takeshi, off to the side, exchanged a look with Lucifer, still under his paper bag.

— We're really going to get Isidora's full story.

— Apparently, Lucifer answered, resigned. Brace yourself mentally.

Isidora took a deep breath, a nostalgic smile crossing her face for the first time all day, strangely at odds with her usual nonchalance.

— Okay, so. It all started...

Isidora took a sip of her beer, beginning her tale with the casual enthusiasm of someone telling a vacation anecdote rather than a cosmic origin story.

— So, when I was little, my bitch of a mother one day dared to do something I will never forget as long as I live. SHE DARED TO FORGET MY AFTER-SCHOOL SNACK.

— ...

— So I grabbed the remote and beat her to death with it, she said with a laugh, as if the anecdote were the most hilarious thing in the world.

A deathly silence settled over the counter.

— Then my dad came home and apparently he was sad. But I only figured that out 30 years later. And precisely because he was sad, I beat him to death with the toilet brush. Took me exactly 2 hours 14 minutes 57 seconds and 47 milliseconds.

— ...

Takeshi had completely stopped drinking, his glass hanging halfway to his mouth, his face frozen in an expression of pure horror.

— Then I settled in some backwater village, captured hundreds of kids and did experiments on them, most of them died but hey, none of them came back to complain.

— ...

The silence, already heavy, became absolutely glacial. Even Death, used to this kind of story for millennia, remained strangely still.

— After that, the gods cursed me and I ended up in the Void. But even there, I made jokes, and the Void couldn't stand me, so it merged with me to die. And, well, that's it.

She finished her beer in one gulp, setting the empty glass down with a satisfied little smile, as if she had just told the most ordinary story in the world.

— ...

81 was the first to break the silence, his voice strangely low.

— ...I've killed gods and destroyed Paradise, and right now I feel like the sanest person at this table.

Lucifer, still under his paper bag, stayed silent for a long moment before finally speaking.

— That's why I've been wearing this bag all this time, huh.

— Kinda, yeah, Isidora answered, utterly unaffected by the atmosphere she had just created.

Agent 47, seemingly unfazed, left an unusually long radio silence before speaking again.

— Riper.

"...I have no further comment."

— Nothing at all?

"I believe I have reached the theoretical limit of my emotional processing capacity for today — if I comment, I'm going to give myself the capacity for suicide."

Poppy, who had remained silent since the start of the story, was staring at Isidora with unusual intensity, her neutral expression cracking slightly for the first time.

— ...And nobody ever stopped you after that?

— Well no, why? Isidora answered, sincerely confused by the question, as if the idea had never even crossed her mind.
