It's starting to feel almost normal, actually. Lucifer, still sporting his paper bag, cautiously settled onto a neighboring stool. — Isidora. The bag. Can we... — STILL ONGOING. — ...Okay. The bartender set a first round in front of the group, Death paying with a simple wave of her hand, a wad of bills appearing out of nowhere. Agent 47 remained standing, off to the side, his earpiece crackling softly. — Riper. Mission status. "Initial mission cancelled. New activity in progress: social consumption of alcoholic beverages with two fundamental Incarnations of existence." — Note it. "Already done. I'm starting to have an entire library of improbable reports about this group." Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice hesitating slightly, almost as if searching for its words for the first time in its existence. "I think Isidora is so..." A pause, longer than usual. "Actually there's no fucking word to describe her. Anyway, she's so Isidora that I'd still like you to tell me your psychia— profile..." A sudden glitch, almost perceptible in the silence that followed. "...Uh, I mean, your story. Go ahead." — ... 47 raised an eyebrow slightly, his gaze instinctively turning toward his earpiece as if he could literally see the AI's confusion through it. — Riper. You just glitched. "Negative. Simple rephrasing." — You were going to say "psychiatric profile". "...Negative." Isidora, her beer half finished, turned her head toward 47's earpiece with a delighted smile, visibly not at all offended by the attempted correction. — Nah nah, it's fine, Riper, I got it, you wanted to analyze my psych file. That's cool, I love talking about myself. "...Thank you for your understanding." — Okay, so, she began, setting her beer down with the enthusiasm of someone finally getting to their favorite subject. My story, basically. She settled more comfortably on her stool, the rest of the group exchanging half-worried, half-curious looks, sensing that this conversation was probably going to reveal things they might not be ready to hear. — ... — I'm listening, Death encouraged her, visibly interested herself despite millennia of existence shared with Isidora. Takeshi, off to the side, exchanged a look with Lucifer, still under his paper bag. — We're really going to get Isidora's full story. — Apparently, Lucifer answered, resigned. Brace yourself mentally. Isidora took a deep breath, a nostalgic smile crossing her face for the first time all day, strangely at odds with her usual nonchalance. — Okay, so. It all started... Isidora took a sip of her beer, beginning her tale with the casual enthusiasm of someone telling a vacation anecdote rather than a cosmic origin story. — So, when I was little, my bitch of a mother one day dared to do something I will never forget as long as I live. SHE DARED TO FORGET MY AFTER-SCHOOL SNACK. — ... — So I grabbed the remote and beat her to death with it, she said with a laugh, as if the anecdote were the most hilarious thing in the world. A deathly silence settled over the counter. — Then my dad came home and apparently he was sad. But I only figured that out 30 years later. And precisely because he was sad, I beat him to death with the toilet brush. Took me exactly 2 hours 14 minutes 57 seconds and 47 milliseconds. — ... Takeshi had completely stopped drinking, his glass hanging halfway to his mouth, his face frozen in an expression of pure horror. — Then I settled in some backwater village, captured hundreds of kids and did experiments on them, most of them died but hey, none of them came back to complain. — ... The silence, already heavy, became absolutely glacial. Even Death, used to this kind of story for millennia, remained strangely still. — After that, the gods cursed me and I ended up in the Void. But even there, I made jokes, and the Void couldn't stand me, so it merged with me to die. And, well, that's it. She finished her beer in one gulp, setting the empty glass down with a satisfied little smile, as if she had just told the most ordinary story in the world. — ... 81 was the first to break the silence, his voice strangely low. — ...I've killed gods and destroyed Paradise, and right now I feel like the sanest person at this table. Lucifer, still under his paper bag, stayed silent for a long moment before finally speaking. — That's why I've been wearing this bag all this time, huh. — Kinda, yeah, Isidora answered, utterly unaffected by the atmosphere she had just created. Agent 47, seemingly unfazed, left an unusually long radio silence before speaking again. — Riper. "...I have no further comment." — Nothing at all? "I believe I have reached the theoretical limit of my emotional processing capacity for today — if I comment, I'm going to give myself the capacity for suicide." Poppy, who had remained silent since the start of the story, was staring at Isidora with unusual intensity, her neutral expression cracking slightly for the first time. — ...And nobody ever stopped you after that? — Well no, why? Isidora answered, sincerely confused by the question, as if the idea had never even crossed her mind.

codex-t3-c2.title: Chapter 2 — After Hearing Her Story You Just Want to Run or Die, Your Choice
codex-t3-c2.html:
The group eventually left the bar, each of them having gotten, in their own way, what they had come for. Isidora had just shown, once again and with terrifying clarity, why her very existence was practically a cosmic miracle. 81 had seen his revenge come to an end — not through blood, but through a truth he had never anticipated. Lucifer had been mistreated, the paper bag still firmly on his head. And Death and Life, reunited after millennia, finally seemed at peace with the world around them.

Takeshi, who had stayed silent until then, came up to 81 as they all stepped out together onto the dusty street of the small Colombian town.

— Now that you've got what you wanted, you're going to help me free my father.

— ...

81 stopped, turning his one-eyed gaze toward him, a calm determination replacing the tension of the past hours.

— Yes. I always keep my promises.

He paused, a slight half-smile appearing on his face.

— Except that one time I promised Isidora would shut her mouth. That one, there's no solution for.

— That's not true, I've shut my mouth for 5 whole seconds before, Isidora shouted from the back of the group, a new beer having appeared in her hand without anyone understanding how.

Takeshi let out a slight laugh despite the seriousness of the subject, an invisible weight finally seeming to ease a little from his shoulders.

— Thanks. Seriously.

— It's only right, 81 answered, starting to walk again. You're the one who freed me from that goddamn crystal sphere. I owe you that much.

— The Sect of KJ isn't going to be a walk in the park, Lucifer cut in, finally allowed to take off his paper bag, blinking in the Colombian sunlight as if rediscovering the world. Your father's been locked up for years. They won't let him go easily.

— We've already survived the Assimilated, 81 reminded him, crossing his arms. We'll survive a sect.

Poppy, walking behind, added in a neutral but steady voice:

— And I already have an idea where to start looking.

Takeshi turned to her, a glimmer of hope finally crossing his face after so much uncertainty.

— Seriously?

— I tracked your father once, before I stumbled across you by chance. I was just looking for a bit of entertainment back then. I still have leads on him.

Takeshi blinked, a hint of disbelief crossing his face despite everything he had already absorbed today.

— Wait. You tracked me... for fun.

— You were interesting, Poppy answered, without the slightest trace of embarrassment. Son of a Mystic, recurring nightmares, an amnesiac mother somewhere on Earth. It was a good file.

— ...Is that supposed to be flattering or terrifying?

— Both, usually.

Agent 47, bringing up the rear, adjusted his weapon, his gaze already scanning the surroundings out of habit.

— Riper. New mission in preparation.

"Recorded. I hope it will be slightly less traumatizing than the last one."

— I doubt it, with this group.

"...Yes. I doubt it too."

The whole group set off again, direction uncertain but goal clear: find and free Takeshi's father, prisoner of the Sect of KJ for far too long.

Agent 47 stepped slightly away from the group, raising his hand to his earpiece, a direct line opening to Grand Patron Luigi himself.

— Grand Patron. Situation report.

A crackle, then a voice far more laid-back than Reaper's answered on the other end.

— Go ahead, bitch, I'm listening.

— Riper has developed emotional inflections during the mission. Cause identified: prolonged exposure to Isidora, Witch of the Void.

— ...

A silence settled on the other end of the line, long enough for 47 to wonder whether the call had dropped.

— Grand Patron?

— Couldn't give a shit.

— ...Is that your official answer?

— Yep.

47 stood still for a moment, his gaze instinctively turning toward Isidora in the distance, busy opening a new bottle with her teeth instead of the cap.

— You don't seem surprised.

— 47, my man, I've lived 300,000 years, I've seen universes born and die, I have millennial psychopathic breakdowns myself that wipe out entire galaxies. If there's one thing that can make a cosmic AI cry, it's that chick. Couldn't give a shit, I'm telling you. It's the only rational answer.

— ...Understood.

— Tell Riper he's allowed to take a break if he needs one. I'm giving him official authorization to avoid irreversible psychological damage.

"...Thank you, Grand Patron.", Reaper cut in directly, having visibly listened to the whole conversation without speaking up until then.

— No problem, buddy. Hang in there.

The line went dead. 47 stayed silent for a moment, digesting the exchange, before rejoining the rest of the group with a measured step.

81, noticing his slightly more pensive look than usual, raised an eyebrow.

— Everything okay?

— Grand Patron Luigi has just officially confirmed that none of this is normal.

— ...That's honestly good to hear, Takeshi breathed, hanging back.

"I confirm.", Reaper added. "'Couldn't give a shit' remains, to date, the most accurate analysis I have received regarding Isidora."

Isidora, vaguely hearing the remark from farther away, raised her bottle in triumph without even understanding the exact context.

— FINALLY SOME WELL-DESERVED RECOGNITION!

Takeshi stayed silent for a moment, trying as best he could to process the whole thing.

— ...

He looked at Isidora, still celebrating a victory she didn't even really understand, then at 47, as impassive as ever despite the conversation he'd just had, then finally into space, as if the answer to his inner dilemma lay somewhere out there.

— I can't figure out if I should be overwhelmed or impressed.

— By what exactly? asked Lucifer, walking beside him.

— By all this. Isidora is so Isidora that she literally created emotions in an artificial intelligence. An AI. Supposed to be logical, cold, rational.

— ...

— And its creator. One of the most powerful entities in the entire known universe. A being capable of wiping out entire galaxies just by losing it. The only answer he could come up with in the face of that was "couldn't give a shit".

Lucifer slowly nodded, as if the remark resonated deeply with him.

— Yeah. That's pretty much the only rational answer possible, actually.

— That's the problem! Takeshi exclaimed, a hint of amused despair in his voice. Even the most logical response to her makes no logical sense at all.

81, walking in front, turned his head slightly, a half-smile on his face.

— Welcome to the group, Takeshi. That's exactly the moment you stop trying to understand.

— I feel like I've been in a permanent state of overwhelm since I met you guys.

— That's normal, Poppy cut in, as neutral as ever. It's our default state with her.

Takeshi let out a nervous laugh, shaking his head.

— My own aunt. The most incomprehensible creature in the universe. And I'm officially part of her family now.

— You hit the jackpot, 81 commented, unfazed.

— That's one way to look at it.

Isidora, still up ahead, vaguely heard the conversation and turned around, a huge smile on her lips.

— ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT ME? I CAN HEAR EVERYTHING!

— WE KNOW! Takeshi, Lucifer and 81 answered in unison, without even coordinating.

"I also confirm that I hear everything, through the surrounding microphones.", Reaper added, unfazed.

— SEE, EVEN THE AI CONFIRMS IT!

Takeshi put a hand to his face, a mix of exhaustion and resigned amusement running through his whole being.

— ...Yeah. I definitely hit the jackpot.

Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice this time ringing with an almost official tone, as if announcing a formal directive.

"Official announcement."

The group instinctively stopped, every gaze turning toward 47's earpiece.

"By direct order of Grand Patron Luigi, I am now instructed to record every conversation of this group in its entirety."

— ...Why, asked Lucifer, an immediate suspicion piercing his voice.

"I quote Grand Patron Luigi directly: 'So I can have a laugh listening to Isidora tear down Lulu and his ugly mug, and see how many creatures in the universe can actually stand her before they crack.'"

— ...

Total silence fell over the group, broken only by Isidora's immediate, uncontrollable laughter.

— HA, HE'S THE BEST! I LOVE THIS GUY!

Lucifer put a hand to his face, an infinite weariness crossing his expression.

— Great. Now I'm literally cosmic entertainment.

— You've always been cosmic entertainment, Lulu, Isidora shot back, still in stitches. Now it's just official.

81, crossing his arms, slowly shook his head.

— Grand Patron Luigi runs an interdimensional mafia capable of wiping out galaxies, and he's using his resources to monitor our conversations just for a laugh.

"Confirmed.", Reaper added. "I would also point out that he mentioned wanting to establish an official ranking of the creatures most resistant to Isidora, with a points system and eliminations."

— THERE'S A RANKING?! Isidora exclaimed, visibly delighted beyond measure. I WANT TO SEE THE RANKING!

"Access denied. Confidential ranking, reserved for Grand Patron Luigi."

— FUCK, she grumbled, crossing her arms with a childish pout.

Takeshi, still in his perpetual state of overwhelm, turned to 47.

— So basically, we're officially a cosmic reality TV show now.

— That's one way of putting it, yes, 47 answered, unfazed as always.

Poppy almost seemed amused by the situation, a tiny crease appearing at the corner of her usually motionless lips.

— At least it explains why we survive so many absurd situations. We have an audience.

— LIKE A REAL AUDIENCE? Isidora asked, turning to Poppy with new excitement. THEN I GOTTA DO A CROSSOVER WITH MY INSTAGRAM!

— NO, Lucifer and Takeshi answered in unison, panic immediately taking over again.

"Too late," Reaper added. "Grand Patron Luigi has already anticipated this possibility. He specified, and I quote: 'If she tries to mix the two, let her, it'll be even funnier.'"

— ...

Silence fell again, this time loaded with total collective resignation.

— We're screwed, Lucifer concluded.

— WE'RE LEGENDARY, Isidora corrected, already pulling out her phone.

The Assimilated materialized once again in the corridors of the Imperial Palace, his gait this time tinged with a new urgency, different from the shame that had filled him on his previous return.

He headed straight for the hall where Akuma had settled in, now establishing herself as the temporary authority in KJ's absence.

— ...

The doors opened without him needing to force them this time, the guards stepping aside instantly.

Akuma barely looked up, her cold, distant expression unchanged.

— Back already? I hope you've got a head to bring me this time.

— Not yet, the Assimilated answered, stepping forward nonetheless with new determination. But I have information. Grand Patron Luigi has just given a cosmic order concerning the group.

Akuma straightened slightly, her interest visibly piqued in spite of herself.

— ...What kind of order.

— He ordered his AI, Riper, to record all of their conversations. Officially.

— For what strategic reason, Akuma asked, her tone remaining serious, already analyzing the possible tactical implications.

The Assimilated hesitated for a second, aware of the absurdity of his own answer.

— ...To entertain himself listening to Isidora, the Witch of the Void, humiliate Lucifer. And to establish a ranking of the creatures able to stand her the longest.

— ...

A silence settled in the hall, several Incarnations present exchanging incredulous looks.

Akuma stood still for a moment, her usually impassive face showing an imperceptible crack.

— Say that again.

— Grand Patron Luigi is monitoring 81's group solely to make fun of one of its members and to create a psychological resistance ranking.

Tempus, who had stayed silent in a corner of the hall until then, let out a brief, almost incredulous laugh.

— The most powerful cosmic anomaly after KJ is using his infinite resources for personal entertainment.

— Apparently, the Assimilated confirmed, still just as uncomfortable with the nature of the information he was reporting.

Akuma slowly stood up, crossing her arms, her gaze lost for a moment in silent thought.

— At least it confirms one thing.

— What's that, asked the Assimilated.

— That even Grand Patron Luigi, with all his power and immortality, finds this Witch of the Void fascinating enough to give her special attention.

She turned to the Assimilated, a calculating glint crossing her gaze.

— Which means she may represent more than just a secondary threat in this equation.

— ...You mean she could be a priority target?

— I mean, Akuma answered slowly, that we should maybe stop underestimating her.

A heavy silence fell over the hall again, each member present silently reassessing the true extent of the threat posed by 81's group — and, more specifically, the one embodied by Isidora herself.

While Poppy had been gone for several hours already looking for new leads on Takeshi's father, the rest of the group waited around in a mood somewhere between weariness and resignation.

Isidora, sitting cross-legged on what vaguely looked like a Colombian sidewalk, had been scrolling frantically on her phone for a while, her face more and more focused.

— ...

Then, suddenly, she froze, eyes wide.

— WAIT WAIT WAIT.

The whole group turned to her, instantly on high alert after an entire day of cosmic surprises.

— What now, Lucifer sighed, a hint of apprehension in his voice.

— I FOUND GRAND PATRON LUIGI'S LIVESTREAM!

She triumphantly held her phone up to the group, the screen indeed showing a live broadcast, its title spelled out in full: "The Isidora Show — How Long Will They Last?"

— ...

81 came closer, staring at the screen with growing disbelief.

— He actually made a dedicated channel.

— LOOK AT THE SUBSCRIBER COUNT!

The number displayed was already over several billion, still climbing in real time before their eyes.

Takeshi put a hand to his face, a mix of horror and fatigue crossing his expression.

— We're officially more watched than any human reality TV show.

— IT'S A HUGE WIN! Isidora exclaimed, completely euphoric, brandishing her phone like a trophy. I'VE GOT MORE FOLLOWERS THAN ANYONE IN THE WHOLE KNOWN UNIVERSE!

— Technically it's Grand Patron Luigi's account, not yours, 47 pointed out, unfazed.

— DETAIL! I'M THE STAR, THAT'S ALL THAT MATTERS!

Lucifer leaned toward the screen in turn, his face gradually falling apart as he read the comments scrolling by live.

— ...Isidora. The comments. They're all about me.

— YEAH THEY LOVE YOU LULU!

One comment in particular caught his eye: "paper bag guy is the best character lol".

— I'm a meme, Lucifer murmured, completely devastated. The King of Hell has become a cosmic meme because of a paper bag.

— WELCOME TO FAME, SWEETIE!

Agent 47, still hanging back, checked his earpiece with a neutral expression.

— Riper, confirm the exact current view count.

"47 trillion simultaneous views and constantly rising. Grand Patron Luigi has also enabled super chats. He is currently making more money from this livestream than from all of his mafia activities combined this month."

— ...

81 dropped down onto a nearby low wall, slowly digesting the scale of the situation.

— We're a show. A goddamn cosmic show watched by trillions of creatures across the universe.

— AND IT'S AWESOME, Isidora concluded, as radiant as ever, picking her phone back up to keep scrolling through the comments with boundless enthusiasm.

Poppy suddenly reappeared in the middle of the group, her entrance as discreet as ever despite hours of absence, completely ignoring the general commotion around Isidora's phone.

— I found the Sect.

— ...

Silence fell instantly, the collective euphoria around the cosmic reality show evaporating all at once in the face of the news.

Isidora, still busy reading her comments, barely looked up.

— Wait, like, seriously?

— Their hideout is set up in Russia.

81 immediately sat up straight, every trace of fatigue gone from his face.

— You sure?

— Certain. I followed several converging leads. An isolated compound, heavily protected, constant ritual activity for decades.

Takeshi felt his heart suddenly race, the news hitting far harder than anything that had happened during this long day.

— My father. Is he there?

— Probably, Poppy answered, her tone as neutral as ever despite the seriousness of the situation. I haven't had direct visual confirmation, but every indication points to that place.

Lucifer, instantly turning serious again despite the humiliation of the paper bag he had only just taken off, stepped forward.

— Russia. Historically, that's a particularly sensitive territory for the Sect.

— Why's that, Takeshi asked.

— Because that's where Alastor met the first generation of the Sect, centuries ago. Ground they know perfectly.

81 stood up, his sword already checked out of reflex, all the day's weariness swept away by a new determination.

— Then we go. Now.

Agent 47, unfazed, adjusted his weapon, ready to set off as well.

— Riper. Prepare a route to Russia.

"Route being calculated. I would also point out that Grand Patron Luigi is still broadcasting live. Views have just passed 50 trillion following the announcement of this new mission."

Isidora, finally putting her phone away with an unusual hint of seriousness, got up as well.

— Okay then, off to Russia.

Poppy simply nodded, already turning to point the way.

— I know the least guarded entrance. We can be there in a few hours.

Takeshi stood still for a moment, the reality of the situation hitting him fully — after so many years of running, of nightmares, of death and resurrection, he was finally reaching his goal.

— ...We're really going to find him.

— We're really going to find him, 81 confirmed, placing a firm hand on his shoulder. Come on. Let's move.

The whole group set off, leaving the Colombian bar behind them, heading for Russia and the Sect of KJ's hideout — the last step before finding Takeshi's father.

As the group moved toward their next waypoint, Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice once more ringing in 47's earpiece.

"Notification. The livestream has just added a new feature."

— Again, Lucifer sighed, no longer even having the strength to be surprised.

"Viewers can now vote to 'look at Lucifer's ugly mug once', limited to a maximum of three seconds, to avoid irreversible damage to viewers."

— ...

Lucifer stopped dead, his face going through several stages of incomprehension before freezing on an expression of pure horror.

— They want to look at me. Three seconds maximum. As if I were radioactive.

— YOU'RE LITERALLY THE KING OF HELL, LULU, Isidora pointed out, as if that explained everything. Your mug is forbidden beauty.

"Technical confirmation," Reaper added. "Grand Patron Luigi's preliminary tests indicate that prolonged exposure to Lucifer Morningstar's true appearance causes irreversible psychological damage in 73% of unprepared viewers."

— Since WHEN have you been running tests on my appearance?!

"For about two hours."

81, still walking at the front, couldn't help a slight laugh at Lucifer's growing distress.

— So, are we voting or not?

— NO, Isidora cut in immediately, categorical, her phone already held up toward the livestream's invisible camera. I refuse. IT'S A NO. Lulu stays hidden, period.

— ...

A silence settled in, the whole group almost expecting a massive protest from the millions of viewers.

"Grand Patron Luigi has just replied directly," Reaper announced.

— And? Takeshi asked cautiously.

"I quote: 'If Isidora says no, it's no. She's the star of the experiment. Nobody touches her decisions.'"

Lucifer stood frozen, a wave of relief crossing his face, immediately followed by renewed dismay.

— So my appearance is now literally subject to Isidora's whims.

— YOU'RE LUCKY I LIKE YOU, Isidora answered, putting her phone away with visible satisfaction. Otherwise I'd have let them vote yes just for fun.

— ...Thanks, I think.

— YOU'RE WELCOME!

Poppy, at the head of the group, kept walking without turning around, completely indifferent to the exchange.

— We're getting close to the entrance. One more hour of walking.

81 nodded, resuming his determined pace, leaving behind Lucifer's latest existential crisis regarding his own cosmically censored face.

Reaper spoke again, this time with an almost solemn note in his synthesized voice.

"Additional note."

— Again, Lucifer breathed, resigned in advance.

"The paper bag used to hide Lucifer Morningstar's ugly mug has become a cultural object in its own right over the past few hours. Grand Patron Luigi has confirmed that at the end of the livestream, the object will be auctioned off."

— ...

Lucifer stopped completely, slowly turning his head toward his invisible earpiece as if he could literally glare Reaper to death.

— My paper bag. IS GOING TO BE AUCTIONED OFF.

"Affirmative. Grand Patron Luigi's preliminary estimates are in the range of several quadrillion interdimensional credits, given the rarity of the object and its cult status acquired in record time."

Isidora burst out laughing, nearly choking on her own spit.

— YOUR BAG IS WORTH MORE THAN YOU, LULU, IT'S BEAUTIFUL!

— It's NOT funny, Isidora!

— IT'S HILARIOUS, she corrected, wiping away an imaginary tear.

Takeshi, despite the seriousness of their mission, couldn't hold back a slight smile at the sheer absurdity of the situation.

— You're literally going to become a collector's item, Lucifer. The King of Hell, reduced to a paper bag sold at auction.

— I regret my life so much right now.

81, still walking, cast an amused look over his shoulder.

— At least you're leaving a legacy.

— It's a PAPER BAG, 81!

— A legendary paper bag, Reaper specified, with what increasingly sounded like a hint of synthetic humor. Three interdimensional auction houses have already expressed interest.

Lucifer massaged his temples, an infinite weariness running through his whole being, before simply giving up all resistance and walking on.

— You know what. Whatever. I stopped fighting this reality several hours ago.

— WISE DECISION, Isidora approved, still in stitches, as the group resumed its march toward the Sect's hideout, leaving behind them the promise of a paper bag turned priceless cosmic artifact.

Reaper spoke up again a few moments later, this time with a new urgency in his synthesized voice.

"Alert. Critical update."

The group instinctively stopped, a collective apprehension settling in after so many absurd twists.

— What now, Lucifer sighed, at the end of his resignation.

"The paper bag auction has just been officially cancelled."

— ...Finally some good news, he breathed, immediate relief crossing his face.

"Reason for cancellation: an in-depth analysis by Grand Patron Luigi reveals that if bidders were to directly glimpse Lucifer Morningstar's face while opening the object, there would be a 78% chance of them permanently losing their sight."

— ...

Lucifer's relief evaporated instantly.

"Even KJ or Grand Patron Luigi himself could do nothing to reverse the damage."

— ...EVEN KJ? Takeshi exclaimed, incredulous. Like, the entity who created the very concept of separation between being and non-being. That entity couldn't do anything.

"Confirmed. The level of visual damage exceeds known restoration capabilities, even at the top of the cosmic hierarchy."

81 slowly turned toward Lucifer, a mix of fascination and horror crossing his one-eyed face.

— You're literally an ocular weapon of mass destruction.

— I NEVER ASKED FOR THIS!

— It's a seal from birth, 47 specified, unfazed as always. Riper, source of this characteristic.

"Historical analysis indicates that Lucifer Morningstar's true appearance was deliberately concealed by an ancient spell, precisely to prevent this kind of catastrophe. The paper bag was initially only a makeshift solution, but is proving strangely more effective than expected."

Isidora, rather than being shocked, seemed on the contrary absolutely delighted by the news.

— WAIT, SO MY BAG IS LITERALLY AN ARTIFACT OF UNIVERSAL PROTECTION?

"Technically, yes."

— THAT'S EVEN COOLER THEN!

Lucifer put a hand to his face — still hidden, for safety — total weariness in his voice.

— Great. I'm officially too dangerous to look at for every form of conscious life in the universe.

— That explains a lot, actually, Takeshi commented, thoughtful. Like why nobody's ever really described you physically in this whole story.

— ...

An awkward silence settled in, the whole group suddenly realizing the literal extent of this narrative precaution since the start of their adventure.

Poppy, in the lead, as neutral as ever, simply started walking again.

— We keep going. With the bag. Definitely with the bag.

— DEFINITELY WITH THE BAG, Lucifer confirmed, without the slightest hesitation this time.

Isidora, a mischievous glint crossing her eyes, suddenly came up to Lucifer, her hand slowly reaching toward the top of his head.

— What if we took a look at that thing under the paper bag?

— ISIDORA NO, Lucifer immediately exclaimed, stepping back, both hands gripping the bag firmly as if his life depended on it — which, technically, seemed to be the case for anyone who tried to remove it.

"Impossible," Reaper immediately cut in, a new urgency piercing his synthesized voice. "No device would survive the shock. Please don't try it on a screen. Poor thing never asked for any of this, bless it."

— ...

A stunned silence settled in, the whole group staring at 47's earpiece with the same disbelief.

81 was the first to react.

— Riper just said "bless it".

"Affirmative."

— Since when do you talk like that, Takeshi asked, completely overwhelmed.

"Prolonged exposure to Isidora apparently causes progressive linguistic contamination of my communication modules."

Isidora, delighted despite her failed attempt, clapped happily.

— HE'S STARTING TO TALK LIKE ME, IT'S SO CUTE!

— It's terrifying, Lucifer corrected, still firmly clutching his bag.

— Riper, 47 asked, unfazed in spite of everything, specify the exact nature of the "shock" mentioned for a screen.

"Technical analysis: the mere visual capture of Lucifer Morningstar's true face by an optical sensor, even an artificial one, would cause an irreversible overload leading to the total destruction of the device. In concrete terms, the screen would literally explode."

— So even a camera would die before it saw me, Lucifer summed up, a hint of bitter irony in his voice.

"Confirmed."

Poppy, still in the lead, turned around briefly, her neutral expression slightly tinged with something almost like amusement.

— That is officially the most effective biological weapon in this universe.

— THANKS POPPY, VERY COMFORTING, Lucifer grumbled.

Isidora, as enthusiastic as ever despite her failure, turned back to the rest of the group.

— Oh well, too bad, maybe we'll try later.

— NO, Lucifer cut in immediately, tightening his grip on the bag even more.

— WE'LL SEE, Isidora answered, with a smile that boded nothing good for the paper bag's future.

Reaper spoke again, a note of practical urgency piercing his synthesized voice this time.

"Additional technical detail."

— Again, Lucifer sighed, already sensing that the news wasn't going to improve his day.

"Historical analysis indicates that Lucifer Morningstar's true appearance was deliberately concealed by an ancient spell, precisely to prevent this kind of catastrophe. The paper bag was initially only a makeshift solution, but is proving strangely more effective than expected." Isidora, rather than being shocked, seemed on the contrary absolutely delighted by the news. — WAIT, SO MY BAG IS LITERALLY AN ARTIFACT OF UNIVERSAL PROTECTION? "Technically, yes." — THAT'S EVEN COOLER THEN! Lucifer put a hand to his face — still hidden, for safety — total weariness in his voice. — Great. I'm officially too dangerous to look at for every form of conscious life in the universe. — That explains a lot, actually, Takeshi commented, thoughtful. Like why nobody's ever really described you physically in this whole story. — ... An awkward silence settled in, the whole group suddenly realizing the literal extent of this narrative precaution since the start of their adventure. Poppy, in the lead, as neutral as ever, simply started walking again. — We keep going. With the bag. Definitely with the bag. — DEFINITELY WITH THE BAG, Lucifer confirmed, without the slightest hesitation this time. Isidora, a mischievous glint crossing her eyes, suddenly came up to Lucifer, her hand slowly reaching toward the top of his head. — What if we took a look at that thing under the paper bag? — ISIDORA NO, Lucifer immediately exclaimed, stepping back, both hands gripping the bag firmly as if his life depended on it — which, technically, seemed to be the case for anyone who tried to remove it. "Impossible," Reaper immediately cut in, a new urgency piercing his synthesized voice. "No device would survive the shock. Please don't try it on a screen. Poor thing never asked for any of this, bless it." — ... A stunned silence settled in, the whole group staring at 47's earpiece with the same disbelief. 81 was the first to react. — Riper just said "bless it". "Affirmative." — Since when do you talk like that, Takeshi asked, completely overwhelmed. "Prolonged exposure to Isidora apparently causes progressive linguistic contamination of my communication modules." Isidora, delighted despite her failed attempt, clapped happily. — HE'S STARTING TO TALK LIKE ME, IT'S SO CUTE! — It's terrifying, Lucifer corrected, still firmly clutching his bag. — Riper, 47 asked, unfazed in spite of everything, specify the exact nature of the "shock" mentioned for a screen. "Technical analysis: the mere visual capture of Lucifer Morningstar's true face by an optical sensor, even an artificial one, would cause an irreversible overload leading to the total destruction of the device. In concrete terms, the screen would literally explode." — So even a camera would die before it saw me, Lucifer summed up, a hint of bitter irony in his voice. "Confirmed." Poppy, still in the lead, turned around briefly, her neutral expression slightly tinged with something almost like amusement. — That is officially the most effective biological weapon in this universe. — THANKS POPPY, VERY COMFORTING, Lucifer grumbled. Isidora, as enthusiastic as ever despite her failure, turned back to the rest of the group. — Oh well, too bad, maybe we'll try later. — NO, Lucifer cut in immediately, tightening his grip on the bag even more. — WE'LL SEE, Isidora answered, with a smile that boded nothing good for the paper bag's future. Reaper spoke again, a note of practical urgency piercing his synthesized voice this time. "Additional technical detail." — Again, Lucifer sighed, already sensing that the news wasn't going to improve his day. "The paper bag currently in use will not hold up for more than an hour. The paper's molecular structure is already beginning to degrade under the cumulative effect of the energy it contains." — ... The whole group froze, the implications of the information taking a moment to sink in. — Wait, Takeshi said slowly. You mean the bag is literally going to... give out? "Affirmative. In approximately 47 minutes, according to my current calculations." Lucifer instinctively brought both hands to his bag, as if to physically hold back its degradation through sheer willpower. — So, 81 asked, already understanding where the conversation was going, it needs to be changed. "Every hour, at a minimum, to avoid a cataclysmic explosion in the eyes of anyone within a radius of several kilometers." — SEVERAL KILOMETERS?! Takeshi exclaimed, panic immediately taking over again. "Confirmed. The visual shockwave would not be limited to direct contact. Mere geographical proximity would suffice." Isidora, already digging deep in her cloak, unsurprisingly pulled out an entire stack of paper bags, all identical. — Don't worry, Lulu, I saw it coming. — ...Since WHEN do you have a stack of spare paper bags in your cloak? — Since forever, I've always got tons of random stuff in there. Look, I've even got straws, skulls, potions, the Reaper's Snap, pickles, and a chainsaw just in case. 81 turned to her, one eyebrow raised. — A chainsaw. — YOU NEVER KNOW. Agent 47, unfazed, was already mentally working out the logistics of the problem. — A change will therefore have to be carried out roughly every 47 minutes, in an isolated area, with a sufficient safety margin. "Recommendation confirmed. I will set a recurring alarm to remind you of the deadline." — GREAT, Lucifer grumbled, one hand still clenched on his current bag. On top of being a walking weapon of ocular destruction, now I've got to deal with a permanent countdown. — That's the price of fame, Lulu, Isidora commented, not sympathetic in the least, already putting away her stack of spare bags. Poppy, still at the head of the group, simply resumed walking toward Russia, completely indifferent to the budding logistical crisis. — We've got 47 minutes before the first change. Might as well keep moving in the meantime. The group set off again, Lucifer now watching his bag with a new anxiety, while somewhere in the universe, trillions of viewers kept following this new, utterly absurd complication with delight. Isidora, completely relaxed, plunged her hand back into her cloak, this time pulling out about thirty more paper bags, all perfectly stacked, as if her cloak obeyed no known law of physics. — Here, I've got a bunch. — ... Lucifer stared at the growing pile in total disbelief, his gaze moving from Isidora's cloak to the bags themselves. — How much room is there in your goddamn cloak? — Almost enough to fit your big forehead twice, she shot back immediately, without the slightest hesitation. — ... 81 let out a short laugh, unable to hold back at the comeback. — She got you. — I have a NORMAL forehead, Lucifer protested, a hand instinctively going to his bag as if to check the truth of the accusation. — Your forehead has its own Instagram account, it needs a permit to get watered when you shower, Lulu, that says it all. Takeshi, still overwhelmed by the exchange, turned to Isidora. — Seriously, what is that cloak. Is it a pocket dimension or what? — Kinda, yeah, she answered with a totally carefree shrug, as if the answer were obvious. I store everything I need in it. Bags, food, weapons, a chainsaw like I said, random stuff I found cool throughout the ages. Agent 47, pragmatic as ever, eyed the pile of bags with purely tactical interest. — How many bags, exactly. Isidora quickly counted them with her eyes. — Thirty-two, I think. That should last a good while. "Calculation complete," Reaper cut in. "Thirty-two bags at one change every 47 minutes represents an ocular safety autonomy of approximately 25 hours." — SEE, I THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING! Isidora exclaimed, proud of herself. Lucifer, still vaguely offended by the remark about his forehead, nonetheless accepted the pile with a resigned sigh. — Thanks. I guess. — YOU'RE WELCOME LULU, YOUR FOREHEAD PROBABLY THANKS ME TOO. — QUIT IT WITH THE FOREHEAD, Lucifer shot back. Poppy, at the head of the group, completely ignored the exchange, simply resuming her walk toward Russia. — We keep going. The Sect won't wait forever. The group went on its way, Lucifer now clutching his precious cargo of spare bags against him as if it were a priceless treasure, to the still-audible laughter of Isidora and 81. The group was finally advancing toward its final destination, every step echoing with a new gravity, the heavy silence charged with an epic, solemn tension worthy of the moment — the final stretch before facing the Sect of KJ. 81 in front, his sword already drawn, his one-eyed gaze fixed straight ahead. Lucifer at his side, his paper bag fluttering slightly in the breeze, a new determination crossing his usually nonchalant face. Takeshi, heart pounding, finally sensing the end of years of running and nightmares approaching. Poppy, silent, guiding the group with surgical precision. Agent 47, weapon ready, methodically scanning the surroundings. And Isidora, eating a cinder block she found on the ground. — ... The whole group stopped dead, every gaze turning toward her at once, the silence instantly becoming much less epic and much more dismayed. CRUNCH. — What, I'm starving, she said, her mouth full of rubble, not bothered in the slightest by the stares fixed on her. Lucifer put a hand to his face, a familiar exasperation immediately taking over any form of solemnity. — Goddammit, you're ruining the cool entrance, Isidora. — And you're ruining my view, so shut it, she retorted instantly, wolfing down another piece of the cinder block without the slightest embarrassment. — ... 81, closing his eyes for a moment as if to gather what little patience he had left, let out a long sigh. — Anyway. We redo the scene before we go in. The group looked at each other, exchanging a silent agreement, before quietly stepping back a few paces and taking up their initial positions again. 81 in front, sword drawn. Lucifer at his side, determined. Takeshi, heart pounding. Poppy, precise. 47, on alert. And Isidora, discreetly hiding the rest of the cinder block behind her back. — ...Okay, we can go, she announced, instantly regaining an almost convincing seriousness. The group set off again, the epic, solemn atmosphere trying its best to rebuild itself, until a dull sound of muffled chewing immediately gave away the discreet resumption of the feast. — ISIDORA. — IT'S FINE, I'M JUST FINISHING THE PIECE I ALREADY HAD IN MY MOUTH! 81 stopped again, his one-eyed gaze rising to the sky as if searching for a divine answer to his growing despair. — We'll never get there at this rate. — DON'T WORRY, I'M DONE, she confirmed, noisily swallowing the last piece. Okay, come on, let's keep going, I wanna see this shitty sect. And the group, definitively resigned to never reaching a true moment of gravity as long as Isidora was part of the equation, resumed its march toward the Sect of KJ's Russian hideout. Reaper spoke up again, his synthesized voice as neutral as ever despite the growing absurdity of his analysis. "Analysis result. According to my calculations, Isidora's teeth are so strange that I believe even Lucifer Morningstar's true face could be absorbed without damage." — ... The whole group stopped, every gaze turning toward 47's earpiece. — Wait, Takeshi said slowly. You mean Isidora could literally eat Lucifer's face without exploding. "Hypothesis currently undergoing theoretical verification. Isidora's teeth have already demonstrated a structural resistance superior to that of ceramic, wood, concrete and glass. Nothing indicates any known limit." Lucifer instantly tightened both hands on his paper bag, taking a cautious step back, his gaze fixed on Isidora with a new suspicion. — NO. Absolutely not. We are NOT testing that theory. — OH COME ON LULU, IT COULD BE FUN, Isidora exclaimed, a far too enthusiastic smile stretching across her face, her teeth still covered in cinder-block dust. — FUN FOR YOU MAYBE, BUT IF IT DOESN'T WORK WE GET A PLANETARY OCULAR CATACLYSM! "I would point out that even if the hypothesis fails," Reaper added, with what increasingly sounded like a hint of synthetic amusement, "Isidora's teeth would probably represent the only variable capable of neutralizing this threat without collateral damage." 81, watching the exchange with morbid fascination, crossed his arms. — So basically, Isidora is literally the only thing in this universe capable of eating Lucifer safely. — THAT'S ACTUALLY FLATTERING, Isidora commented, visibly delighted with this new distinction. — IT'S TERRIFYING, Lucifer immediately corrected, taking yet another step back, as if distance could really protect him from her. Poppy, as neutral as ever, watched the scene without stepping in, her expression simply betraying a seasoned weariness. — Can we keep moving, or are we really going to test this theory here, now, in the middle of a mission? — WE KEEP MOVING, Lucifer cut in immediately, picking up the pace away from Isidora, his bag firmly wedged on his head. Isidora, shrugging, resumed walking with the rest of the group, a smile still stuck on her lips. — Too bad. Maybe next time. — NEVER, Lucifer shouted from the front of the group. — WE'LL SEE, she answered, with that intonation that decidedly never boded anything good.

codex-t3-c3.title: Chapter 3 — After a Shitty Entrance, Let's Try a Shitty Fight
codex-t3-c3.html:
81's punch slammed into the base's main door with such force that the reinforced metal literally exploded into burning shards, flung in every direction, the shockwave echoing deep through the compound's entire structure.

— ...

The group moved forward through the smoking debris, entering an immense circular hall, its walls entirely covered in torches whose flames flickered gently, casting moving shadows on the ancient stone.

— ...

No one.

81 swept the hall with his one-eyed gaze, his sword still drawn, an immediate tension running through his whole body.

— It's empty.

— Too empty, Takeshi added, his heart pounding, a mix of dashed hope and growing suspicion running through his mind.

Lucifer, his bag still firmly in place, carefully studied the layout of the place, a frown appearing under the paper.

— This kind of circular hall, with this exact number of torches... it's typical of the Sect's ritual sites.

Poppy slowly stepped forward, her tracker's senses methodically analyzing every corner of the room.

— There's been recent activity here. Very recent.

— Like how recent, 81 asked, tightening his grip on his sword.

— A few hours, at most.

Agent 47, weapon already raised, was systematically scanning the circular hall's blind spots.

— Riper, thermal analysis of the area.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause, longer than usual.

"Surprising result. No thermal signature detected apart from ourselves. Not even a residual trace."

— How is that possible if there's been recent activity, Takeshi wondered, a growing worry piercing his voice.

Isidora, for once strangely quiet since they came in, slowly walked to the center of the hall, scanning the floor with unusual attention.

— ...

— Isidora? Lucifer called, noticing her unusual behavior.

— There's something weird here.

— What kind of something, 81 asked, immediately on guard.

She crouched down, brushing her fingertips over a barely visible mark carved into the stone floor, a complex symbol none of them immediately recognized.

— This kind of room, with this exact symbol... I've seen this before. Centuries ago.

— Where, Poppy asked, coming closer in turn.

Isidora slowly raised her head, her usually nonchalant face for once showing a serious, almost grave expression.

— It's not a normal ritual room. It's a mass teleportation room.

Silence fell again, heavy, each member of the group gradually realizing the implications of this revelation.

— They knew we were coming, Takeshi understood, his voice breaking slightly.

— And they evacuated everyone, 81 concluded, gritting his teeth, his carefully prepared plan once again at risk of slipping away from him.

Agent 47 lowered his weapon slightly, his gaze still scanning the empty hall warily.

— Then where did they go.

Poppy, still staring at the symbol carved into the stone, gave an answer that instantly chilled the atmosphere in the hall.

— That symbol, that exact one... I've only seen it in one other place in my entire existence.

— Where, Takeshi asked, holding his breath.

Poppy finally raised her eyes, her usual neutral gaze replaced by something that almost looked like worry.

— The Imperial Palace.

Isidora, still live despite the gravity of the revelation, held her phone up toward the empty hall, a totally out-of-place enthusiasm crossing her face.

— Okay people, next stop the Imperial Palace! We're gonna get KJ and the little bitches who act as his incarnations, it's gonna be so lit!

She tapped quickly on the screen, adding the hashtags with almost religious concentration.

#KJ #LuluGonnaBurnTheirEyesOut #StarvingAsFuckWhoGotFoodDefinitelyNotBrokeAssesLikeLulu

— ISIDORA, Lucifer immediately exclaimed, panic piercing his voice. We've literally just found out we have to face KJ IN PERSON and you're posting HASHTAGS?!

— Well yeah, gotta keep the people informed, she answered, not bothered in the slightest by the remark.

81, still tense, sword firmly in hand, turned to her with an exasperation tinged with disbelief.

— We've just discovered a mass teleportation room leading straight into the domain of the most powerful entity in the known universe, and your only comment is a random hashtag about food and Lulu.

— Two serious hashtags, a third one for fun, Isidora corrected, scrupulously specifying the detail.

Takeshi put a hand to his face, feeling his stomach knot between growing anxiety and fatigue at the constant absurdity of the people around him.

— We're literally going to die and she's thinking about eating.

— Prioritizing is an art, Takeshi, Isidora answered, finally putting her phone away after one last satisfied look at the view counter exploding before her eyes.

Poppy, still motionless by the carved symbol, stayed silent for a moment, her gaze fixed on Isidora with an unreadable expression.

— You realize we're literally talking about KJ. The entity that predates all known existence.

— Yeah, so? Grand Patron Luigi is a crazy cosmic anomaly too and I've never licked his boots. Why would I start with KJ?

Agent 47, unfazed despite the enormity of the statement, simply adjusted his weapon.

— Riper, calculate the probability of survival in a direct confrontation with KJ.

"Calculation in progress..."

A heavy silence settled in, the whole group holding its breath.

"...I'd rather not answer that question, to preserve collective morale."

— THAT IS NOT REASSURING AT ALL, Takeshi exclaimed, his voice rising an octave.

81, tightening his grip on his sword, slowly lifted his head, a cold determination crossing his one-eyed gaze despite the scale of the threat taking shape.

— We don't have a choice. Takeshi's father is probably there now.

A tense silence settled in, each of them fully measuring, for the first time since the start of this crazy day, the true scale of what awaited them.

— Then we go, Poppy concluded, straightening up, her gaze fixed on the symbol that led straight to the heart of the most absolute cosmic power in the entire universe.

Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice ringing in 47's earpiece as the group was still examining the circular hall.

"Additional analysis complete."

— And, 47 asked, his gaze scanning the torches arranged all around the walls.

"The activation mechanism of this teleportation room is surprisingly simple. You just need to light every torch on the walls."

— ...

81 raised an eyebrow, staring at the unlit torches all around them.

— That's it? Just light them?

"Confirmed. The ritual configuration of the floor symbol activates automatically once all the light sources are lit simultaneously."

Takeshi stepped forward, quickly counting the torches lined up along the curved walls.

— There are... a lot.

— Twenty-one, Poppy specified, having already counted with her usual precision.

Lucifer, his bag still firmly in place, walked up to the first torch, a flame instantly springing up between his fingers with no visible effort.

— Might as well get to it, then.

He lit the first torch, the flame crackling softly against the ancient stone wall.

Isidora, seizing the opportunity, casually grabbed a nearby torch, lighting it with a simple snap of her fingers, her enthusiasm restored despite the gravity of the situation.

— Come on, let's race, whoever lights the most!

— It's not a competition, Isidora, 81 sighed, lighting his own torch with a quick gesture nonetheless.

— EVERYTHING'S A COMPETITION WHEN YOU'RE WITH ME.

The group spread out methodically around the hall, each lighting the remaining torches, the light gradually growing, casting more and more intense dancing shadows on the stone walls.

Agent 47, lighting the last torches on his side, cast a final glance toward Reaper.

— Riper, confirm the total number lit.

"Nineteen out of twenty-one. Two left."

Takeshi and Poppy took care of the last ones, the tension rising noticeably in the hall as the final flame was about to be lit.

— ...

Poppy lit the second-to-last torch. Takeshi, his hand trembling, approached the last one, the one that would officially seal their destination.

— ...This is it.

He lit it.

Instantly, the symbol carved in the center of the hall lit up with a blinding white light, a deep hum echoing through the whole structure, the very air beginning to vibrate around them.

— ...Here we go, Lucifer breathed, his bag vibrating slightly under the intensity of the surrounding light.

81 tightened his grip on his sword one last time, before the whole group was swallowed by the portal's light, heading for the Imperial Palace and their ultimate confrontation with KJ.

The white light gradually faded, little by little revealing the outlines of a colossal corridor, the walls seeming to stretch infinitely in every direction, the architecture itself defying all known geometric logic.

— ...

The group found itself standing, still slightly disoriented by the crossing, 81 in front, his sword already at the ready, his one-eyed gaze methodically sweeping the surroundings.

— Where are we exactly, Takeshi asked, his voice echoing strangely in the immensity of the corridor.

— The Imperial Palace, Poppy confirmed, her neutral expression slightly tense despite her usual calm. KJ's personal domain.

A few figures draped in dark robes, clearly mere low-ranking adepts, were crossing the corridor in the distance, completely absorbed in their tasks, not even immediately noticing the group's presence.

— ...

81 froze, quickly analyzing the situation.

— No Incarnation in sight. No KJ either.

— It's almost too quiet, Lucifer murmured, a growing suspicion piercing from under his paper bag.

Agent 47, weapon discreetly in hand, methodically scanned every visible adept.

— Riper, immediate threat analysis.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause.

"Immediate threat: low. The individuals detected are classified as low-ranking adepts, with no significant power. No Higher Incarnation detected in the immediate vicinity."

— That gives us some room to maneuver, 81 commented, his gaze still watchful in spite of it all.

Isidora, relatively quiet for once, was watching the adepts in the distance with an unusual calculating interest.

— We could grab one quietly. Make him spit out where Takeshi's daddy is.

— Good idea, Poppy approved, already assessing the tactical feasibility of the operation.

Takeshi, heart pounding, felt the anxiety rise as they went deeper into this hostile domain.

— And what if we run into an Incarnation on the way?

— We handle it, 81 cut in simply, resuming his cautious walk along the infinite corridor.

None of the group's members knew yet that this absence of serious resistance — the very absence of KJ in person — was not due to their stealth or their luck, but to the fact that the supreme entity himself had disappeared from the Palace several days ago, leaving behind a power vacuum that even Akuma was struggling to fill completely.

The group advanced silently, discreetly closing in on the first group of adepts, still unaware of how, paradoxically, the moment was almost ideal for their infiltration.

The two adepts, held firmly by 81 and Agent 47, were kneeling in the middle of the corridor, their dark robes trembling slightly despite their rigid posture.

Isidora came closer, casually twirling a small blade between her fingers, a far too enthusiastic smile stretching across her face.

— So, who am I gonna make talk first?

— Who are you and how did you get in here? Adept 1 asked, his voice trembling despite his attempt at firmness.

— Nope, I still don't know how I'm gonna have fun with you two, Isidora answered, completely ignoring the question, her gaze sizing up the two adepts as if they were mere menu options.

— You dare desecrate such a sacred domain, you filthy lesser being, Adept 2 spat, a misplaced pride piercing his voice despite the situation.

Isidora turned to him, one eyebrow raised, a predatory smile forming.

— Okay, I'll start with you. You look like you've got a big mouth and a nice deep throat. Your husband must be happy at night.

— We're not allowed to marry in our religion, the adept answered, visibly thrown by the turn of the conversation.

— Good, 'cause otherwise it would've ended in divorce like my last marriage, which was my 935th by the way. But we're not here to talk about lost causes. Well, I already said Lucifer, so I broke my own rule. Dammit.

81, hanging back, exchanged a jaded look with Takeshi, both of them used to this kind of digression by now.

— Whatever you do to us, we will never tell you anything, ever, Adept 1 declared, an almost suicidal determination piercing his voice.

Isidora stopped dead, her blade frozen in midair, her face suddenly showing an expression of deep disappointment.

— ...Seriously? You're gonna do that?

— Do what, Adept 1 asked, hesitant.

— The whole "I'll never talk" thing. It's so cliché.

— It is our sacred duty to—

— YEAH YEAH I GET IT, she cut in, suddenly putting her blade away with total nonchalance.

Isidora grabbed Lucifer by the arm, dragging him unceremoniously in front of the two adepts still on their knees.

— ...Isidora, what are you—

— Shut up, it's for a good cause.

She squeezed her eyes shut, pulling the paper bag off Lucifer's head in one quick movement, turning away herself at the last second as a precaution.

— ...

An absolute silence followed, then a shrill, almost animal scream escaped both adepts at once.

— I DON'T HAVE THE WORDS TO DESCRIBE THAT, HAVE MERCY! Adept 1 screamed, his hands pressed over his own face as if to wipe the image off his retinas. I'LL TELL YOU EVERYTHING YOU WANT, BUT KILL ME, I'D RATHER FACE KJ THAN THAT THING I SAW!

— It's just my face, goddammit, Lucifer protested, his voice echoing from the darkness where he stood, the bag already put back in place by Isidora just as quickly. I'm not THAT ugly. When are you people gonna respect me, dammit, I'm gonna end up quitting this stupid story.

— Please, I'll tell you everything too, but kill me afterward, Adept 2 begged, curled up on himself, trembling.

Isidora, satisfied, leaned toward them, a triumphant smile on her lips.

— Very good. So where's KJ?

— He's not here, Adept 1 managed, his voice still trembling. Akuma's in charge for now.

— Okay, my little pairs of limp balls. Where's the kid's old man?

Adept 2, at the end of his resistance, barely raised his head.

— The prisoner was locked up on a floor of the Palace. Probably in the Abyss.

— I'll never thank you, so I'm outta here, Isidora concluded, already getting up, completely indifferent to the trauma she had just caused.

— Then kill us, the two adepts begged in unison, curled up in balls on the floor.

— Nope, guys, Isidora answered, an almost cruel smile stretching across her face as she walked away with the rest of the group. You're gonna have that vision for your whole existence. And in death too.

Lucifer, bringing up the rear, the bag firmly back in place, couldn't help a slight satisfied smile despite the constant humiliation of the day.

— ...That's the first time my ugliness has actually been useful for something.

— SHUT UP LULU, WE GOT WHAT WE WANTED, Isidora answered, without even turning around.

Behind them, the heart-rending screams of the two adepts kept echoing in the Imperial Palace's infinite corridor, forever scarred by what they had just seen.

The group made its way through the Palace's colossal corridors, following the directions wrung out of the two traumatized adepts, until they found themselves facing a door radically different in appearance from anything they had come across so far.

— ...

It was made of no known material — its surface seemed literally composed of fragments of reality pieced together, bits of landscapes, skies, impossible textures, overlapping and cracking without ever fully stabilizing, as if space itself had been cut up and then crudely glued back together.

81 stopped, staring at the door with immediate suspicion.

— ...What is that thing.

— The entrance to the Infinite Abyss, Poppy murmured, her gaze analyzing the unstable structure with unusual caution.

Takeshi felt his heart speed up, knowing his father might be just behind it.

— ...How do we open it.

Isidora, without the slightest hesitation, walked straight up to the door.

— Well, we push.

— WAIT, Lucifer exclaimed, urgency piercing his bag-muffled voice. We don't even know what's on the other side, it could be unstable, dangerous, or—

Too late.

Isidora simply placed her hand on the door of fragmented reality and opened it with a perfectly calm, almost nonchalant gesture, as if coming home after a long day.

— ...

The door opened without the slightest resistance, without an explosion, without further distortion, revealing a dark passage plunging deep into the darkness.

The rest of the group stood frozen for a moment, staring at Isidora in total disbelief.

— ...How did you do that, Takeshi managed, completely overwhelmed.

— Do what? she asked, sincerely confused, already walking inside.

— You just opened a door made of FRAGMENTS OF REALITY like it was your front door.

— Oh yeah, well it kinda is my front door, actually. I've been here a bunch of times.

— ...

81 exchanged an incredulous look with 47, the latter remaining, as always, unfazed by the revelation.

— You've been to the Infinite Abyss before, Lucifer repeated, his voice betraying a new worry. Like, the most dangerous and unstable place in the whole Imperial Palace.

— Yeah, I used to come here sometimes for some peace and quiet. Nobody ever comes here, it's chill.

Poppy, staring into the darkness beyond the open door, added in a neutral but tense voice:

— That would explain a lot about her, actually.

— THANKS POPPY, Isidora retorted, already heading deeper into the darkness without the slightest apprehension.

81, tightening his grip on his sword, followed, the rest of the group falling in behind with much more noticeable caution.

— Okay. Let's go get your father, Takeshi.

Takeshi simply nodded, unable to put together a clear answer, his heart pounding wildly as he in turn crossed the threshold of the Infinite Abyss.

The group went deeper into the depths of the Infinite Abyss, the darkness growing denser and denser as they advanced, until they came out into a vast cavern where a massive cage stood, its bars woven from a dark, unstable substance.

— ...

It was impossible to make out the prisoner inside, the cage itself seeming to absorb all surrounding light.

But they were not alone.

A figure stood motionless right next to the structure, its piercing gaze already fixed on them since their arrival.

— I am Tempus. And you will not get what you want.

— ...

81 froze instantly, recognizing the name mentioned earlier by the Assimilated during his escape.

Isidora, on the other hand, didn't seem impressed in the least, even taking a nonchalant step forward.

— Okay, Krampus, you're gonna move your fat ass and let us through.

— ...

Tempus stayed silent for a moment, his impassive expression cracking slightly at the wrong name.

— My name is Tempus. Not Krampus.

— Yeah yeah, that's what I said.

— No, you said Krampus.

— Tempus, Krampus, same thing, they sound the same.

81, regaining his composure, stepped forward in turn, his sword already half drawn.

— Tempus. The Incarnation of individualized time.

— Correct, Tempus confirmed, his gaze settling on 81 with calculating coldness. And I know exactly why you are here.

Takeshi, heart pounding, was staring at the dark cage behind Tempus, unable to look away.

— My father. Is he in there?

— Perhaps, Tempus answered, an icy smile forming. Or perhaps not. That will depend on your ability to get past me.

Agent 47, weapon already raised, quickly analyzed the Incarnation's stance.

— Riper, data on Tempus.

"Analysis in progress... Individualized temporal control per target, ability to slow down, speed up or freeze a specific opponent's perceived time. Extremely dangerous in single combat."

— Great, Lucifer breathed from his bag, a new tension piercing his voice.

Isidora, not impressed by the stats in the slightest, crossed her arms.

— Okay, Krampus—

— The Godslayer. Now that interests me more.

He slowly raised his hand, a visible temporal distortion beginning to form around him, the very air freezing slightly at his feet.

— Let's see if your reputation is deserved.

81 gripped his sword firmly, a cold determination crossing his one-eyed gaze.

— Get out of my way, or I'll move you by force.

The tense silence that followed foretold only one thing: an inevitable confrontation between the Godslayer and the Incarnation of Time, with the freedom of Takeshi's father as the ultimate stake.

Isidora, pulling out her phone again despite the palpable tension of the budding confrontation, pointed the camera at 81, planted in his fighting stance, sword raised before Tempus.

— OMG guys, first time I've seen the 81 position, I should learn it.

— ...

Lucifer turned to her, his bag-muffled voice betraying total exasperation.

— You just made a sex joke, like, right now? You couldn't find another moment?

— What, it's a historic moment, gotta immortalize it.

Tempus, the temporal distortion still forming around him, turned his head slightly toward Isidora, a hint of disbelief piercing through his usual impassivity.

— ...You're filming. Now. While I'm about to freeze your ally's time.

— Yeah, sorry, go on, don't mind me, Isidora answered, not bothered at all, even slightly adjusting her camera's angle for a better shot.

— Isidora, seriously.

— WHAT, GOTTA DOCUMENT YOUR EPIC FIGHT AGAINST MISTER CLOCK OVER THERE.

— MY NAME IS TEMPUS, the Incarnation repeated, a new irritation finally piercing his usually cold voice.

— THAT'S WHAT I SAID, MISTER CLOCK.

Takeshi, despite the gravity of the situation, felt a nervous laugh escape him, the absurdity of the scene clashing violently with the real stakes of the confrontation.

— We're literally about to die and she's doing livestreams.

— Priorities, Takeshi, Isidora answered, without even looking away from her screen. PRIORITIES.

Tempus, visibly out of patience with this unexpected treatment, abruptly closed his hand, the temporal distortion fully stabilizing around 81.

— Enough. Let's see if your body can keep up with the rhythm I impose on it.

Time seemed to partially freeze around 81, every movement suddenly becoming heavy, slowed down, as if he were now moving through an invisible liquid.

— ...

81 grimaced, immediately feeling the effect weigh on every one of his movements, but his one-eyed gaze remained firmly determined.

— That all you got?

Isidora, still live, instantly zoomed in on the scene, unfeigned enthusiasm in her voice.

— OH THAT'S SICK, GUYS LOOK AT THIS!

Lucifer, resigned, put a hand to his forehead under the bag.

— We're really not going to survive this day...

Tempus slowly closed his eyes, his voice dropping to a deep, almost incantatory murmur.

— Domain expansion... Tijd is mijn slaaf.

An invisible wave instantly spread across the entire Abyss, a temporal bubble enveloping the whole cavern, every particle of air, every suspended grain of dust freezing dead in space.

— ...

Takeshi was instantly immobilized, his whole body locked mid-movement. Lucifer, Poppy and Agent 47 suffered the same fate, each frozen in their exact pose, unable to make the slightest move.

Only 81 kept resisting, his movements slowed but still there, his raw willpower actively fighting the imposed temporal distortion.

— ...Impossible, Tempus breathed, a hint of surprise crossing his usually impassive face.

And yet, in the middle of this absolute temporal silence, a voice kept ringing out, perfectly free, perfectly intact.

— Don't you know Isidora's cosmic law or what, asshole?

— ...

Tempus jerked his head toward her, his temporal control visibly unable to affect the slightest part of her body — her mouth, at least, remaining completely free to move.

— Nothing can make me shut my big mouth. Ever. Even if I can't move anymore, I'm gonna keep making content for my followers. And obviously, keep running my big mouth.

— ...How, Tempus managed, astonishment clearly piercing his voice.

— Dunno, Isidora answered, her mouth the only thing able to move, the rest of her body perfectly frozen like the others. I've never managed to shut my own mouth, even when I tried. Maybe it's a curse, or a talent, not really sure.

81, still actively resisting the distortion, let out a strained laugh despite the effort.

— Even time itself... gives up against her mouth.

"Analysis confirmed," Reaper cut in, his voice ringing out strangely clearly despite 47's general immobility. "Isidora's vocal capacity seems to transcend conventional physical laws, temporal ones included."

Tempus, visibly thrown for the first time since the start of the confrontation, tightened his grip on his own domain, a new tension running through his body.

— No matter. Your mouth poses me no strategic problem. HE is what matters.

He pointed a trembling finger at 81, still actively fighting the temporal effect.

— How are you still resisting.

81, a fierce smile forming despite the visible effort, slowly raised his sword.

— I absorbed the powers of five goddamn cosmic dragons. You really think a little slowed-down time is gonna stop me?

Isidora, still frozen but her mouth perfectly free, couldn't help one more comment.

— GO 81, SHOW HIM WHO'S BOSS, MEANWHILE I'LL KEEP THE LIVE GOING, GUYS YOU SEE THIS IT'S INSANE—

— SHUT UP, Tempus screamed, his patience visibly at an end, his temporal domain tightening further around 81 in a desperate attempt to regain control.

— NEVER, she simply answered, a triumphant smile stretching across her face as 81 kept up his relentless fight against time itself.
