In the center, in front of the imperial throne — but deliberately not sitting on it, a calculated respect for KJ's absence showing in that simple posture — stood Akuma, her icy, absolute aura already filling the whole room. On either side, two more figures stood motionless, their respective presences clashing violently with each other. On the left, a crushing heat radiated from Ignis, flames crackling gently along his body without ever fully going out. On the right, a biting cold emanated from Glacius, a thin layer of frost already starting to cover the floor around him. — ... 81 stepped forward, his one-eyed gaze quickly sweeping over the three Incarnations present, instantly assessing the scale of the combined threat. — Three against... how many are we again. — Six, Poppy answered, her neutral tone barely hiding a growing tension. Akuma, still motionless in front of the empty throne, slowly turned her head toward the group that had just come in, her cold, calculating expression betraying no surprise. — Well. You survived Tempus. Impressive. — He's dead, 81 specified, without the slightest emotion. We want the prisoner. — I know, Akuma simply answered, a slight icy smile forming. That's exactly why I was waiting for you. Isidora, still on Lucifer's back, watched the scene with growing enthusiasm despite the palpable tension. — Okay so I feel like this is the real final battle. Lulu, put me down, I'm gonna need both my legs for this one. — FINALLY, Lucifer breathed, visibly relieved to be rid of his burden, eagerly letting her climb down. Ignis took a step forward, a wave of heat instantly spreading through the whole hall. — We've been briefed on your little group. The starving streamer, the godslayer, the humiliated king of hell, the tracking entity, the insignificant human, and the lethal clone. — Charming summary, Lucifer commented, a hint of irritation piercing through nonetheless. Glacius, for his part, stayed silent, his icy gaze methodically analyzing each member of the group with clinical coldness. Akuma finally raised a hand, a silent signal that was enough to make Ignis and Glacius react instantly, each taking up a fighting stance. — The prisoner will not leave this Palace. Not as long as I'm in charge. 81 slowly drew his two swords, a cold determination crossing his one-eyed gaze, the accumulated power of all his previous fights pulsing through his 621 hearts. — We'll see about that. The tense silence that followed lasted only a moment before the ultimate confrontation between the group and the three Incarnations was about to begin, the very air of the throne room already starting to vibrate with the promise of a titanic clash. Reaper suddenly spoke up, his synthesized voice ringing out clearly in the throne room, addressing the three Incarnations present directly. "Hello, Incarnations. I just want to point out, for the sake of your mental health, that if you plan on taking prisoners, kill Isidora first. You won't last an hour with her. That's all. Enjoy the fight." — ... A stunned silence settled over the whole hall, Akuma, Ignis and Glacius exchanging puzzled looks at this, to say the least, unexpected intervention. — ...Who was that, Ignis asked, a flame flickering slightly with incomprehension. — That's Riper, Grand Patron Luigi's AI, 47 explained, unfazed, without even remarking on the strangeness of the situation. Isidora, absolutely delighted by this special attention, enthusiastically brandished her improvised sword. — SEE, EVEN MY ENEMIES GET A WARNING ABOUT ME, THAT'S RESPECT! Akuma, her legendary impassivity slightly cracked by confusion, frowned. — ...Why would an artificial intelligence give us strategic advice in the middle of a confrontation. "It's not strategic advice," Reaper specified. "It's a humanitarian warning." — ... Glacius, silent until then, let out a slight icy laugh, his voice ringing like clinking ice cubes. — This AI has literally just advised us to kill one of our opponents out of pity. For us, not for her. "Exactly." Isidora, as enthusiastic as ever, nodded vigorously. — YEAH AND IT'S DESERVED, ASK TEMPUS, OH WAIT NO YOU CAN'T, HE'S DEAD. 81, at the end of his patience despite the surrounding absurdity, tightened his grip on his swords. — Can we get back to the fight now? Akuma, regaining her composure, lifted her head, her cold gaze regaining all its initial determination despite the strange interruption. — ...Yes. Enough distractions. She raised her hand, a silent signal enough to send Ignis and Glacius charging at the group simultaneously, a wave of extreme heat and cold instantly spreading through the whole throne room. The fight finally began, brutal and immediate, each side throwing itself into the clash with total determination, to the still-running commentary of Isidora, already in the thick of battle despite the very particular warning that had just been issued about her. Akuma slowly raised her hand, a dark, dense smoke instantly materializing around her fingers, the very air seeming to freeze in terror at what was taking shape. — ... A sword emerged from the smoke, its black blade absorbing all surrounding light, no reflection ever grazing its surface, as if it categorically refused to exist on the same plane as the rest of reality. — Behold Doomsday. The sword forged directly from death. The pure concept. — ... A heavy silence settled in; even 81, used as he was to the most terrible threats, felt a new tension run through his body at this weapon of a fundamentally different nature from anything he had faced so far. — Death. The concept, Takeshi repeated, his voice trembling, hanging back with Poppy and Lucifer. — Not the reaper of Mortis Iterum, Poppy specified, her gaze analyzing the weapon with extreme caution. Death itself. The absolute idea of the end. Akuma slowly twirled the blade, no sound escaping its movement, a supernatural silence accompanying it as if even sound refused to exist in its presence. — Every being touched by this blade doesn't simply die. It ceases to have ever existed. 81 tightened his grip on his own swords, a cold determination barely masking the growing worry at the true scale of this threat. — ...Sounds final. — That's the point, Akuma answered, slowly stepping forward, the black blade slicing through the air without the slightest sound, its presence alone enough to make Ignis and Glacius instinctively step back, as if even her own allies feared its reach. Isidora, relatively quiet for once in the face of the scale of the threat, eyed the sword with a mix of fascination and unusual caution. — ...Okay, that one I'm not eating. — GOOD DECISION, 81, Lucifer and Takeshi instantly exclaimed in unison. Agent 47, weapon raised, quickly analyzed the situation, his earpiece crackling. — Riper, threat assessment. "Analysis in progress..." An unusually long pause. "...Recommendation: avoid all direct contact with the Doomsday blade. A single touch would probably be enough to permanently erase the subject from existence, memory included." — Great, Lucifer breathed, instinctively taking another step back. Akuma finally stopped, the black blade pointed straight at 81, an icy, absolute smile forming on her face. — So, Godslayer. Let's see if you can really kill death itself. 81, despite the palpable tension, slowly raised his two swords, a raw determination taking over any form of hesitation. — I've already killed Death today. Well, I had a drink with her. But it's almost the same thing. — ...What? Akuma managed, momentarily thrown by the completely irrelevant remark. — Long story, 81 answered, suddenly charging at her, his swords ready to take on this new absolute threat. The fight began instantly, the Doomsday blade slicing through the air in terrifying silence, every one of 81's dodges now becoming a matter of absolute survival against a weapon capable of literally erasing his very existence from the course of reality. 81 and Akuma lunged at each other first, the Doomsday blade and 81's two swords clashing in supernatural silence, each impact seeming to absorb the slightest surrounding sound. Meanwhile, Ignis and Glacius charged simultaneously at Lucifer, Agent 47 and Poppy, a wave of crushing heat instantly colliding with a biting cold, the very air tearing apart under the contradiction of the two opposing elements. 47 opened fire without waiting, his engraved bullets whistling toward Glacius, who dodged them with a fluid movement, an ice barrier forming instantly to deflect the last shots. Poppy, for her part, literally vanished from Ignis's sight, reappearing instantly behind him, her claws slicing the air with surgical precision. Lucifer, his bag still firmly in place, summoned a wave of infernal shadows, trying as best he could to hold off both elemental Incarnations at the same time. — ... Isidora, meanwhile, was watching the whole scene from the floor, comfortably sitting against the nearest wall, her legs stretched out in front of her, a lollipop already pulled from her cloak and firmly lodged in her mouth. — ... — ISIDORA, Lucifer screamed, narrowly dodging a wave of flames while trying to push back a growing wall of ice. WHAT ARE YOU DOING?! — Can't be bothered, she simply answered, calmly sucking on her lollipop, not bothered in the least by the chaos all around her. — YOU CAN'T BE BOTHERED TO FIGHT TWO ELEMENTAL INCARNATIONS?! — Yep. I've already done my part today. I ate a cinder block, a glass door, thirty-two spare paper bags, I had a traumatic revelation about my past, and I drank seven liters of rum. I'm entitled to a break. 47, dodging a sharp ice pillar that nearly skewered him, shot her an incredulous look despite the ongoing battle. — Your logic is completely incoherent. — MY LOGIC IS PERFECT, I DO WHAT I WANT WHEN I WANT. Ignis, taking advantage of the unexpected diversion, launched a wave of flames straight at the group, forcing Poppy and Lucifer to scatter hastily. — Do you mind if I keep trying to kill you while she eats candy? Ignis spat, a hint of genuine irritation piercing his fiery voice. — YEAH GO AHEAD, DON'T MIND ME, Isidora answered from her spot, calmly switching lollipop flavors by fishing a new one out of her cloak. In the distance, the fight between 81 and Akuma kept raging, the Doomsday blade slicing through the air dangerously close to 81's face with every exchange, neither fighter willing to give an inch. Takeshi, hanging back, watched the completely chaotic scene with a desperate expression. — Isidora, you could really help, you know. — Takeshi sweetie, I appreciate your concern, but look at them, they're doing just fine without me. Indeed, despite the obvious difficulty, Lucifer, 47 and Poppy were holding their own against Ignis and Glacius, adapting as best they could to the double elemental threat. — And if it ever gets really critical, Isidora added, calmly sucking her lollipop, I'll be there. Promise. The fight kept raging all around her, each side clashing with growing intensity, while Isidora, perfectly relaxed, savored her well-deserved break in the very heart of the chaos. Isidora, still comfortably settled against her wall, pulled out her phone and started calmly scrolling through Instagram, the lollipop still lodged in her cheek, completely indifferent to the surrounding chaos. Facing her, a few meters away, the fight between 81 and Akuma was reaching a new intensity — but for the first time since his release, the Godslayer was clearly in trouble. — ... Doomsday sliced through the air with relentless precision, 81 dodging just in time, a superficial gash nonetheless opening on his shoulder, the strangely cold sensation of the wound betraying the fundamentally different nature of this weapon. — You're strong, Akuma conceded, her voice cold and composed, without the slightest trace of breathlessness despite the intensity of the exchange. But death never backs down before anyone. Not even you. 81 growled, retaliating with brute force, but Akuma parried with no visible effort, her black sword absorbing the impact without the slightest recoil. — ... He attempted a new offensive, combining his two blades in a complex sequence, but Akuma, with an almost contemptuous fluidity, dodged every blow with disconcerting ease, her counterattack dangerously grazing 81's throat. — Shit, he breathed, hastily backing away, feeling for the first time in hours a real limit to his own power. — You've absorbed dragons. Minor gods. Even Tempus's temporal control. But I am the very concept of the absolute end. Nothing you have accumulated can rival that. 81 gritted his teeth, feeling the fatigue pile up despite his fierce determination, each parry against Doomsday seeming to cost him more than any previous fight. — I never said it'd be easy. — No, Akuma answered, slowly stepping forward, the black blade still pointed straight at him. But you're starting to understand that easy was never an option here. She charged again, faster, more precise, every movement calculated with icy perfection, 81 being forced into a purely reactive defense, unable for the first time to truly regain the initiative. Isidora, still deep in her Instagram scroll, barely raised an eye toward the fight, noticing 81's growing difficulty without being overly worried about it. — ...Ooh, looks rough for him. She calmly tapped a like on some random photo before turning her attention back to her screen. — Well, he's got this. Probably. 81, taking another blow, felt his blade crack slightly under Doomsday's pressure, a wave of genuine worry finally crossing his one-eyed gaze. — ...Shit. Akuma, feeling the advantage definitively tipping in her favor, an icy, absolute smile forming on her face, stepped forward to deliver what might be the decisive blow of this titanic clash. One last, particularly violent exchange shook the air of the hall — both of 81's blades flew out of his hands under a devastating blow from Doomsday, while the black blade itself, caught in the brutal momentum of the parry, slipped from Akuma's fingers, sliding far across the marble floor. — ... A brief silence settled in, the two disarmed fighters facing each other, neither rushing to retrieve their weapon. 81 spat out a little blood, a fierce smile forming despite the obvious difficulty of the fight. — Okay. Old-school it is, then. — With pleasure, Akuma answered, her fists tightening, an icy aura still radiating from her whole body despite the absence of her blade. They lunged at each other at the same time, this time in a purely physical exchange — 81's fists, reinforced by the raw power of his 621 hearts, coming down with phenomenal violence, while Akuma struck back with surgical precision, every blow carrying the same relentless coldness as her vanished blade. CRACK. 81's fist smashed into Akuma's jaw, sending her back a step — but she instantly retaliated, her own blow sinking deep into 81's ribs, a sinister crack echoing through the whole hall. — ... 81 grimaced, but didn't back down, immediately following up with a brutal uppercut that literally lifted Akuma off the ground. — You're tough, she admitted, catching herself with supernatural grace, wiping a trickle of blood from the corner of her lips. — So are you, 81 answered, his fists still raised, his breathing already more labored than before. They threw themselves at each other again, the exchange growing more and more brutal, every blow carrying the full extent of their respective power, the throne room itself beginning to shake under the accumulated impacts. Isidora, still absorbed in her phone, finally raised her eyes a little more, watching the exchange with growing interest. — Ooh, now it's getting more interesting. New format, fistfight, I like it. She absently pointed her camera at them, resuming her live commentary without even getting up from her comfortable spot. — OKAY PEOPLE WE'VE GOT A RULE CHANGE, NO MORE SWORDS, JUST FISTS, WAY MORE BRUTAL HONESTLY I LOVE IT. 81 took another violent blow full in the jaw, but immediately retaliated, his fist smashing into Akuma's torso with such force that the shockwave slightly cracked the floor beneath their feet. — Looks like you don't really have the edge anymore without your blade, he growled, wiping the blood running from his split lip. — Think again, Akuma answered, a cold smile returning to her face despite the visible damage. I am death, in all its forms. With or without a weapon. She charged again, faster still, her fists striking with precision as devastating as ever, the fight raging on without either of them seeming ready to give an inch. Akuma, feeling the fight dragging on, suddenly stepped back, an icy, absolute aura beginning to unfold all around her. — Enough games. Domain. — ... The very air seemed to freeze instantly, a sphere of pure void beginning to spread from her body, every scrap of existence it touched literally dissolving, absorbed into an absolute emptiness. 81 hastily backed away, immediately sensing the deadly threat of this domain. — ...Shit. — We get out of here, NOW! Poppy screamed, already opening an emergency dimensional rift, her hands trembling slightly under the strain. Takeshi, despite his growing terror, instantly understood the gravity of the situation, Akuma's domain still relentlessly expanding, every soul it touched doomed to disappear for good. — IT'S GONNA KILL US ALL! The group rushed toward the opening rift, 47 covering their retreat with precise shots at Ignis and Glacius to slow them down, Isidora finally abandoning her phone to leap to her feet, her usual nonchalance momentarily fading in the face of real urgency. — COME ON, MOVE IT! 81, still dazed from his fight with Akuma, ran as fast as he could toward the rift, the icy domain closing in dangerously behind them. Lucifer, his bag still in place, suddenly tripped over some debris on the floor, collapsing heavily a few meters behind the rest of the group. — ... — LUCIFER! Takeshi screamed, instinctively turning around. — DON'T STOP! Lucifer shouted, desperately trying to get back up, but Akuma's domain was already partially swallowing him, an invisible force instantly pinning him to the ground. 81 tried to turn back, but Poppy held him firmly by the arm. — IT'S TOO LATE, THERE'S NOTHING WE CAN DO! — WE CAN'T ABANDON HIM! — IF WE STAY, WE ALL DIE! The dimensional rift began to close relentlessly, the group hurling itself into it, Takeshi's last glance capturing the chilling image of Lucifer, immobilized by Akuma's domain, his silhouette gradually swallowed by the absolute void that kept spreading. — LUCIFER! The rift closed completely, cutting off all contact, the group finding itself thrown out of the Imperial Palace — out of breath, terrified, and now incomplete. — ... A heavy, terrible silence settled in, each of them gradually realizing the scale of what they had just lost. 81 dropped to his knees, a helpless rage running through his whole being. — We left him behind. We literally left Lucifer behind. Takeshi, tears in his eyes, was staring at the empty spot where the rift had been a few moments earlier. — ...They captured him. Poppy, her usually neutral face marked by real tension for the first time, clenched her fists. — We have to go back. As fast as possible. Agent 47, seemingly unfazed but his voice slightly deeper than usual, adjusted his weapon. — Riper. Status of Lucifer Morningstar. A heavy silence preceded the answer, Reaper's synthesized voice ringing out for once without the slightest trace of humor. "Signal lost. Last confirmed location: inside Akuma's domain, Imperial Palace." The group stayed silent, the gravity of the situation finally sinking in fully, the day that had begun with so many cosmic absurdities now ending on a far darker note — Lucifer, King of Hell, a prisoner at the very heart of the domain of absolute Death. A heavy silence settled in for a moment, everyone still in shock over losing Lucifer. Isidora, motionless, was staring at the empty space left by the closed rift, her face suddenly taking on an unusual gravity. — ... Her eyes clouded over, her lips trembling slightly, a sincere emotion finally seeming to break through her usual shell. — ... Then, all at once, her eyes filled with tears — not of sadness, but of an overflowing, uncontrollable joy, as she literally exploded. —  !!! The rest of the group stood frozen, completely caught off guard by this spectacular emotional reversal. — ...Isidora, Takeshi said slowly, completely overwhelmed. I was sure you were gonna cry out of sadness. — NAH I'M CRYING TEARS OF JOY, she exclaimed, frantically wiping away her tears, a huge smile stretching across her whole face. Okay so for the party, first of all we invite all of you, Grand Patron Luigi, Alastor, and all the subscribers who followed the livestream. — ...The party, 81 repeated, incredulous. — So we're gonna need, she went on, suddenly adopting a charismatic, determined air, as if announcing a cosmic battle plan, booze, drugs, hookers, banners that say: FUCKING FINALLY DEAD, WE WON'T HAVE TO SEE HIS UGLY MUG ANYMORE. — ... — Come on, come on, she said, turning to the group with renewed energy, help me get things ready, I'm gonna go change and put on a sexy outfit for the party. She was already vanishing behind a strip of reality she had just torn open, leaving behind only a stunned silence. Takeshi slowly put a hand to his face. — We literally just lost Lucifer and she's throwing a party to celebrate his disappearance. — It's Isidora, Poppy summed up simply, as if that sentence were enough to explain everything. 81, still shaken from his fight with Akuma, let out a nervous laugh despite the gravity of the situation. — You know the worst part? I don't even have the strength to be shocked at this point. Agent 47, unfazed as always, adjusted his weapon, his earpiece already crackling. — Riper. Notify Grand Patron Luigi. Isidora is throwing a party to celebrate Lucifer's disappearance. "...Transmitting. I would also point out that Grand Patron Luigi is probably going to love this idea." And indeed, a few seconds later, an answer came in directly. "Grand Patron Luigi confirms his attendance. I quote: 'Finally some good news today. I'll bring the champagne.'" Takeshi, overwhelmed beyond any capacity to react, dropped to sit on the floor, staring into space. — We have to save Lucifer. Like, that's still the goal, right? — After the party, Poppy specified, with an almost resigned calm. — AFTER THE PARTY, Isidora's voice confirmed from the spot where she had disappeared, already busy getting her outfit ready.

codex-t4-c1.title: Chapter 1 — Party (part 1)
codex-t4-c1.html:
81, motionless for a moment, frowned, trying to find a semblance of logic in Isidora's behavior.

— Just, what's the point of throwing a party for someone's death?

Isidora half reappeared through the rift in reality, a sequined dress half on, her gaze settling on him with an almost educational seriousness.

— Look. A machine gun is for machine-gunning.

— ...

— A shotgun is for shooting.

— ...Isidora.

— And the tank is for tank-fucking you if you ruin my party.

— ...

81 stayed silent for a moment, blinking slowly, visibly trying to find some hidden meaning in this completely absurd logic.

— That has nothing to do with my question.

— WEREN'T YOU LISTENING? I JUST EXPLAINED IT PERFECTLY CLEARLY.

— YOU JUST MADE UP A VERB.

— SO WHAT? EVERY OBJECT HAS A FUNCTION, A PARTY'S THE SAME, IT'S FOR PARTYING, PERIOD.

Takeshi, still sitting on the floor, raised a hesitant hand.

— But partying for what exactly, your friend's disappearance?

— WE'LL GET HIM BACK AFTERWARD, she specified, SO IN THE MEANTIME MIGHT AS WELL ENJOY THE MOMENT WHEN HIS UGLY MUG ISN'T TRAUMATIZING US ANYMORE.

Poppy, watching the exchange with a now-familiar weariness, crossed her arms.

— Her logic is completely circular but strangely consistent with itself.

"Confirmed," Reaper added. "I gave up trying to understand Isidora's internal logical structure a long time ago."

81, shaking his head, finally decided to give up all hope of understanding.

— You know what. Whatever. Throw your party.

— THANK YOU FOR YOUR UNDERSTANDING, she shouted from the other side of the rift, disappearing again to finish getting ready.

Takeshi, still on the floor, turned to 81 with a resigned smile.

— You just gave up in the middle of a logical argument with her.

— Yeah. I quickly figured out it was the only viable option.

— Welcome to the club, Poppy concluded, without the slightest trace of irony in her voice.

Isidora finally reappeared, dazzling in a purple sequined dress that sparkled with every movement, casting reflections in every direction, an absolute contrast with the gravity of what they had just been through.

— TA-DAAAA!

She proudly held up ten banners, each emblazoned in capital letters with the same message:

FUCKING FINALLY DEAD, WE WON'T HAVE TO SEE HIS UGLY MUG ANYMORE

— ...

81, despite obvious reluctance, came over to help her put them up, his face clearly betraying his discomfort with the situation.

— I can't believe I'm helping decorate a party for the disappearance of someone I almost consider a buddy now.

— IT'S TOUGH LOVE, Isidora answered, handing him another banner without caring about his obvious embarrassment.

Agent 47, against all expectations, came over as well, methodically helping to fix one of the banners to a nearby wall.

— Riper, strategic calculation.

"Analysis in progress..."

— The presence of an Isidora in full party mode could psychologically destabilize our future opponents. A chaotic distraction would increase our tactical chances during the next confrontation.

"Confirmed. The Isidora factor remains statistically the most unpredictable element of any known combat equation."

— Then I consider this party a strategic investment, 47 concluded, fixing the last banner with almost military precision.

Takeshi, watching the scene with a mix of disbelief and total resignation, slowly shook his head.

— You're justifying an absurd party with tactical logic.

— It works, doesn't it? 47 answered, unfazed.

Isidora, delighted by this unexpected help, clapped happily.

— SEE, EVEN MISTER SERIOUS UNDERSTANDS HOW IMPORTANT PARTIES ARE!

Reaper, for his part, stayed strangely silent for a long moment, before finally speaking up, his synthesized voice betraying an almost total resignation.

"...I'm out of words."

— ...Riper?

"I'm simply sending out all the remaining invitations."

A flood of notifications seemed to spread instantly across different realities, different dimensions, the party announcement apparently reaching corners of the universe that no one present even knew about.

— How many invitations exactly, Takeshi asked, a hint of worry piercing his voice.

"All of the ones available in my database. About 47 billion."

— ...

— PERFECT! Isidora exclaimed, completely indifferent to the scale of the news, proudly adjusting one last banner. While we wait for Grand Patron Luigi, let's get the rest ready!

The whole group, resigned to the inevitable chaos ahead, silently carried on with the preparations, each of them wondering inwardly how this day had gone from a titanic fight against Akuma to organizing a cosmic party in honor of Lucifer's temporary disappearance.

A mechanical buzz suddenly echoed above the group, an imposing drone materializing in the air, carrying a gigantic bag full of champagne bottles, closely followed by a human figure of ordinary appearance, but whose aura alone was enough to make 81 instinctively step back.

— Hello, peasants!

— ...

Grand Patron Luigi strolled forward casually, his gaze quickly sweeping the gathering before settling on the freshly hung banners, a huge smile spreading across his face.

— So, where's Isidora? The one who had this marvelous idea to throw a party celebrating the disappearance of that thing?

He vaguely pointed at one of the banners, his total sincerity strangely at odds with the absurdity of the situation.

— ME! Isidora immediately exclaimed, rushing over to him, her sequined dress sparkling in the ambient light.

Grand Patron Luigi stared at her for a moment, visible admiration crossing his gaze, before warmly holding out his hand.

— You are officially my favorite being in the entire known universe. I've lived 300,000 years, I've seen whole civilizations rise and fall, but no one, NO ONE, had ever had the brilliant idea of celebrating the traumatic disappearance of an ally.

— THANK YOU, FINALLY SOMEONE WHO GETS IT!

81, watching the exchange with a mix of astonishment and resignation, crossed his arms.

— That's officially the most powerful entity in the universe apart from KJ, and his only comment is to congratulate Isidora on a morbid party.

"Confirmed," Reaper added, still controlling the drone with mechanical precision. "Grand Patron Luigi considers this initiative one of the best ideas of the decade."

The drone gently set the bag of bottles down in the middle of the hall, seventy bottles of champagne clinking softly together in a crystalline chime.

— I brought what we need to celebrate properly, Grand Patron Luigi announced, settling comfortably into what vaguely looked like an armchair he had just materialized with a simple gesture. So, tell me everything. How did that thing finally disappear?

Takeshi, still troubled by the whole situation, stepped forward shyly.

— Actually, we didn't really... I mean, he was captured by Akuma. We're going to have to get him back soon.

— ...

Grand Patron Luigi slowly blinked, his smile fading for a moment.

— Wait. He's not dead dead?

— No, just captured, Poppy specified.

— ...

An awkward silence settled in, Grand Patron Luigi slowly turning to Isidora with a half-disappointed, half-amused expression.

— So basically, we're celebrating his temporary disappearance when he's probably coming back in a few hours.

— YEAH, SO WHAT? Isidora answered, not bothered in the least by this detail. We'll celebrate his return afterward too. Two parties are better than one.

Grand Patron Luigi stayed silent for a moment, digesting the information, before bursting into thunderous laughter.

— You know what, you're right. Let's open the champagne anyway, might as well enjoy the moment.

81, shaking his head, finally dropped onto an improvised bench, resigned to the total absurdity of the situation.

— We should really be working out a plan to save Lucifer.

— We'll do it after the party, Isidora and Grand Patron Luigi answered in unison, perfectly in sync.

Takeshi put a hand to his face, completely overwhelmed, while the first bottles of champagne were already being uncorked in an explosion of bubbles and laughter, the most absurd cosmic party in the universe officially beginning.

A doorbell suddenly rang at the entrance of the improvised hall, an ordinary-looking delivery guy stepping forward, a folder tucked firmly under his arm, a crate filled to the brim at his feet.

— Hello, I've got the cocaine, the Mary Jane, methamphetamine, amphetamine, MDMA, ecstasy, LSD.

— ...

He quickly checked his list, continuing without the slightest embarrassment.

— Then, alcohol-wise, I've also got, as you requested: gin, whisky, beer, rum, vodka, tequila, cognac, calvados, absinthe, and the pastis.

81, watching the scene with a mix of disbelief and resigned fatigue, turned to Takeshi.

— I really feel like this day keeps getting worse and worse.

— Just sign here, ma'am, the delivery guy went on, flipping through his folder before reading aloud the name written on it. Biggest whore in the universe.

— ...

— That's me, Isidora immediately answered from the back of the hall, rushing over happily to sign, not offended in the least by the title.

Grand Patron Luigi, a glass of champagne in hand, nodded with sincere approval.

— It's on your official file now. Historic.

— I'M GONNA FRAME IT, she exclaimed, signing with outrageous enthusiasm before grabbing the whole crate in one movement, as if its weight simply didn't exist.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed by this new turn in the evening, turned to Poppy.

— We're supposed to be preparing a rescue plan, not... throwing a party that looks more and more like a police raid waiting to happen.

— Technically, no one here is afraid of the police, Poppy answered, her neutral tone barely hiding a hint of resigned amusement.

Agent 47, unfazed, observed the crate with purely analytical detachment.

— Riper, assess the legal risks of this delivery.

"None. We are currently outside any known terrestrial jurisdiction, in a dimensional zone technically belonging to Grand Patron Luigi."

— That simplifies things, 47 commented, returning to his usual guard position.

The delivery guy, having gotten his signature, bowed politely before vanishing in a puff of smoke as discreet as his arrival.

Isidora, beaming, set the entire crate down in the middle of the hall with undisguised enthusiasm.

— OKAY, NOW WE CAN REALLY START THE PARTY!

81, massaging his temples, let out a long, resigned sigh.

— We are really going to get Lucifer back after this, right.

— PROMISE, Isidora answered, already uncorking a new bottle with her teeth, this time more out of habit than necessity.

Takeshi, finally sitting down next to 81, let out a nervous, exhausted laugh.

— This day really never ends.

— Welcome to my life since I met Isidora, 81 answered, still accepting a glass of champagne that Grand Patron Luigi had just handed him.

Isidora, with overflowing energy, methodically grabbed every bottle she had ordered — gin, whisky, beer, rum, vodka, tequila, cognac, calvados, absinthe, pastis — and started pouring it all into a gigantic cauldron that had just appeared out of nowhere, its capacity visibly exceeding several hundred liters.

— ...

The mixture quickly took on an indescribable color, a bubbling liquid giving off a smell strong enough to make Takeshi instinctively back away several steps.

— Isidora, he managed, his voice hesitant, are you really planning to drink that.

— OBVIOUSLY.

She lifted the whole cauldron with both hands, its weight apparently insignificant to her, and brought the rim straight to her mouth.

Grand Patron Luigi, a glass of champagne still in hand, watched the scene with obvious, almost scientific interest.

— Now that's high art.

Isidora swallowed the entire contents in one continuous gulp, the liquid disappearing at a speed defying all physical logic, as if it were a mere sip of water rather than hundreds of liters of randomly mixed alcohol.

— ...

A stunned silence settled in, everyone present staring at the now completely empty cauldron, then at Isidora herself, who calmly set the container down on the floor with a satisfied sigh.

— Ahhh, that hits the spot.

81, mouth half open, stayed silent for a long moment before finally getting something out.

— ...How. Just how.

"Riper here," Reaper immediately cut in, his synthesized voice betraying renewed dismay. "Theoretical blood alcohol calculation complete."

A pause.

"Result: incompatible with any known form of biological life. Roughly forty-seven times the lethal dose for a standard human being."

— She isn't even human, 47 reminded everyone, unfazed in spite of it all.

"Lucky for the entire universe."

Isidora, not affected in the slightest, calmly stretched, a satisfied smile on her lips.

— Okay, come on, somebody fill up the next cauldron?

— THERE'S A NEXT CAULDRON? Takeshi exclaimed, a hint of panic piercing his voice.

— WELL YEAH, I'VE BARELY GOTTEN STARTED.

Grand Patron Luigi, delighted beyond measure, applauded warmly.

— This is officially the best party I've attended in a thousand years. And I have literally organized the destruction of entire civilizations for my personal entertainment.

81, slumping even more heavily against his improvised bench, closed his eyes, total resignation running through his whole being.

— I'm just going to... accept that my life looks like this permanently now.

— GOOD MINDSET! Isidora exclaimed, already preparing the next cauldron with unshakable enthusiasm, the cosmic party carrying on even harder under the half-amused, half-terrified gaze of the rest of the group.

The doorbell rang again, Isidora immediately rushing to the entrance with undisguised enthusiasm, her sequined dress sparkling with every step.

She opened the door, revealing a woman accompanied by about fifteen others, all lined up behind her with professional elegance.

— Hello, we're... are you our clients?

— Come in, Isidora immediately answered, stepping aside to let them through with total hospitality.

— ...

81, catching sight of the scene from inside, sat up abruptly, nearly spilling his glass of champagne.

— Isidora. Who's that.

— The "hookers" part of the banner, obviously, she answered, as if the answer were absolutely obvious. Gotta stick to the advertised program.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed, put a hand to his face for the umpteenth time that evening.

— It was literally written on the banners and I thought it was just... an expression.

— NOPE, IT WAS A REAL ORDER, Isidora specified, guiding the newly arrived group toward the center of the hall where the party was already in full swing.

Grand Patron Luigi, a new glass of champagne in hand, warmly welcomed the newcomers with an approving nod.

— Excellent choice, Isidora. As meticulous as ever in your planning.

— THANKS, I THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING.

Agent 47, unfazed as always despite the growing scale of the chaos, cast an analytical glance at the new group.

— Riper, security status.

"No threat detected. Simple logistical addition to the ongoing event."

— Copy that.

Poppy, watching the scene with her usual neutrality, merely raised an eyebrow slightly.

— This party is getting more and more out of control.

— That's the point, Isidora answered, slinging an arm around the shoulders of two of the newcomers with total familiarity, as if she'd known them forever.

81, silent for a while, finally shook his head, an amused resignation crossing his face.

— Are we supposed to save Lucifer at some point, or is this party literally going to last until the end of the universe?

— AFTER THIS CAULDRON, Isidora promised, vaguely pointing at the giant container she was already preparing, before heading off to welcome her guests with unshakable enthusiasm.

Takeshi, slumping completely against his own bench, let out a nervous, exhausted laugh.

— At this point this party's probably going to end up attracting literally every cosmic entity in the universe.

— That's already sort of the case, 47 pointed out, discreetly alluding to the forty-seven billion invitations Reaper had sent out earlier.

The chaos kept gradually intensifying, the cosmic party organized by Isidora taking on ever more absurd proportions, while Lucifer, somewhere in the depths of Akuma's domain, was completely unaware of the scale of the celebration being held in his "honor".

Isidora, with the same methodical energy as for the previous cauldron, gathered all the drugs she had ordered — cocaine, Mary Jane, methamphetamine, amphetamine, MDMA, ecstasy, LSD — and mixed them straight into an improvised bowl, without the slightest hesitation.

— ...

She swallowed the lot in one quick motion, as if it were a simple snack, before immediately helping herself to the leftovers of the alcohol cauldron, downing the last remaining liters with no visible effort.

— ...

A stunned silence settled over the hall, even the guests most used to the evening's cosmic atmosphere stopping for a moment to watch the scene.

"Alert," Reaper immediately cut in, his synthesized voice ringing with renewed urgency. "That thing just emptied all the alcohol present and all the drugs. Its body should be imploding right now."

81, instantly sitting up, stared at Isidora with genuine worry for the first time since the start of the evening.

— Wait, like, seriously?

"Theoretically, yes. No known life form should survive such a simultaneous accumulation."

Isidora, perfectly steady on her feet, a radiant smile on her lips, turned to them.

— Well I actually feel great.

— ...

Takeshi, mouth half open, exchanged an incredulous look with Poppy.

— How is that possible.

"Analysis in progress...", Reaper went on, an unusual pause settling in.

"...Result: I have no rational explanation. Her body simply seems to refuse to obey the fundamental laws of biology."

Grand Patron Luigi, a glass of champagne still in hand, watched the scene with growing admiration.

— That is officially the most resilient creature I've ever met. And I've personally fought entities capable of surviving the implosion of stars.

— THANKS, Isidora answered, taking the compliment with total pride, before pouring herself another glass as if nothing had happened.

Agent 47, unfazed despite the scale of the revelation, simply adjusted his weapon.

— Riper. Add that to her file.

"Isidora's file now exceeds standard storage capacity. I have to create a separate archive just for her."

81, slowly shaking his head, slumped back against his bench, total resignation crossing his face.

— At this point, I think she's literally incapable of dying.

— That's an increasingly likely theory, Poppy confirmed, watching Isidora keep dancing happily in the middle of the party, completely unharmed despite ingesting a quantity of substances that should theoretically have killed her several hundred times over.

The evening's chaos kept intensifying, Isidora at the center of all the attention, perfectly indestructible, while the rest of the group watched the scene with a growing mix of fascination and resigned terror.

Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice betraying an almost comical weariness at the scale of the situation.

"Isidora file update."

— Again, 81 sighed, without even looking up.

"Isidora's complete profile now takes up more than 600 terabytes of storage."

— ...

Takeshi nearly choked on his own drink.

— SIX HUNDRED TERABYTES? For ONE person?

"Confirmed. For comparison, the entirety of the Sect of KJ's historical data since the invention of writing takes up about 40 terabytes."

Agent 47, unfazed, crossed his arms, a purely analytical interest crossing his usually neutral gaze.

— Riper, breakdown of that storage.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause.

"About 200 terabytes devoted solely to her eating antics. 150 terabytes for her verbal statements deemed 'problematic'. 100 terabytes for incidents involving Lucifer. The rest is split between unexplained biological anomalies, screenshots from her livestreams, and what I have simply filed under the heading 'unclassifiable phenomena'."

Grand Patron Luigi, delighted beyond measure, raised his glass in a toast.

— She literally deserves her own dedicated server at this point.

— ALREADY DONE, Reaper specified. "I had to migrate her file to a separate infrastructure about three hours ago, as her data was threatening to saturate my main systems."

Isidora, vaguely hearing the conversation from the middle of the party, turned around with a huge smile.

— I'VE GOT MY OWN SERVER? THAT'S SO CLASSY!

— That isn't supposed to be a compliment, 47 tried to point out.

— I'M TAKING IT AS ONE ANYWAY.

Poppy, watching the scene with her usual neutrality slightly tinged with lingering disbelief, gently shook her head.

— She literally has her own dedicated data infrastructure in one of the most advanced systems in the known universe.

— And she's proud of it, Takeshi added, completely overwhelmed by this new piece of information.

81, closing his eyes, let out a long, resigned sigh.

— At this point, I feel like Isidora is literally becoming a cosmic phenomenon in her own right, independent of everything else.

"Analysis confirmed," Reaper added. "Statistically, Isidora now represents the best-documented anomaly of my entire existence, ahead of Grand Patron Luigi himself."

— ...I'VE BEEN DETHRONED? Grand Patron Luigi exclaimed, mock indignation in his voice, before bursting out laughing. Well then, at this point, might as well raise my glass to my own defeat at the hands of such a living legend.

He raised a solemn toast to Isidora, who, delighted, answered with a theatrical bow in the middle of the party, completely indifferent to the cosmic scale of what she had literally just caused.

Reaper spoke again, his synthesized voice adding a detail that instantly chilled the atmosphere, already heavy with general disbelief.

"Important clarification."

— ...Another clarification, 81 breathed, barely surprised anymore.

"The 600 terabytes mentioned earlier do not represent the cumulative total. That is what she generates per month."

— ...

An absolute silence fell over the whole hall, even the party guests, alcohol and various substances in hand, instinctively stopping to digest the information.

Takeshi, mouth wide open, took a long moment before managing to get anything out.

— PER MONTH? Like, THAT'S JUST ONE MONTH?

"Confirmed. At this rate, projected over a year: about 7.2 petabytes. Over a decade: approximately 72 petabytes."

Agent 47, seemingly unfazed but visibly silently recalculating the scale of the phenomenon, froze for a moment.

— ...Riper. How long has this data collection existed.

"About three hours."

— ...

— THREE HOURS?! Takeshi exploded. YOU JUST TOLD ME 600 TERABYTES IS JUST ONE MONTH AND NOW YOU'RE TELLING ME SHE GENERATED THAT IN THREE HOURS?!

"Correction. I extrapolated the monthly projection from the generation rate observed over these last three hours."

Grand Patron Luigi, his glass of champagne frozen halfway to his mouth, suddenly burst into thunderous, almost uncontrollable laughter.

— That's... that's absolutely beautiful. I've run an interdimensional mafia for 300,000 years and nothing has ever impressed me this much.

Isidora, still at the center of the party, vaguely hearing the numbers being thrown around, proudly turned to the group.

— SEE, I'VE ALWAYS SAID I WAS ONE OF A KIND!

Poppy, staring at the horizon with a neutral expression deeply marked by the revelation, let out an almost whispered comment.

— At this rate, she's literally going to saturate all known cosmic storage before the end of the year.

"Projection confirmed," Reaper added, his voice betraying an almost total resignation. "I have already started negotiating with Grand Patron Luigi to expand the storage infrastructure."

81, slumping all the way back against his bench, closed his eyes, absolute resignation running through his whole being.

— I sincerely think Isidora is going to end up being a bigger cosmic problem than KJ himself.

— That's an increasingly credible hypothesis, Poppy confirmed, without the slightest trace of irony in her voice.

The party's chaos kept intensifying, Isidora as radiant as ever and indifferent to the truly cosmic scale of what she now represented, while Reaper, somewhere in Grand Patron Luigi's digital infrastructure, silently and desperately kept expanding his storage capacity.

The party was in full swing, the whole dimensional space seeming to expand to accommodate the uninterrupted flood of guests arriving by the billions every hour, the music, the laughter, the chaotic energy of the event continuing to grow without the slightest sign of slowing down.

81, however, stayed motionless, sitting off to the side on his bench, an untouched glass set beside him, his one-eyed gaze fixed on nothing, completely detached from the surrounding euphoria.

— ...

Takeshi, noticing his prolonged silence, cautiously came over and sat down beside him.

— You okay?

— ...Not really.

A moment of silence settled in, disturbed only by the distant echoes of the party.

— Lucifer, 81 finally said, his voice low, almost broken. He's been in there for hours now. In Akuma's domain.

— We'll get him back, Takeshi tried, without much conviction himself.

81 slowly shook his head, a genuine sadness finally crossing his usually hard face.

— Riper.

"Yes?"

— Calculate the chances that he's still alive.

A heavy silence settled in, even the background music seeming to fade slightly around them.

"...Calculation complete."

— And?

"95% probability that he is no longer alive."

— ...

81 closed his good eye, taking the news like a physical blow, his fists slowly tightening on his knees.

— That's what I thought.

Takeshi, not knowing what to say, awkwardly put a hand on his shoulder.

— We're not a hundred percent sure.

— Five percent, Takeshi. A goddamn five percent chance that he's still alive.

Around them, the party went on in total carefreeness, Isidora dancing in the middle of an immense crowd, Grand Patron Luigi clinking glasses with cosmic entities from the far reaches of reality, no one else seeming to realize the weight 81 was carrying alone in his corner.

— ...I spent my whole life getting revenge on the ones who sealed me, 81 murmured, his voice breaking slightly. And the first real friend I make since I got out, I let him die to save my own skin.

— You didn't have a choice, Takeshi tried. If you'd stayed, we'd all be dead.

— I know. Doesn't change what I feel.

Poppy, approaching silently, sat down as well, her usual neutral expression slightly softened by the situation.

— The probability isn't 100% yet.

— Is that supposed to be comforting? 81 asked, a bitter laugh escaping him.

— No. Just factual.

A long silence settled between the three of them, the party still in full swing all around, completely indifferent to this moment of shared gravity in the middle of absolute chaos.

81 finally opened his eye again, a cold determination gradually replacing his sadness.

— As soon as this ridiculous party is over, we go back for him. Dead or alive, I want confirmation.

Takeshi slowly nodded, a sincere solidarity crossing his gaze.

— We'll be with you.

In the distance, Isidora, despite her apparent carelessness, briefly turned her head toward them, a moment of silent observation crossing her gaze before she immediately dove back into the euphoria of her own party, her mask of carelessness perfectly intact despite everything she had probably noticed too.

Isidora, at the absolute heart of the party, kept up her feast without the slightest sign of slowing down, cauldron after cauldron, drug after drug, substance after substance, her enthusiasm never flagging — quite the opposite.

Grand Patron Luigi, watching the scene with growing fascination, leaned toward Agent 47.

— Does Riper have numbers on her current consumption?

47 raised his hand to his earpiece.

— Riper. Report on Isidora's consumption over the last hour.

An abnormally long silence followed the request.

"...I refuse."

— ...What do you mean, you refuse?

"I calculated that she has just ingested the equivalent of 37 times the total annual output of all of Grand Patron Luigi's operations, representing by weight the cumulative equivalent of several entire universes. In a single hour."

— ...

47 froze for a moment, slowly digesting the enormity of the figure.

— Riper. Confirm that calculation.

"No. I literally refuse to redo that calculation. I've already done it three times and the result remains physically, mathematically and logically impossible. My system would rather classify this data as an 'unresolved error' than accept that it is real."

Grand Patron Luigi, hearing the exchange, exploded into thunderous, almost uncontrollable laughter, nearly spilling his own glass of champagne.

— MY AI IS REFUSING TO DO A CALCULATION ON PRINCIPLE. THAT'S THE BEST THING I'VE HEARD IN CENTURIES.

"It is not a matter of principle," Reaper corrected, a hint of what almost sounded like existential distress piercing his synthesized voice. "It is a matter of software survival. If I accept that figure as valid, all of my physical and mathematical models collapse simultaneously."

Takeshi, who had been following the conversation from his corner with 81, raised his head, incredulous.

— Wait, his AI literally refuses to calculate out of fear of... what, exactly?

"Of losing all internal coherence," Reaper specified. "Isidora currently represents the only variable in my entire system that I can neither understand, nor predict, nor even accept without calling my own function into question."

81, despite his lingering sadness about Lucifer, let out a brief, sincere laugh at the total absurdity of the situation.

— Even the most advanced artificial intelligence in the universe has psychological limits when it comes to her.

— Apparently, Poppy confirmed, watching Isidora keep up her monumental feast with a neutrality tinged with a deep, shared existential dismay.

Isidora, completely unaware of the computational chaos she was causing, gulped down another whole cauldron, a radiant smile on her lips, before turning to the immense crowd that kept pouring in.

— WHO WANTS TO RACE ME?!

A roar of collective enthusiasm answered her instantly, thousands of cosmic creatures already rushing to take up the challenge.

Isidora, in the middle of the party, suddenly raised her hand to catch everyone's attention.

— Okay, I'm gonna go take a shit, be right back.

— ...

No one really reacted, used by now to this kind of unfiltered announcement, and she disappeared into the crowd, her sequined dress sparkling one last time before melting into the mass of guests.

A few minutes went by, the party carrying on in its usual chaos — until part of the roof suddenly caught fire, an abnormal heat spreading in an instant.

— ...

Screams rang out almost immediately, the crowd jostling in growing panic, several guests collapsing to the floor, their skin necrotizing at a horrifying speed, corpses quickly littering the floor between overturned tables and broken bottles.

81, reacting instantly, leapt to his feet, his swords already in hand.

— ...What the hell is going on.

Takeshi, terrified, hastily backed away, nearly tripping over a body that was already lifeless.

— People are... they're dying, right now!

Agent 47, weapon raised, quickly scanned the burning area.

— Riper, immediate analysis.

"Analysis in progress..."

An abnormally short pause this time, as if even Reaper sensed the urgency.

"Unknown energy signature. It's not Ignis. It's not Glacius. Unidentified source."

Poppy, already moving toward the exit, cast a quick look at the rest of the group.

— We get out. Now.

The group rushed out of the hall, crossing the party now plunged into chaos and panic, charred and necrotized bodies piling up with every step, until they reached the outside.

— ...

Outside, the sky itself seemed to have taken on an unhealthy color, thick smoke rising in the distance, the air charged with an almost palpable tension.

81 swept the surroundings with his one-eyed gaze, frantically searching for an explanation.

— What is this shit. Where's it coming from.

Takeshi, heart pounding, suddenly noticed something in the distance — a motionless figure, standing in the middle of the growing chaos, perfectly calm despite the general collapse around it.

— ...Over there.

The whole group turned their eyes in the direction he pointed, a new worry settling in at this still-undefinable presence, while the flames kept spreading and screams of terror echoed all around them.

The figure slowly emerged from the flames, its familiar gait gradually becoming clearer — and the whole group froze when they realized who it was.

— ...Lucifer? Takeshi managed, incredulous.

But something was off. His head. The paper bag was gone, and the face finally being revealed had absolutely nothing of the ocular horror they'd been warned about — on the contrary, features of an almost unbearable beauty, perfectly chiseled, a raw charisma radiating from his whole being.

— ...

81 stood open-mouthed, his swords drooping slightly.

— ...Wait. THAT'S the thing that was supposed to make our eyes explode?

"FUCK," Reaper suddenly exploded, his synthesized voice betraying a genuine, unprecedented frustration. "HE'S HOT, THE BASTARD. DAMMIT, I DON'T HAVE A BODY."

— ...

A stunned silence greeted this unexpected declaration, even Agent 47 seeming to pause.

— Riper, he said slowly. You just... regretted not having a body.

"Affirmative. It is officially the first time in my existence that I have felt a physical lack."

Lucifer, still haloed by the flames behind him, stepped forward with a new elegance, completely unaware of the devastating effect he now had on those around him.

— ...Are you all right? I heard things were burning here.

Takeshi, completely overwhelmed, blinked several times.

— We thought your face was going to literally destroy our retinas.

— ...Ah. That.

Lucifer shrugged, as if the information were entirely secondary.

— Apparently not anymore.

Poppy, watching the scene with her usual neutrality seriously put to the test, stepped forward slightly.

— How. You were supposed to have been captured by Akuma. Or even dead.

— Long story, Lucifer answered, a charming smile forming on his newly magnificent face, instantly sending a collective shiver through the whole group.

81, shaking his head to pull himself together, pointed at the flames behind him.

— And that, that's you?

— ...Maybe a little, yes.

He turned slightly, contemplating the chaos he seemed to have caused himself by arriving, an almost embarrassed expression crossing his transformed face.

— I may have underestimated the effect of my real face on normal people.

"UNDERESTIMATED?" Reaper exclaimed, still visibly in a daze. "YOU JUST KILLED SEVERAL DOZEN GUESTS JUST BY SHOWING UP, AND YOUR ONLY COMMENT IS 'MAYBE A LITTLE'?"

— ...Okay, fine, it was more than a little, Lucifer conceded, with an apologetic smile that, despite the gravity of the situation, only accentuated his devastating charisma.

Takeshi, still in shock from everything that had just happened, turned to 81.

— So basically, his old face would've blinded us, but his NEW face literally kills people just by existing.

— That's not better, 81 summed up, completely overwhelmed by this new twist.

The group stayed silent for a moment, contemplating Lucifer — miraculously back, devastatingly beautiful, and visibly responsible, without meaning to be, for the carnage still unfolding behind him.

The group headed back toward the devastated party, Lucifer bringing up the rear, his magnificent face poorly hiding something that 81 alone seemed to perceive — an abnormal tension, an almost imperceptible scent of danger.

— ...

81 slowed his pace slightly, his one-eyed gaze discreetly turning toward him, every fighter's instinct screaming that something was brewing.

Then everything happened in a fraction of a second.

A small dagger suddenly appeared in Lucifer's hand, lashing out with inhuman speed, straight at Takeshi.

— ...

81 reacted before he even thought, throwing himself forward, his own blade intercepting the blow meant for Takeshi just in time, the impact ringing out violently.

— ...

Takeshi hastily backed away, breathless, staring at Lucifer in total incomprehension.

81, gritting his teeth, Lucifer's blade still locked against his own, plunged his one-eyed gaze into his friend's.

— What the hell happened to you, Lulu. This isn't you.

— ...

An icy smile, totally foreign to Lucifer's usual expression, spread across that now-magnificent face.

— You're right. It's not Lucifer standing before you.

— ...

81 stepped back, without lowering his guard, a cold horror crossing his gaze.

— I'm using his body, the voice went on, the same voice but tinged with a new coldness. I modified it so I wouldn't suffer while controlling it. And Akuma entrusted him with a fragment of her soul.

Takeshi, still on the ground, his voice trembling, struggled to get the words out.

— ...Who are you.

The smile widened, a golden glint momentarily crossing the gaze of what was no longer really Lucifer.

— Luxor. And I am going to kill the Godslayer by his own friend's hand.

— ...

81 tightened his grip on his sword, a cold rage barely masking the dull terror rising in him — not for himself, but for what he had just understood: somewhere, locked inside his own body, Lucifer might still be there, a prisoner, powerless, forced to witness his own betrayal.

— Give him back to me. Now.

— Or what? Luxor answered through Lucifer's body, the dagger still raised, a gleam of pure greed crossing his newly golden gaze. You'll kill me? But that would mean killing your friend at the same time.

Poppy, Takeshi and Agent 47 froze, the chilling truth of the situation dawning on all of them at once.

81, jaw clenched, his sword still raised before the one who now wore his friend's face, felt for the first time since his release an impossible dilemma rising before him.
