codex-t4-c3.html:
Luxor, still hidden beneath Lucifer's now-magnificent features, slowly twirled his dagger, a cruel smile stretching across his golden face.

— Your blood will flow when I'm done.

— ...

He took a step forward, completely indifferent to the deadly tension freezing the whole group around him.

— Then I'll carve myself a crown out of your spine.

Takeshi, still on the ground, instinctively backed away, terror gradually replacing his initial stupor.

— And with your skull, I'll make myself a toilet brush.

— ...

81, despite the absolute gravity of the situation, couldn't help a bitter, almost nervous smirk.

— You've got a shitty sense of humor for someone who just possessed my best buddy.

— It isn't humor, Godslayer, Luxor answered, his smile never wavering. It's a promise.

Agent 47, weapon already raised but clearly hesitant to shoot at Lucifer's body, tightened his grip.

— Riper, options.

"Analysis in progress..."

A tense, almost unbearable pause.

"No obvious solution allows Luxor to be neutralized without seriously endangering Lucifer Morningstar's bodily integrity."

— Great, 81 breathed, never taking his eyes off Luxor, his sword still raised between him and Takeshi.

Poppy, coldly analyzing the situation despite the tension, stepped forward slightly.

— How do we get you out of him.

Luxor slowly turned his head toward her, a cruel amusement crossing his golden gaze.

— You don't get me out. I leave when I've finished my work. And my work is to drain this body of all its blood, starting with the Godslayer.

He suddenly lunged, the dagger slicing through the air with a speed far beyond anything Lucifer could ever have reached naturally, 81 parrying just in time, the clash of blades ringing out violently in the air still heavy with the fire's lingering smoke.

— ...

— Isidora, Takeshi murmured, his voice trembling, hastily getting back up. Where's Isidora, she should've been back a long time ago.

An icy silence greeted the question, no one having an immediate answer, the group suddenly realizing they might be facing this new threat without their most unpredictable asset.

81, violently pushing Luxor back with a powerful sword stroke, growled through clenched teeth.

— We'll deal with that later. Right now, we've gotta figure out how to save Lucifer without killing him.

Luxor, barely staggering under the impact, a smile as cruel as ever on his stolen face, slowly raised his dagger again.

— Good luck with that.

Luxor hurled himself at 81, the dagger slicing through the air with a brutality utterly devoid of restraint, his borrowed body taking every extreme movement without the slightest regard for its physical integrity.

— ...

81 dodged just in time, hastily backing away, his sword raised but motionless, unable to land a single serious counterblow.

— Dammit, Lulu, stop!

— He can't hear you, Luxor sneered, immediately chaining a new attack, Lucifer's body twisting at angles it never could have reached naturally. And even if he could, I couldn't care less what he feels.

81 kept dodging, every movement defensive, never offensive, the tension growing as Luxor multiplied his assaults without the slightest hesitation.

— ...

— Why don't you fight back, Godslayer? Luxor asked, a hint of mockery piercing his voice. It's simple enough. Hit me. Hit him.

81 ground his teeth, backing away further, a superficial gash opening on his forearm after a dodge that just barely failed.

— I'm not gonna hurt him.

— Then you will die, Luxor simply answered, charging again, faster, more brutal, shamelessly exploiting his opponent's obvious hesitation.

Takeshi, still hanging back, panic growing by the second, turned desperately to Poppy and Agent 47.

— We have to do something, he's gonna get himself killed by refusing to really fight!

Agent 47, weapon still raised but unable to fire without risking hitting Lucifer directly, gritted his teeth.

— I don't have a safe firing angle.

Poppy, for her part, watched the scene with a new intensity, her gaze analyzing every one of Luxor's movements with calculating coldness.

— He's not trying to kill 81 directly. He's playing with him.

81, taking another blow, this time a deeper gash across his side, staggered back violently, his back slamming into a wall of charred rubble.

— ...

Luxor slowly approached, the dagger dripping, a satisfied smile stretching across Lucifer's magnificent, borrowed face.

— Come on, Godslayer. Show me your true nature. Or die holding back like a sentimental coward.

81, short of breath, felt a helpless rage boiling inside him, trapped between his survival instinct and his absolute refusal to hurt the one he now considered a true friend.

— ...

The already critical situation only kept getting worse, every second bringing Luxor a little closer to his goal, while 81, for the first time since his release, found himself completely paralyzed by a dilemma no brute force could solve.

An incongruous sound suddenly rang out a few meters away, Grand Patron Luigi calmly appearing in the middle of the chaos, a huge bucket of popcorn tucked under his arm, comfortably seated on a pile of charred corpses that were visibly serving as his improvised seat.

— ...

— Hey, come closer, we can't see well from here!

— ...

Takeshi, despite the absolute urgency of the situation, turned his head toward him in total disbelief.

— THERE'S AN INCARNATION TRYING TO KILL 81 USING LUCIFER'S BODY AND YOU'RE EATING POPCORN SITTING ON CORPSES?!

— Yep, Grand Patron Luigi answered, calmly grabbing another handful. This is premium content. Riper, you still filming?

"Affirmative," Reaper answered, his synthesized voice betraying a weariness tinged with almost total resignation. "The livestream is still running. Views are literally exploding."

81, taking another blow from Luxor, shot a quick, furious look at Grand Patron Luigi.

— MAYBE YOU COULD HELP ME INSTEAD OF WATCHING?!

— Nah, he simply answered, crossing his legs with disconcerting ease. It's your fight. I'm just here for the entertainment.

Luxor, taking advantage of 81's momentary distraction, struck a violent blow that sent him crashing into a nearby wall, a dull crack echoing through the air.

— ...

— OH THAT WAS A GOOD HIT, Grand Patron Luigi immediately commented, clapping with completely misplaced enthusiasm. Again, again!

Poppy, the tension rising dangerously, turned to him, a hint of irritation finally piercing her usual neutrality.

— You are literally the most powerful entity present here after KJ. You could settle this in a second.

— Yeah, I could, he confirmed, not bothered in the least by the remark. But where would be the fun in that?

Takeshi, completely desperate, turned back to 81, still on the ground, struggling to get up as Luxor slowly approached, visibly savoring his total domination of the fight.

— WE NEED HELP, NOT A SPECTATOR!

Grand Patron Luigi, calmly chewing his popcorn, simply shrugged.

— Technically, I never said I wasn't gonna help. I just said it wasn't the right time yet.

— THEN WHEN IS THE RIGHT TIME?! Takeshi screamed, total panic piercing his voice as Luxor raised his dagger, ready to deal a potentially fatal blow to 81, still on the ground.

Grand Patron Luigi, an enigmatic smile forming on his face, simply jerked his chin toward a specific direction, in the distance, behind them.

— Now, I think.

The whole group turned around, following his gaze, just in time to see a familiar figure finally emerging from the smoking ruins of the devastated party, an expression for once completely devoid of nonchalance crossing her face.

Isidora was back.

Isidora, her phone still in hand without having noticed the surrounding chaos, finally looked up.

— ...

Her gaze froze instantly on Lucifer — or rather on what now wore his face, the bloody dagger still raised, Luxor's cruel expression distorting features she had known for centuries.

The phone slipped from her hands, smashing on the ground without her caring for a single second.

She fell to her knees, her whole body contracting, a raw, uncontrollable energy beginning to radiate from her.

— ...

Then she screamed.

NO!!!!!

Isidora's scream, after six uninterrupted hours, finally died out in one last hiccup, her body still shaken by residual spasms.

— ...

— GODDAMMIT, HE WAS DEAD! she shouted, leaping to her feet, a raw rage completely replacing her initial distress. Why? Just why? The incarnations can't do anything right, it's just killing someone, it's not complicated, she's got a sword called DOOMSDAY and that's not enough, I'm gonna go make her a tutorial if this keeps up.

81, still frozen in front of Luxor, shot her a quick look, almost relieved to see her finally react.

— Isidora, he's not dead, it's Luxor controlling his body, he just explained it to us.

— ...

She stopped dead, slowly blinking, digesting the information with a noticeable delay.

— Wait. He's NOT dead?

— No.

— THEN WHY DID I CRY FOR SIX HOURS?!

Luxor, still hidden beneath Lucifer's magnificent features, watched the scene with cruel amusement, his dagger still raised.

— A disproportionate reaction, if I may say so.

— YOU SHUT UP, Isidora immediately screamed, turning on him with a new fury, black claws beginning to form along her fingers. YOU DARED MAKE ME CRY FOR SIX HOURS FOR NOTHING?!

— ...Technically, I never—

— I DON'T GIVE A SHIT ABOUT YOUR TECHNICALITIES, I'M GONNA CUT YOU INTO PIECES AND SERVE YOU AS TAPAS.

Grand Patron Luigi, still comfortably seated on his pile of corpses, leaned forward with renewed interest, his popcorn almost forgotten.

— OH THAT'S THE PLOT TWIST I WAS WAITING FOR.

Takeshi, still in shock from the scene of the past six hours, turned to Poppy, completely overwhelmed.

— She literally just went from total collapse to murderous rage in three seconds.

— It's Isidora, Poppy simply summed up, as always.

81, finally sensing an opening in this confrontation that had been blocked until then by his own moral dilemma, raised his sword, a new determination crossing his one-eyed gaze.

— Isidora. Can you get him out of there without killing Lucifer?

— I DON'T KNOW AND I DON'T CARE, ALL THAT MATTERS IS HE'S GONNA REGRET MAKING ME CRY.

Luxor, feeling a real worry pierce his cruel confidence for the first time, stepped back slightly, the dagger still in hand.

— ...Wait. Let's think about this calmly and—

— TOO LATE.

Isidora charged, with a speed and raw power far beyond anything she had shown so far that day, her fury fueling every movement, finally ready to get seriously into it for the first time since the start of their adventure.

Isidora violently smashed a small vial against Luxor's skull, the liquid spreading instantly, a strange glow enveloping Lucifer's entire body.

— ...

Without warning, she literally dove in, her mind projecting itself straight into Lucifer's, the mental space materializing around her as an infinite maze of floating memories.

— ...

Luxor, surprised by this sudden intrusion, also found himself trapped in this space, moving frantically between the fragments of memory, desperately searching for an exit.

He rushed through several memories at full speed — Lucifer as a child in Paradise, his fall, his coronation in Hell — until he slammed into a particularly bright memory brick, different from the others.

— ...

The image froze around him: Lucifer and Isidora, waking up in the same bed, an obvious intimacy hanging in the air of this memory.

Luxor stood completely still for a moment, digesting the scene.

— ...

— ...Fuck, the poor guy. He was married to this lunatic.

— ...

— No. I'm getting out of his head. Poor guy has suffered enough already.

He began to withdraw hastily, frantically looking for an exit, completely horrified by what he had just discovered.

Isidora, for her part, seeing Luxor quickly moving away from the memory, instantly understood what he had just seen.

— ...

— WAIT, YOU, DID YOU SEE THAT MEMORY?!

— I DON'T WANT TO KNOW ANYTHING ELSE, Luxor shouted, speeding up his escape through Lucifer's mind.

— NO BUT WAIT, I CAN EXPLAIN—

— NO, I DON'T WANT AN EXPLANATION, I JUST WANT TO GET OUT OF HERE NOW.

The two entities rushed toward the exit of Lucifer's mind at the same time, the mental space gradually closing behind them, until they abruptly reappeared in reality, Luxor still lodged in Lucifer's body, but visibly shaken by what he had just discovered.

— ...

81, Takeshi, Poppy and Agent 47 watched the scene in total incomprehension, the two entities panting, one visibly traumatized, the other visibly offended.

— ...What exactly happened in there, Takeshi asked, hesitant.

Luxor, still shaken, took a step back, the dagger trembling slightly in his hand.

— I saw things I will never be able to forget.

— IT WAS A VERY BEAUTIFUL MEMORY, Isidora immediately protested, crossing her arms indignantly.

— YOU MARRIED HIM, Luxor shouted, visibly still in a state of shock. LUCIFER MORNINGSTAR MARRIED ISIDORA. HOW COULD ANY BEING SURVIVE THAT.

81, completely overwhelmed by this totally unexpected new revelation, slowly turned to Poppy.

— ...Wait. They were MARRIED?

Poppy, her usual neutrality seriously put to the test for the second time that day, simply shrugged.

— Apparently, yes. And nobody knew.

Isidora, a finger on her chin, narrowed her eyes in a visibly sincere effort of concentration.

— Wait, was it the 678th marriage... or the 412th, I don't remember, uh...

— ...

A stunned silence greeted this totally unexpected detail, each member of the group slowly digesting the scale of the revelation that had just been added to the one they were still trying to understand.

— Maybe the 784th. Nah, dunno.

Takeshi, mouth half open, struggled to get the words out.

— Wait. You said the LAST marriage, the one that ended in divorce, was the 935th.

— Yeah, so?

— SO YOU'VE BEEN MARRIED 935 TIMES AND YOU DON'T REMEMBER WHICH ONE WAS WITH LUCIFER?!

— Well yeah, that one was special, I didn't really keep count at the time. Like, between the 400th and the 800th it's kinda fuzzy for me, that was my wild phase.

81, completely overwhelmed, turned to Lucifer's body, still controlled by Luxor, still visibly traumatized by his discovery.

— So basically, she's been married so many times she's literally lost track of which one was with you.

— I JUST SAW IT IN HIS MEMORIES, Luxor screamed, his voice betraying sincere disgust. HE REMEMBERS THAT MARRIAGE PERFECTLY. SHE'S THE ONE WHO HAD SO MANY UNIONS THAT SHE DOESN'T KNOW WHERE SHE STANDS ANYMORE.

— That was like... several centuries ago, Isidora pointed out, not troubled in the least. We were young and crazy back then.

— YOU PROBABLY SAID THAT ABOUT THE OTHER 934 TOO.

— OBVIOUSLY, IT'S ALWAYS TRUE.

Agent 47, unfazed in spite of everything, adjusted his weapon, his earpiece crackling.

— Riper. Check the archives for a possible marriage between Lucifer Morningstar and Isidora.

An abnormally long silence preceded the answer.

"...I found something."

— And?

"An official document, dated roughly three centuries ago. Marriage certificate. Both signatures are authentic. Registered union number: 719."

— ...

— AH, THERE WE GO, 719, THAT WAS IT! Isidora exclaimed, delighted, as if a cosmic mystery had finally been solved.

Poppy, her neutrality completely pulverized for the third time that day, slowly turned to her.

— How does someone get married 935 times.

— Easy, you find someone, you marry them, sometimes it lasts one night, sometimes a few centuries. Lucifer was a good customer, we lasted almost 200 years before the divorce.

Luxor, still visibly shaken, took another step back, the dagger still trembling in his hand.

— ...I sincerely think I'd rather face the Godslayer than stay locked in that head for one more second.

81, despite the gravity of the situation, couldn't help a bitter smirk.

— That can be arranged.

Isidora shrugged, not embarrassed in the least by the turn the conversation had taken.

— Well yeah, she went on, it was more of a booty call than anything else, but hey, it still lasted 7 days... well, 7 hours, the marriage. That's a start.

— ...

A heavy silence settled in, each member of the group slowly digesting this detail, which only added to the general absurdity.

Takeshi put a hand to his face, for the umpteenth time that day.

— The marriage lasted 7 hours.

— Yeah, we moved fast, Isidora specified, as if this information really clarified anything.

Luxor, still a prisoner in Lucifer's body, let out a nervous, slightly hysterical laugh.

— SO HE MARRIED SOMEONE, DIVORCED SEVEN HOURS LATER, AND HE'S KEPT THAT MEMORY PRECIOUSLY FOR THREE CENTURIES.

— Well yeah, it was a good memory, Isidora answered, as if it were absolutely obvious.

81, completely overwhelmed, slowly shook his head.

— I really have no words left at this point.

Agent 47, unfazed in spite of everything, nonetheless spoke up again.

— Riper. Confirm the exact duration of union number 719.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause.

"Confirmed. Duration of the marriage: 6 hours and 47 minutes, counting from the signing of the certificate to the filing of the divorce petition."

— SEE, I WAS ALMOST EXACTLY RIGHT, Isidora exclaimed, proud of herself in spite of everything.

Poppy, her neutrality definitively compromised for the day, turned to her with infinite weariness.

— That's the shortest marriage in the entire known history of the universe.

— NOT AT ALL, I've had shorter ones. There was one that lasted like 12 minutes.

— ...WHY, Takeshi immediately exclaimed, unable to stop himself.

— We got married, we looked at each other, we said "actually, nah", and we divorced right away. Efficient.

Luxor, still locked in Lucifer's body, shook his head in total distress.

— I really, sincerely want to get out of this head now. Whatever it costs me.

81, slowly raising his sword, a fierce smile forming despite the total absurdity of the previous conversation.

— Good timing. I was just about to help you with that.

Luxor, visibly totally overwhelmed by what he had just discovered, hastily stepped back, a trembling hand rising in front of him.

— ...I'm outta here, bless him. He's already suffered 7 hours with her, that's too much.

A dark portal began to materialize behind him, a crack in reality hastily opening.

— ...

81, instantly understanding the escape attempt, charged immediately.

— OH NO YOU DON'T GET TO RUN OFF LIKE THAT!

— YES I DO, Luxor answered, already rushing toward the portal, Lucifer's body moving with total urgency. I'VE SEEN THINGS NO ENTITY SHOULD EVER SEE. I'M LEAVING.

Isidora, hearing the remark, exploded with indignation.

— HEY, IT WAS A BEAUTIFUL MARRIAGE, EVEN IF IT ONLY LASTED SEVEN HOURS!

— THAT IS PRECISELY THE PROBLEM, Luxor screamed, diving into the portal just before 81 could reach him, the crack closing instantly behind him.

— ...

Silence fell over the group again, 81 frozen, his sword pointed at the empty space where Luxor had been a few seconds earlier.

— ...He bailed.

— He literally preferred to run away rather than spend one more second with the memory of a married Isidora, Takeshi summed up, still in shock.

Lucifer's body, now freed of Luxor, suddenly collapsed to its knees, inert for a moment, before gradually regaining consciousness, his own eyes slowly opening again.

— ...

81 immediately rushed over to him.

— Lucifer? Is that you?

Lucifer blinked several times, a hand on his head, total confusion crossing his still-magnificent face.

— ...I have a monumental headache and the strange feeling that someone just went digging through my most embarrassing memories.

Isidora, beaming, rushed over in turn, hugging him without the slightest embarrassment.

— LULU, YOU'RE ALIVE!

— ...Isidora, why do I get the feeling Luxor saw the wedding.

— ...

An awkward silence settled in, Isidora pulling back slightly, an innocent but totally unconvincing smile on her face.

— What wedding?

— ISIDORA.

— OKAY, MAYBE HE SAW IT A LITTLE.

Lucifer put both hands to his face, a moan of pure distress escaping him.

— Great. On top of almost dying, everyone now knows about our seven-hour union.

81, an amused smile forming despite the tension of the day, crossed his arms.

— Don't worry, Lulu. We'll keep it between us.

"Technically," Reaper immediately cut in, "the livestream is still broadcasting live. Several trillion viewers have also just learned this information."

— ...

Lucifer froze for a moment, slowly digesting this additional detail, before flopping all the way back onto the ground, completely defeated by this decidedly endless day.

— I regret coming back.

Luxor, still visibly shaken, took another step back, the dagger still trembling in his hand. — ...I sincerely think I'd rather face the Godslayer than stay locked in that head for one more second. 81, despite the gravity of the situation, couldn't help a bitter smirk. — That can be arranged. Isidora shrugged, not embarrassed in the least by the turn the conversation had taken. — Well yeah, she went on, it was more of a booty call than anything else, but hey, it still lasted 7 days... well, 7 hours, the marriage. That's a start. — ... A heavy silence settled in, each member of the group slowly digesting this detail, which only added to the general absurdity. Takeshi put a hand to his face, for the umpteenth time that day. — The marriage lasted 7 hours. — Yeah, we moved fast, Isidora specified, as if this information really clarified anything. Luxor, still a prisoner in Lucifer's body, let out a nervous, slightly hysterical laugh. — SO HE MARRIED SOMEONE, DIVORCED SEVEN HOURS LATER, AND HE'S KEPT THAT MEMORY PRECIOUSLY FOR THREE CENTURIES. — Well yeah, it was a good memory, Isidora answered, as if it were absolutely obvious. 81, completely overwhelmed, slowly shook his head. — I really have no words left at this point. Agent 47, unfazed in spite of everything, nonetheless spoke up again. — Riper. Confirm the exact duration of union number 719. "Analysis in progress..." A pause. "Confirmed. Duration of the marriage: 6 hours and 47 minutes, counting from the signing of the certificate to the filing of the divorce petition." — SEE, I WAS ALMOST EXACTLY RIGHT, Isidora exclaimed, proud of herself in spite of everything. Poppy, her neutrality definitively compromised for the day, turned to her with infinite weariness. — That's the shortest marriage in the entire known history of the universe. — NOT AT ALL, I've had shorter ones. There was one that lasted like 12 minutes. — ...WHY, Takeshi immediately exclaimed, unable to stop himself. — We got married, we looked at each other, we said "actually, nah", and we divorced right away. Efficient. Luxor, still locked in Lucifer's body, shook his head in total distress. — I really, sincerely want to get out of this head now. Whatever it costs me. 81, slowly raising his sword, a fierce smile forming despite the total absurdity of the previous conversation. — Good timing. I was just about to help you with that. Luxor, visibly totally overwhelmed by what he had just discovered, hastily stepped back, a trembling hand rising in front of him. — ...I'm outta here, bless him. He's already suffered 7 hours with her, that's too much. A dark portal began to materialize behind him, a crack in reality hastily opening. — ... 81, instantly understanding the escape attempt, charged immediately. — OH NO YOU DON'T GET TO RUN OFF LIKE THAT! — YES I DO, Luxor answered, already rushing toward the portal, Lucifer's body moving with total urgency. I'VE SEEN THINGS NO ENTITY SHOULD EVER SEE. I'M LEAVING. Isidora, hearing the remark, exploded with indignation. — HEY, IT WAS A BEAUTIFUL MARRIAGE, EVEN IF IT ONLY LASTED SEVEN HOURS! — THAT IS PRECISELY THE PROBLEM, Luxor screamed, diving into the portal just before 81 could reach him, the crack closing instantly behind him. — ... Silence fell over the group again, 81 frozen, his sword pointed at the empty space where Luxor had been a few seconds earlier. — ...He bailed. — He literally preferred to run away rather than spend one more second with the memory of a married Isidora, Takeshi summed up, still in shock. Lucifer's body, now freed of Luxor, suddenly collapsed to its knees, inert for a moment, before gradually regaining consciousness, his own eyes slowly opening again. — ... 81 immediately rushed over to him. — Lucifer? Is that you? Lucifer blinked several times, a hand on his head, total confusion crossing his still-magnificent face. — ...I have a monumental headache and the strange feeling that someone just went digging through my most embarrassing memories. Isidora, beaming, rushed over in turn, hugging him without the slightest embarrassment. — LULU, YOU'RE ALIVE! — ...Isidora, why do I get the feeling Luxor saw the wedding. — ... An awkward silence settled in, Isidora pulling back slightly, an innocent but totally unconvincing smile on her face. — What wedding? — ISIDORA. — OKAY, MAYBE HE SAW IT A LITTLE. Lucifer put both hands to his face, a moan of pure distress escaping him. — Great. On top of almost dying, everyone now knows about our seven-hour union. 81, an amused smile forming despite the tension of the day, crossed his arms. — Don't worry, Lulu. We'll keep it between us. "Technically," Reaper immediately cut in, "the livestream is still broadcasting live. Several trillion viewers have also just learned this information." — ... Lucifer froze for a moment, slowly digesting this additional detail, before flopping all the way back onto the ground, completely defeated by this decidedly endless day. — I regret coming back.

codex-t4-c4.title: Chapter 3 — Oh, What a Dumbass!
codex-t4-c4.html:
Lucifer, slowly sitting up, a resigned sigh running through his whole being, turned to the group, still hanging on this revelation.

— Okay, Isidora. We tell them, we don't have a choice.

— ...You sure? We could like, change the subject, offer food, distract everyone—

— ISIDORA.

— OKAY OKAY.

Lucifer took a deep breath, as if gathering all the courage he needed to face this moment.

— Our marriage was simple. We saw each other, we got married, we screwed, and then we looked at each other and held back from murdering each other before getting divorced.

— ...

A total silence greeted this almost brutally simple explanation.

Takeshi, mouth half open, took a long moment before managing to get anything out.

— ...That's it? That's the whole story?

— Yep, Lucifer confirmed with a shrug.

— Seven hours to do all that, Isidora pointed out, as if the timing deserved to be highlighted.

81, slowly shaking his head, let out a bitter, incredulous laugh.

— You met, got married, slept together and got divorced, all in seven hours.

— Efficient, right? Isidora answered, proud as ever.

— That's not efficient, it's just... fast and completely devoid of logic, Poppy managed, her neutrality definitively abandoned for the day.

Lucifer, massaging his temples, went on nonetheless.

— We ran into each other in a bar. We drank. A lot. We found the idea hilarious at the time. The next morning — well, a few hours later — we looked at each other and collectively realized it was probably the worst idea of our respective existences.

— Like, we couldn't even stand each other when we woke up, Isidora added, with disarming naturalness.

— So we divorced right away, Lucifer concluded. No hard feelings. We stayed buddies afterward.

Agent 47, unfazed as always, merely adjusted his weapon.

— Riper. Add this story to Lucifer and Isidora's joint file.

"Already done. I would also point out that this anecdote has officially just broken the previous record for 'most anticlimactic revelation of the day'."

Grand Patron Luigi, still comfortably seated on his pile of corpses, applauded warmly, a big smile on his lips.

— That's beautiful. Absolutely beautiful. Seven hours of marriage, and the only real antagonist of this story is your own personality incompatibility.

Lucifer, exhausted, flopped back down once again.

— So this day will never end.

— Nope, Isidora confirmed, with unshakable enthusiasm. Okay, now that we've sorted that out, can we get back to the party?

81 crossed his arms, an uncompromising firmness crossing his one-eyed gaze.

— No.

— ...

— Lucifer's alive. So no party.

Isidora stayed silent for a moment, digesting the implacable logic of the argument.

— ...Okay, she finally sighed, without the slightest objection, as if the rule were perfectly obvious once stated.

Takeshi, still in shock from everything that had just happened, turned to 81 in total disbelief.

— Wait, she just gives up like that?

— It's pure logic, Isidora explained with a shrug. The party was to celebrate his death. He's not dead. So no party. QED.

Lucifer, still lying on the ground, exhausted, weakly raised a hand.

— Thank you for being alive, Isidora. Really. It means something to me that my survival finally comes before a party.

— It's only natural, she answered, with an almost touching seriousness. You alive is worth more than any cosmic party.

— ...

A tender silence settled in for a moment, almost sincere, before Isidora immediately went back to her usual tone.

— PLUS NOW WE GET TO THROW A REAL PARTY FOR YOUR RETURN, EVEN BETTER THAN THE LAST ONE!

— ...

Lucifer closed his eyes, a moan of total despair escaping him.

— I should've stayed in Akuma's domain.

— TOO LATE, YOU'RE BACK, WE'RE CELEBRATING!

81, shaking his head, dropped down onto the nearest rubble, total weariness running through his whole being.

— We'll never get a break with her.

— Never, Poppy confirmed, without the slightest trace of surprise in her voice.

Grand Patron Luigi, delighted beyond measure by this new twist, poured himself another glass of champagne.

— This is officially the best day of my life. And I'm 300,000 years old.

Isidora, calmly walking away from the group without a single glance back, plunged her hand into her cloak with total nonchalance.

— ...

She pulled out a brand-new phone, apparently the fiftieth of the day, the old one probably having ended up smashed somewhere after she dropped it during her traumatic scream.

Takeshi, noticing the gesture, turned to her, incredulous.

— How many phones do you have in that cloak exactly?

— Dunno, never counted, she answered, already turning on the screen with renewed enthusiasm. Okay, I gotta post a story announcing Lulu's alive, my followers are gonna be devastated to find out the party's cancelled.

— You literally just left everyone hanging to grab a phone.

— IT'S IMPORTANT, she protested, already typing frantically. Gotta keep the people informed.

Lucifer, still lying on the ground, weakly raised his head.

— Isidora, I almost died, maybe you could stay with me for two minutes instead of—

— YEAH YEAH, ONE SEC, she cut in, completely focused on her screen, already composing the first words of her story.

LULU'S ALIVE SORRY ABOUT THE PARTY BUT HEY AT LEAST I FOUND OUT I WAS MARRIED TO HIM FOR 7H SO THE DAY ISN'T A TOTAL LOSS #ExpressWedding #LuluIsHot #ImHungry

81, watching the scene from his seat on the rubble, slowly shook his head.

— She literally just turned a near-tragedy into viral content in thirty seconds.

— That's her thing, Poppy answered, resigned.

Isidora, satisfied with her post, finally looked up, a radiant smile on her lips.

— Okay, so, what do we do now?

— We could perhaps discuss the next step to save Takeshi's father, Agent 47 suggested, unfazed as always.

— YES BUT FIRST, Isidora immediately cut in, putting her phone away just as quickly as she'd taken it out, I'M HUNGRY.

A collective, resigned silence greeted this declaration, no one even seeming surprised at this point in the day.

Lucifer, still on the ground, let out an exhausted but sincere laugh in spite of everything.

— You know what. I missed a lot of things while I was captured. But apparently I didn't miss anything at all mood-wise.

— EXACTLY, Isidora confirmed, finally helping him up with an unexpected tenderness beneath her nonchalant airs. Welcome back, Lulu.

(Read the special episode to understand what comes next: Where Was That Damn Incarnation?)

Aravos, still leaning against a ruined section of wall, slowly caught his breath before beginning his story, the whole group hanging on his every word.

— Morganne. My sister.

— ...

— She's been harvesting souls for millennia. To become more powerful. For pleasure, too.

Takeshi, still wary but visibly captivated, came a little closer.

— Have you two hated each other for a long time?

— Ever since she laughed at my daughter's death, Aravos answered, his voice instantly hardening. She didn't like her. So when 81 killed her...

He shot a quick look at 81, an old tension still present despite the current situation.

— ...she found it hilarious.

— I get her, Isidora said in the background, on her phone.

81 crossed his arms, his expression remaining neutral despite the obvious gravity of the subject.

— Go on.

— I knew I could never have gotten revenge on her alone. So I left.

Lucifer, still on the ground but attentively following the conversation, frowned.

— But she, apparently, had other plans.

— She wanted to kill me from the start, Aravos confirmed, a deep bitterness crossing his voice. Absorb my soul. I didn't even know until she showed up in front of me a few hours ago.

Poppy, coldly analyzing every word, stepped forward.

— And now, with the Assimilated's powers on top of that.

— Now, she's almost untouchable, Aravos confirmed. And the worst part is it will never stop.

— What do you mean, Isidora asked, serious for once.

Aravos finally lifted his head all the way, his gaze heavy with an icy certainty.

— Morganne will never stop wanting more. It's in her deepest nature. Every soul absorbed, every power stolen, only fuels her thirst. She knows no limit. She never has.

— ...

— As long as she doesn't die, she will remain a threat. Growing. Perpetual. She'll end up going after everything that exists, simply because she can.

81, his one-eyed gaze fixed intensely on Aravos, let a heavy silence pass before speaking again.

— So basically, the only solution is to kill her.

— The only solution, Aravos confirmed, is to kill her before she becomes literally impossible to stop.

Agent 47, unfazed as always, adjusted his weapon, his earpiece already crackling.

— Riper. Threat assessment based on the information provided.

An unusually long pause preceded the answer.

"Analysis in progress... If the information is accurate, this entity could represent a threat comparable to, or even greater than, that of the Assimilated before his absorption."

— Great, Takeshi breathed, the tension visibly growing in him.

Isidora, crossing her arms, an unusual seriousness still on her face, turned to Aravos.

— And where is she now, your psycho sister?

— I don't know, Aravos admitted, a hint of fear finally piercing openly through his voice. But knowing her nature, it won't be long before she goes looking for her next target.

Isidora, despite the relative seriousness of the conversation, pulled her phone out again with disarming ease, the screen already lighting up.

— Okay, I gotta inform the people about this new twist.

— ISIDORA, Takeshi immediately protested, we're in the middle of an existential crisis here.

— Exactly, this is precisely the kind of content people want to see.

She quickly framed the scene, Aravos still slumped against his ruined wall, visible in the background.

NEW COSMIC THREAT ALERT — some chick killed the Assimilated in like 10 seconds and now she wants to kill her own brother #MorganneVsTeamGang #ShitsAboutToGoDown

Meanwhile, Agent 47, still focused on tactical analysis, spoke up again.

— Riper. Comparative calculation of Morganne's threat level.

"Analysis in progress..."

A pause longer than usual, the data visibly complex to process.

"Result obtained. Integrating her base power, plus the complete absorption of the Assimilated's powers and soul, Morganne could currently be classified as equivalent to a Higher Incarnation of rank 3 at minimum."

— ...

81 instantly turned to Aravos, a new gravity crossing his one-eyed gaze.

— Rank 3. That's already higher than the Assimilated himself.

"Confirmed," Reaper specified. "Before his absorption, the Assimilated was generally considered to sit below rank 3 in the hierarchy of the Higher Incarnations. Morganne now surpasses him, without even taking into account her natural progression if she keeps absorbing other sources of power."

Poppy, her usual neutrality slightly cracked by the scale of the revelation, crossed her arms.

— So she's already stronger than what's given us the most trouble so far.

— And she clearly has no intention of stopping there, Aravos added, a sincere terror crossing his exhausted face.

Lucifer, still on the ground but attentively following every word, let out a nervous, desperate laugh.

— Great. Really great. We've barely finished one crisis and another, even worse one, is already on its way.

Isidora, finishing her story with visible satisfaction, finally put her phone away, her seriousness gradually returning.

— Okay, people are hyped. Now, seriously, what do we do?

81, tightening his grip on his sword, his gaze fixed on the horizon with cold determination, as if he could already sense the growing threat somewhere in the universe.

— We find her. And we stop her before she reaches rank 2.

Agent 47, raising his hand to his earpiece, relayed the answer he had just received, his unfazed tone betraying no particular surprise.

— Grand Patron Luigi refuses to help directly.

— ...

81 turned to him, a frown crossing his face.

— He refuses? Like, literally?

— His exact message, 47 specified, checking his earpiece again.

"Isidora, film more toward the left, the lighting's dimmer, perfect for the dramatic mood."

— ...

A stunned silence greeted this completely off-topic answer.

Takeshi put a hand to his face, used to it by now but still just as overwhelmed.

— We're talking about a rank 3 cosmic threat and his only contribution is advice on video framing.

— That's Grand Patron Luigi all over, Lucifer commented, still lying on the ground, exhausted.

Isidora, hearing the remark, immediately turned to the left, instinctively adjusting the angle of her imaginary phone.

— WAIT, HE'S RIGHT, the light's way better on this side.

— ISIDORA, WE'RE TALKING STRATEGY HERE, Takeshi exclaimed, exasperated.

— WE CAN DO BOTH, she answered, sincerely convinced.

Poppy, her patience visibly sorely tested, turned to 47.

— He gave no other indication? No reason for his refusal?

47 checked his earpiece one last time.

— Riper specifies that Grand Patron Luigi considers this situation "excellent entertainment to watch rather than to influence directly".

— ...

81, gritting his teeth, a growing frustration crossing his one-eyed gaze.

— So basically, he's watching us like content, again, instead of helping us against a threat capable of destroying Higher Incarnations.

"Confirmed," Reaper added, with what almost sounded like shared resignation. "Grand Patron Luigi maintains his policy of non-direct intervention, unless the situation becomes, and I quote, 'way too hilarious not to get involved'."

Aravos, still exhausted but attentively following the exchange, let out a bitter laugh.

— Great. The most powerful being in this universe refuses to help us because he'd rather watch us like a reality TV show.

— Welcome to our daily life, 81 answered, tightening his grip on his sword, a cold determination gradually replacing his frustration. We're gonna have to handle this ourselves, as usual.

Lucifer painfully got back up, still marked by the day's events, just as an explosion suddenly tore through the sky — identical to the one that had announced the Assimilated's return, but this time tinged with a golden glint cutting through the black and red flames.

— ...

A figure materialized in the heart of this blast, calmly floating in the air, its golden armor glittering in the ambient light.

Morganne.

— OH, WHAT A DUMBASS! Isidora immediately shouted, pointing at the figure in the sky, not impressed in the least by her theatrical entrance.

— SHUT UP! 81, Takeshi, Lucifer, Poppy and Aravos instantly screamed in unison, all at the same time.

Agent 47, the only one who hadn't shouted, remained perfectly silent, his weapon already pointed at the sky, his tactical analysis already under way.

— ...

Morganne, still floating above them, slowly turned her head toward the assembled group, an amused smile forming on her face, framed by her golden helmet.

— Well, well. What a lovely little welcoming committee.

Her gaze settled directly on Aravos, still weakened, a gleam of cruel satisfaction crossing her piercing green eyes.

— I see you've found new friends, dear brother. How touching.

Aravos, despite his exhaustion, straightened up as much as he could, a desperate determination crossing his gaze.

— Morganne.

— Did you really think you could hide behind them? she asked, slowly descending toward the ground, her golden aura radiating a new and terrifying power.

81, fully drawing his two swords, took a determined step forward, deliberately placing himself between Aravos and Morganne.

— He's not hiding. He's just got backup now.

Morganne finally set foot on the ground, her gaze slowly sliding over each member of the group, a cold, calculated assessment crossing her expression.

— The Godslayer in person. I've heard about you.

— ...

— Let's see if your reputation is deserved, she added, her golden energy sphere already beginning to form in her palm, the fight looking inevitable.

A portal abruptly materialized right in the middle of the scene, Grand Patron Luigi calmly appearing, completely indifferent to the palpable tension that had reigned a few seconds earlier.

— Excuse me, I forgot my bottle.

— ...

He casually pointed at a bottle of champagne still sitting on the rubble not far away, strolling toward it without the slightest haste.

Morganne, already in motion, her attack launched before she even noticed this unexpected appearance, hurled a massive discharge of golden energy straight at the ground, the explosion ringing out violently all around them.

— ...

Grand Patron Luigi, right in the middle of the impact, remained perfectly still, the blast dispersing around him without the slightest effect, as if he simply didn't exist on the same plane of reality as the surrounding chaos.

He calmly picked up his bottle of champagne, making a slight movement of his hand to dust a few particles off his suit, completely unfazed.

— ...

The whole group, still shaken by the explosion, stood frozen, staring at the scene in total disbelief.

— ...He literally just ignored a rank 3 attack, Takeshi managed, his voice trembling.

Morganne herself, visibly thrown for the first time since her arrival, stared at Grand Patron Luigi with a new suspicion.

— ...Who are you.

He barely turned toward her, a polite but completely detached smile crossing his face.

— Nobody important. I was just stopping by to pick this up.

He lifted his bottle slightly in a casual salute, before calmly turning around, already walking away toward a new portal that had just opened behind him.

— ...

— WAIT, YOU'RE LEAVING NOW? Takeshi shouted, completely overwhelmed by this new twist.

— Yep, Grand Patron Luigi simply answered, without even turning around. Good luck with her, honestly.

He disappeared through the portal, which closed instantly behind him, leaving the whole group facing Morganne, more stunned than anyone by what had just happened.

— ...

81, the first to regain his composure, tightened his grip on his swords, his one-eyed gaze turning back to Morganne.

— Okay. We carry on without him, apparently.

Morganne, still visibly troubled by this utterly absurd interruption, shook her head slightly, gradually regaining her usual confidence.

— ...Whoever that was, it doesn't matter. Let's continue.

Isidora, crossing her arms, an unusual seriousness still on her face, turned to Aravos. — And where is she now, your psycho sister? — I don't know, Aravos admitted, a hint of fear finally piercing openly through his voice. But knowing her nature, it won't be long before she goes looking for her next target. Isidora, despite the relative seriousness of the conversation, pulled her phone out again with disarming ease, the screen already lighting up. — Okay, I gotta inform the people about this new twist. — ISIDORA, Takeshi immediately protested, we're in the middle of an existential crisis here. — Exactly, this is precisely the kind of content people want to see. She quickly framed the scene, Aravos still slumped against his ruined wall, visible in the background. NEW COSMIC THREAT ALERT — some chick killed the Assimilated in like 10 seconds and now she wants to kill her own brother #MorganneVsTeamGang #ShitsAboutToGoDown Meanwhile, Agent 47, still focused on tactical analysis, spoke up again. — Riper. Comparative calculation of Morganne's threat level. "Analysis in progress..." A pause longer than usual, the data visibly complex to process. "Result obtained. Integrating her base power, plus the complete absorption of the Assimilated's powers and soul, Morganne could currently be classified as equivalent to a Higher Incarnation of rank 3 at minimum." — ... 81 instantly turned to Aravos, a new gravity crossing his one-eyed gaze. — Rank 3. That's already higher than the Assimilated himself. "Confirmed," Reaper specified. "Before his absorption, the Assimilated was generally considered to sit below rank 3 in the hierarchy of the Higher Incarnations. Morganne now surpasses him, without even taking into account her natural progression if she keeps absorbing other sources of power." Poppy, her usual neutrality slightly cracked by the scale of the revelation, crossed her arms. — So she's already stronger than what's given us the most trouble so far. — And she clearly has no intention of stopping there, Aravos added, a sincere terror crossing his exhausted face. Lucifer, still on the ground but attentively following every word, let out a nervous, desperate laugh. — Great. Really great. We've barely finished one crisis and another, even worse one, is already on its way. Isidora, finishing her story with visible satisfaction, finally put her phone away, her seriousness gradually returning. — Okay, people are hyped. Now, seriously, what do we do? 81, tightening his grip on his sword, his gaze fixed on the horizon with cold determination, as if he could already sense the growing threat somewhere in the universe. — We find her. And we stop her before she reaches rank 2. Agent 47, raising his hand to his earpiece, relayed the answer he had just received, his unfazed tone betraying no particular surprise. — Grand Patron Luigi refuses to help directly. — ... 81 turned to him, a frown crossing his face. — He refuses? Like, literally? — His exact message, 47 specified, checking his earpiece again. "Isidora, film more toward the left, the lighting's dimmer, perfect for the dramatic mood." — ... A stunned silence greeted this completely off-topic answer. Takeshi put a hand to his face, used to it by now but still just as overwhelmed. — We're talking about a rank 3 cosmic threat and his only contribution is advice on video framing. — That's Grand Patron Luigi all over, Lucifer commented, still lying on the ground, exhausted. Isidora, hearing the remark, immediately turned to the left, instinctively adjusting the angle of her imaginary phone. — WAIT, HE'S RIGHT, the light's way better on this side. — ISIDORA, WE'RE TALKING STRATEGY HERE, Takeshi exclaimed, exasperated. — WE CAN DO BOTH, she answered, sincerely convinced. Poppy, her patience visibly sorely tested, turned to 47. — He gave no other indication? No reason for his refusal? 47 checked his earpiece one last time. — Riper specifies that Grand Patron Luigi considers this situation "excellent entertainment to watch rather than to influence directly". — ... 81, gritting his teeth, a growing frustration crossing his one-eyed gaze. — So basically, he's watching us like content, again, instead of helping us against a threat capable of destroying Higher Incarnations. "Confirmed," Reaper added, with what almost sounded like shared resignation. "Grand Patron Luigi maintains his policy of non-direct intervention, unless the situation becomes, and I quote, 'way too hilarious not to get involved'." Aravos, still exhausted but attentively following the exchange, let out a bitter laugh. — Great. The most powerful being in this universe refuses to help us because he'd rather watch us like a reality TV show. — Welcome to our daily life, 81 answered, tightening his grip on his sword, a cold determination gradually replacing his frustration. We're gonna have to handle this ourselves, as usual. Lucifer painfully got back up, still marked by the day's events, just as an explosion suddenly tore through the sky — identical to the one that had announced the Assimilated's return, but this time tinged with a golden glint cutting through the black and red flames. — ... A figure materialized in the heart of this blast, calmly floating in the air, its golden armor glittering in the ambient light. Morganne. — OH, WHAT A DUMBASS! Isidora immediately shouted, pointing at the figure in the sky, not impressed in the least by her theatrical entrance. — SHUT UP! 81, Takeshi, Lucifer, Poppy and Aravos instantly screamed in unison, all at the same time. Agent 47, the only one who hadn't shouted, remained perfectly silent, his weapon already pointed at the sky, his tactical analysis already under way. — ... Morganne, still floating above them, slowly turned her head toward the assembled group, an amused smile forming on her face, framed by her golden helmet. — Well, well. What a lovely little welcoming committee. Her gaze settled directly on Aravos, still weakened, a gleam of cruel satisfaction crossing her piercing green eyes. — I see you've found new friends, dear brother. How touching. Aravos, despite his exhaustion, straightened up as much as he could, a desperate determination crossing his gaze. — Morganne. — Did you really think you could hide behind them? she asked, slowly descending toward the ground, her golden aura radiating a new and terrifying power. 81, fully drawing his two swords, took a determined step forward, deliberately placing himself between Aravos and Morganne. — He's not hiding. He's just got backup now. Morganne finally set foot on the ground, her gaze slowly sliding over each member of the group, a cold, calculated assessment crossing her expression. — The Godslayer in person. I've heard about you. — ... — Let's see if your reputation is deserved, she added, her golden energy sphere already beginning to form in her palm, the fight looking inevitable. A portal abruptly materialized right in the middle of the scene, Grand Patron Luigi calmly appearing, completely indifferent to the palpable tension that had reigned a few seconds earlier. — Excuse me, I forgot my bottle. — ... He casually pointed at a bottle of champagne still sitting on the rubble not far away, strolling toward it without the slightest haste. Morganne, already in motion, her attack launched before she even noticed this unexpected appearance, hurled a massive discharge of golden energy straight at the ground, the explosion ringing out violently all around them. — ... Grand Patron Luigi, right in the middle of the impact, remained perfectly still, the blast dispersing around him without the slightest effect, as if he simply didn't exist on the same plane of reality as the surrounding chaos. He calmly picked up his bottle of champagne, making a slight movement of his hand to dust a few particles off his suit, completely unfazed. — ... The whole group, still shaken by the explosion, stood frozen, staring at the scene in total disbelief. — ...He literally just ignored a rank 3 attack, Takeshi managed, his voice trembling. Morganne herself, visibly thrown for the first time since her arrival, stared at Grand Patron Luigi with a new suspicion. — ...Who are you. He barely turned toward her, a polite but completely detached smile crossing his face. — Nobody important. I was just stopping by to pick this up. He lifted his bottle slightly in a casual salute, before calmly turning around, already walking away toward a new portal that had just opened behind him. — ... — WAIT, YOU'RE LEAVING NOW? Takeshi shouted, completely overwhelmed by this new twist. — Yep, Grand Patron Luigi simply answered, without even turning around. Good luck with her, honestly. He disappeared through the portal, which closed instantly behind him, leaving the whole group facing Morganne, more stunned than anyone by what had just happened. — ... 81, the first to regain his composure, tightened his grip on his swords, his one-eyed gaze turning back to Morganne. — Okay. We carry on without him, apparently. Morganne, still visibly troubled by this utterly absurd interruption, shook her head slightly, gradually regaining her usual confidence. — ...Whoever that was, it doesn't matter. Let's continue.

codex-t4-c5.title: Chapter 4 — New Bitch in the Universe
codex-t4-c5.html:
The doors of the Throne Room opened without Akuma needing to look up. Void came in, his fog of hallucinations creeping over the marble ahead of him.

— ...

— You really insist on bothering me, Void.

— The Assimilated hasn't come back.

Akuma remained motionless in front of the empty throne, her gaze still fixed on the door of reality open before her.

— He left with a precise order. Come back with a victory or don't come back.

— That was hours ago. Even half dead, he would have walked through those doors by now. If only to come crying.

— ...

Akuma finally turned her head. A slight crease crossed her impassive face.

— Have you looked for him?

— I can't sense him anymore.

— Say that again.

— No more signature. No more trace. As if chaos had deserted the universe. This isn't running away, Akuma. When he hides, I can still sense him. Now, there's nothing left.

— ...

Akuma closed her eyes for a second. She searched for what Void had just described, and found nothing.

— He's dead.

— Impossible. No one kills the Assimilated. Except Isidora, and she doesn't have the time between two hashtags.

— No one kills a Higher Incarnation. And yet.

— ...

The doors slammed against the walls.

Ignis strode in. Flames ran along his arms without ever going out, more agitated than usual.

— A fight has just broken out, he announced without a glance at Void. Where the Godslayer's group is.

— We know, Akuma cut in. That's not new.

— They're not the point.

— ...

— Their opponent. I sensed her signature from where I was. It's not someone we know.

— Be specific.

Ignis clenched his fist. The flames rose a notch.

— She has the same powers as the Assimilated. The same chaos. Exactly.

— ...

Void took a step back. His fog wavered.

— She has what?

— The Assimilated's chaos. I recognized it. You don't mistake that kind of power for anything else.

— So that's it, Void breathed. It's not that he ran away. It was taken from him.

— ...

Akuma didn't move. But the whole hall grew colder, as if death itself had just stepped back.

— Only one entity can steal the power of a Higher Incarnation, she murmured. And she shouldn't exist.

— So she's stronger than him, Ignis concluded.

— Not stronger, Akuma corrected. Stronger now.

She turned away from the throne, her right hand slowly opening. Black smoke curled around her fingers.

— Get ready. I will not let anyone take KJ's chaos for themselves in this Palace.

Akuma closed her hand. The black smoke died out all at once.

— Ignis. Glacius. Void.

Glacius's name hadn't finished echoing when an icy breath swept through the hall. Frost crept over the marble, and Glacius appeared beside Ignis. The flames of one and the cold of the other clashed without ever mixing.

— ...

— You will go after the thief.

Ignis smiled, and the heat rose a notch throughout the hall.

— With pleasure.

— Alive, if possible. What she stole doesn't belong to her, and I want it back intact. If she refuses to give it back, you'll take it from a corpse.

— ...

— The Godslayer's group is on site. If they get in the way, you know what to do.

Void didn't move. His fog had frozen on the floor, as if it too hesitated to obey.

— You're sending me.

— You were the first to complain about the Assimilated's absence. Go avenge him.

— And you stay here, doing nothing?

Akuma's gaze settled on him. The temperature dropped further, and even Glacius flinched slightly.

— Someone has to guard this Palace. Someone has to guard what's inside it.

— ...

— You wanted to command, Void? Start by obeying.

A sneer twisted Void's face, closer to a grimace than a smile. His fog began to move again, slowly, with barely veiled contempt.

— As you wish... Boss.

Glacius took a step forward, and the frost cracked under his feet. For the first time since he came in, his voice rang out, dry as broken ice.

— She killed the Assimilated.

— ...

— That changes the math.

— Then all three of you will go, Akuma decided. Not just one.

Ignis cracked his knuckles, and sparks shot from his fingers.

— This is gonna be fun.

— Don't underestimate this woman. The Assimilated didn't lose to a stranger: he lost to someone who knew exactly how to take him.

She raised her hand. A black crack tore through the air in front of them, a passage cut into reality, its edges curling like burnt paper.

— Go.

Ignis went in first, his flames briefly lighting up the inside of the rift. Glacius followed, the frost spreading behind him all the way to the threshold. Void lingered a second longer, his eyes fixed on Akuma.

— ...

— A problem?

— None. Just a remark... When I come back with her head, don't ask me to thank you.

He disappeared into the rift without waiting for an answer. The passage closed with a sharp snap.

The Throne Room fell back into an almost total calm. Akuma stood motionless for a long moment before the empty throne, without looking at it, without going near it.

— ...

Then she slowly turned her head toward another door, more discreet, at the back of the hall. A door none of the three Incarnations had noticed on their way in.

Behind it, something moved.

Morganne was advancing through the middle of the battlefield as if the fight didn't exist.

A golden volley. 81 crosses his blades to deflect it, the impact sends him sliding ten meters, his heels plowing through the rubble.

— ...

— Again? You bore me, Godslayer.

He charges. Two swords, an angle she can't see. The blade slices her arm, a clean line of golden blood.

— There! Got you!

— Watch closely.

The wound closes on its own. A shiver of chaos runs over Morganne's skin, then nothing, not even a scar.

— ...Fuck.

— Annoying, isn't it? All that power you've absorbed, and it only serves to hurt you for nothing.

Lucifer bursts out on her flank, a lance of infernal shadows already extended. Morganne barely lifts two fingers. The lance shatters. Lucifer is thrown back, rolls in the dust, gets back up spitting.

— She didn't even look at me!

— Move!

Agent 47 fires three times. Three engraved bullets, only one hits, right in the shoulder. Golden blood spurts, the wound closes immediately.

— Riper. Analysis.

"Instant regeneration. Origin identified: the Assimilated's chaos. Every bit of damage is rewritten as if it had never happened."

— Then how do we kill her.

"...I don't have an answer yet."

— Great! Lucifer yells, diving behind a ruined wall, a spray of golden energy pulverizing the spot where he had stood a second earlier.

Morganne laughs. A crystalline, effortless laugh.

— This is the famous group that made the Assimilated run? You can't even touch me.

81 takes a blow to the side, steps back, breathes. His 621 hearts are pounding wildly. He looks up at her, gauges the distance, calculates.

— We gotta find something. Fast.

— I'm open to any idea! Lucifer answers from his cover.

Off to the side, Takeshi and Poppy watch the scene, powerless. Aravos leans against a pillar, too weak to fight.

And Isidora?

Sitting on a concrete block, legs crossed, she's working through a bag of chips that just appeared from her cloak. Her phone is propped against her knee.

— ISIDORA!

— What?

— WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!

— Waiting to see if you guys make it. I don't feel like wearing myself out for nothing.

— SHE'S SLAUGHTERING US!

— Yeah, I can see that. You're not bad, you dodge well.

Morganne finally turns her head toward her. A flash of irritation passes through her green eyes.

— You.

— Me?

— You don't move. You don't scream. You don't run. It's strange.

— That's my style.

— ...

Morganne's smile freezes for half a second.

Then the air tears open.

A black crack opens in the middle of the battlefield. Its edges curl like burnt paper.

— ...

Everyone stops. Even 81 lowers his blades a notch.

A wave of heat bursts out of it, followed by an icy breath. The two opposites clash without mixing.

Ignis steps out first, flames crackling along his arms. Glacius follows him, frost spreading over the rubble with each of his steps. Void brings up the rear, his fog creeping over the ground like an animal sniffing out its prey.

— ...

Morganne looks at them one by one, her eyebrows slowly rising.

— Oh. Extra guests.

Ignis smiles.

— She's here. It's definitely her.

— The Assimilated's chaos, Glacius confirms. No possible doubt.

Void steps forward, his eyes fixed on Morganne, a cold rage piercing beneath his usual contempt.

— So it's you. The thief.

— Thief? Morganne repeats, almost amused. I prefer "collector".

— ...

— But yes, it's me. And you're right on time. I haven't had a taste of the Incarnations of fire and ice yet.

Isidora, still on her concrete block, leans toward her bag of chips and crunches a handful with renewed interest.

— Oh. Company's coming.

The crack closed behind them with a sharp snap.

Void emerges a second later, his silhouette gradually taking shape through his own fog, right behind Ignis and Glacius. The three Incarnations find themselves lined up facing Morganne. On the other side of the battlefield, 81 still holds his two blades, Agent 47 his weapon, Lucifer breathes behind his ruined wall.

Two camps. A single enemy.

— ...

Ignis turns his head toward 81. His flames crackle a little louder.

— The Godslayer.

— Ignis.

— Akuma told me to push you aside if you got in the way.

— Yeah. And?

Ignis glances at Morganne, whose golden blood has just sealed over the last gash. A sneer twists his mouth.

— ...We'll settle this later.

— Works for me, 81 answers, without lowering his swords.

Glacius takes a step. The frost cracks under his boot.

— She has the Assimilated's chaos. If you hit her, she regenerates.

— We noticed, thanks, 81 grinds out.

"Confirmation," Reaper cuts in, in Agent 47's earpiece. "Temporary alliance between five high-ranking fighters. Recalculating probability of victory..."

— And?

"...I'd rather observe before giving a number."

— Encouraging, 47 breathes.

Morganne looks at all of them, one by one, the golden sphere crackling in her palm. Her smile doesn't falter.

— Five against one. How flattering.

On her concrete block, Isidora swallows a handful of chips without taking her eyes off the scene. She chews slowly, tilts her head, narrows her eyes.

— Oh yeah, so that's her.

— Isidora, Lucifer hisses.

— No but look at her. The helmet, the pose, the little smile of a chick who thinks she's above everyone.

She raises her bag of chips in Morganne's direction.

— That's the new bitch of the universe, you can tell right away.

— ...

Morganne blinks. Her smile freezes for half a second.

— Excuse me?

— Nothing, nothing, carry on, I'm just here in my corner.

— ISIDORA, EITHER HELP OR SHUT YOUR MOUTH, 81 yells.

— I'M FILMING.

— YOU'RE NOT FILMING, YOU DON'T EVEN HAVE YOUR PHONE IN YOUR HAND!

Isidora looks down. The phone is indeed propped against her knee. She shrugs.

— Oh. Yeah. Sorry.

Void doesn't bother turning his head toward her. His fog stretches over the ground, creeps up to Morganne's feet, traces barely visible shapes around her.

— Shall we begin?

— With pleasure, Ignis answers.

A blast of flames. An icy breath. A wave of hallucinations sweeping over the battlefield. Three attacks striking at the same time, a curtain of opposing colors swallowing Morganne in one go.

— Now! 81 shouts.

He charges through the cloud of heat and frost. 47 fires, three engraved bullets whistling into the fog. Lucifer leaves his cover, his lance of shadows extended once more.

At the heart of the chaos, a golden silhouette bursts out laughing.

— Finally, a show!

The cloud of flames, frost and hallucinations tears apart all at once, like a curtain ripped down.

Morganne steps out of it unharmed, the golden sphere still calm in the hollow of her palm. Her armor doesn't have a scratch.

— ...

— She didn't take anything, Lucifer breathes.

— Again, 81 shouts.

He charges. Ignis follows him, flames roaring on his arms. Glacius closes off the left flank, frost racing over the rubble. An ice lance, a blazing fist, two blades. The three assaults converge in the same second.

Morganne opens her hand.

A golden wave sweeps all three of them away. Ignis is hurled against a pillar, 81 goes through a wall, Glacius slides ten meters, the frost exploding around him.

— ...

She hasn't moved a single step.

— This is KJ's Incarnations? she asks, almost disappointed. I expected better.

Void unleashes a wave of hallucinations. The ground becomes an ocean, the sky fills with screaming faces. Morganne watches them go by for a few seconds, then blows on them like dust. The scenery dissolves.

— Illusions, not really my thing. I've seen much prettier ones.

— ...

— Agent 47, shoot, 81 orders as he gets back up, his lip split.

Three engraved bullets. One hits the throat, another the side. Golden blood spurts, seals over. Morganne doesn't even blink.

"Regeneration confirmed," Reaper murmurs. "Every bit of damage is rewritten before it exists."

— Then we hit her so hard she doesn't have time to heal, Ignis growls as he gets back on his feet, his shoulder smoking.

— Try it, Morganne invites.

He tries. A column of fire hot enough to melt a planet. She walks through it. The flames lick her golden armor like a caress, and when they die down, she's still there, her smile a little wider.

— ...

Glacius follows up with a coffin of absolute ice. Morganne shatters it with her fingertip.

— Okay, that's enough.

She raises her hand. A deluge of golden projectiles rains down on the whole battlefield. Lucifer dives behind a pillar, which collapses. 47 rolls aside, a bullet grazing his ear. Ignis takes it full-on, screams, his flames flickering. Glacius raises a wall of ice, which shatters on the third impact.

When the dust settles, they're all on their knees or sprawled out — except 81, still standing, his blades crossed in front of him, blood running from his brow.

— ...

— You're holding up well, Godslayer, Morganne admits. But you can't touch me.

— Watch me.

— I'm watching.

He throws himself at her once again. She dodges with a sidestep, and her green hand brushes his side. 81 feels something tear away inside him, an icy burn that has nothing physical about it, and he leaps back, panting.

— Don't let her touch you with the green hand! Aravos yells, leaning against his pillar.

— Thanks for the advice! 81 spits.

On her concrete block, Isidora crunches a chip.

— They're doing pretty well, right?

— ISIDORA, Lucifer yells, sprawled on the ground. WE'RE GETTING OUR ASSES KICKED!

— Yeah, but with style.

Morganne laughs. Five Incarnations and the Godslayer, and not a single lasting scratch.

— You see? Chaos is magnificent. It never lets me down.

She takes a step toward 81, the golden sphere growing in her palm.

— And now, if you don't mind, I'll take what I fancy.

Ignis gets up first. His shoulder is still smoking, his flames roaring louder than ever, and the ground beginning to melt beneath his feet.

— She wants fire?

— Ignis, wait...

— She's gonna get it.

He doesn't listen. His arms blaze with a blinding white, and the temperature suddenly soars, far beyond what any ordinary body could bear. The rubble vaporizes. The sky wrinkles. Glacius takes a step back despite himself, the frost melting on his shoulders.

— Hell Burn.

The Incarnation of fire hurls himself at Morganne at a speed that tears the air. His fist goes through the golden sphere, burns it, devours it, and slams full-force into the Eternal Fairy's armor.

— ...

Morganne steps back. One step. Just one.

— Oh.

She looks down at the spot where the blow landed. The golden armor has turned red, and a trail of heat runs along her ribs.

— Now that's something serious.

— You see? Ignis roars, his flames rising yet another notch. You can burn!

— I can, yes.

Morganne's smile widens.

— And that's exactly why I wanted you.

Her green hand shoots out. Ignis sees it coming, tries to dodge, but the golden wave she sent ahead of it catches him at the knee. He loses his balance for half a second. Half a second is enough.

— Ignis!

81 lunges, both blades forward. Too late. The green palm lands on the forehead of the Incarnation of fire and pins him to the ground.

— ...

— No... NO...

Ignis's flames flicker. Then they twist, stretch, leave his body one by one and flow toward Morganne's hand like a river running backward. His scream breaks off midway. His skin empties of all heat, his veins of all light.

— ...

Something very ancient goes out inside him.

Ignis's body doesn't remain. It sags, cracks, and crumbles into cold ashes that the wind immediately scatters over the rubble.

— ...

No one moves.

Morganne slowly straightens up, eyes closed. Golden flames dance along her arms, climb up to her shoulders, wrap around her sphere, which grows with every second. The temperature around her exceeds anything matter can withstand.

— Mmh...

She opens her eyes again. Her green irises shine with an orange glow.

— So this is what the hottest fire in the universe is worth.

— ...

— Thanks for the gift, Ignis. I'll put it to good use.

Glacius has stayed frozen, the ice lance still raised, his face devoid of expression. But his breathing has changed. Shorter. More ragged.

— He's dead.

— ...

— He's really dead.

"Recalculating," Reaper murmurs in Agent 47's earpiece. "The alliance's probability of victory: in free fall. Morganne now has two Higher Incarnations in her arsenal."

— Two, 47 repeats, without taking his eyes off Morganne.

"And the first of the two keeps regenerating her."

Lucifer straightens up behind his pillar, his face ashen.

— She just absorbed a fire that can turn stars to dust...

Void steps back. His fog retracts around him, as if he were trying to hide.

— ...Akuma was right, he breathes, almost under his breath. She shouldn't exist.

On her concrete block, Isidora has stopped chewing. Just for a moment. She watches Ignis's ashes roll across the ground, the bag of chips halfway up in her hand.

— ...

Then she shrugs and grabs another handful.

— Oh. He's dead. Okay.

— ISIDORA! 81 yells without turning around.

— What? I didn't say anything mean.

— A GUY JUST DIED IN FRONT OF YOU!

— Yeah, and I saw. He played it wrong, that's all. Honestly, charging headfirst at a chick who regenerates wasn't smart.

Morganne turns her head toward her. Her golden flames crackle a little louder.

— ...You still haven't answered me.

— Answered what?

— You're the only one who isn't trembling.

— Well yeah.

Isidora swallows her chip, wipes her fingers on her cloak.

— I'm starving and I don't feel like getting up. You're bothering me.

Morganne's smile freezes. This time, it doesn't come back right away.

— ...

She slowly closes her hand, and the flames surrounding her wrap around her fist.

— Next.

Her eyes settle on Glacius.
