Ignis smiled, and the heat rose a notch throughout the hall. — With pleasure. — Alive, if possible. What she stole doesn't belong to her, and I want it back intact. If she refuses to give it back, you'll take it from a corpse. — ... — The Godslayer's group is on site. If they get in the way, you know what to do. Void didn't move. His fog had frozen on the floor, as if it too hesitated to obey. — You're sending me. — You were the first to complain about the Assimilated's absence. Go avenge him. — And you stay here, doing nothing? Akuma's gaze settled on him. The temperature dropped further, and even Glacius flinched slightly. — Someone has to guard this Palace. Someone has to guard what's inside it. — ... — You wanted to command, Void? Start by obeying. A sneer twisted Void's face, closer to a grimace than a smile. His fog began to move again, slowly, with barely veiled contempt. — As you wish... Boss. Glacius took a step forward, and the frost cracked under his feet. For the first time since he came in, his voice rang out, dry as broken ice. — She killed the Assimilated. — ... — That changes the math. — Then all three of you will go, Akuma decided. Not just one. Ignis cracked his knuckles, and sparks shot from his fingers. — This is gonna be fun. — Don't underestimate this woman. The Assimilated didn't lose to a stranger: he lost to someone who knew exactly how to take him. She raised her hand. A black crack tore through the air in front of them, a passage cut into reality, its edges curling like burnt paper. — Go. Ignis went in first, his flames briefly lighting up the inside of the rift. Glacius followed, the frost spreading behind him all the way to the threshold. Void lingered a second longer, his eyes fixed on Akuma. — ... — A problem? — None. Just a remark... When I come back with her head, don't ask me to thank you. He disappeared into the rift without waiting for an answer. The passage closed with a sharp snap. The Throne Room fell back into an almost total calm. Akuma stood motionless for a long moment before the empty throne, without looking at it, without going near it. — ... Then she slowly turned her head toward another door, more discreet, at the back of the hall. A door none of the three Incarnations had noticed on their way in. Behind it, something moved. Morganne was advancing through the middle of the battlefield as if the fight didn't exist. A golden volley. 81 crosses his blades to deflect it, the impact sends him sliding ten meters, his heels plowing through the rubble. — ... — Again? You bore me, Godslayer. He charges. Two swords, an angle she can't see. The blade slices her arm, a clean line of golden blood. — There! Got you! — Watch closely. The wound closes on its own. A shiver of chaos runs over Morganne's skin, then nothing, not even a scar. — ...Fuck. — Annoying, isn't it? All that power you've absorbed, and it only serves to hurt you for nothing. Lucifer bursts out on her flank, a lance of infernal shadows already extended. Morganne barely lifts two fingers. The lance shatters. Lucifer is thrown back, rolls in the dust, gets back up spitting. — She didn't even look at me! — Move! Agent 47 fires three times. Three engraved bullets, only one hits, right in the shoulder. Golden blood spurts, the wound closes immediately. — Riper. Analysis. "Instant regeneration. Origin identified: the Assimilated's chaos. Every bit of damage is rewritten as if it had never happened." — Then how do we kill her. "...I don't have an answer yet." — Great! Lucifer yells, diving behind a ruined wall, a spray of golden energy pulverizing the spot where he had stood a second earlier. Morganne laughs. A crystalline, effortless laugh. — This is the famous group that made the Assimilated run? You can't even touch me. 81 takes a blow to the side, steps back, breathes. His 621 hearts are pounding wildly. He looks up at her, gauges the distance, calculates. — We gotta find something. Fast. — I'm open to any idea! Lucifer answers from his cover. Off to the side, Takeshi and Poppy watch the scene, powerless. Aravos leans against a pillar, too weak to fight. And Isidora? Sitting on a concrete block, legs crossed, she's working through a bag of chips that just appeared from her cloak. Her phone is propped against her knee. — ISIDORA! — What? — WHAT ARE YOU DOING?! — Waiting to see if you guys make it. I don't feel like wearing myself out for nothing. — SHE'S SLAUGHTERING US! — Yeah, I can see that. You're not bad, you dodge well. Morganne finally turns her head toward her. A flash of irritation passes through her green eyes. — You. — Me? — You don't move. You don't scream. You don't run. It's strange. — That's my style. — ... Morganne's smile freezes for half a second. Then the air tears open. A black crack opens in the middle of the battlefield. Its edges curl like burnt paper. — ... Everyone stops. Even 81 lowers his blades a notch. A wave of heat bursts out of it, followed by an icy breath. The two opposites clash without mixing. Ignis steps out first, flames crackling along his arms. Glacius follows him, frost spreading over the rubble with each of his steps. Void brings up the rear, his fog creeping over the ground like an animal sniffing out its prey. — ... Morganne looks at them one by one, her eyebrows slowly rising. — Oh. Extra guests. Ignis smiles. — She's here. It's definitely her. — The Assimilated's chaos, Glacius confirms. No possible doubt. Void steps forward, his eyes fixed on Morganne, a cold rage piercing beneath his usual contempt. — So it's you. The thief. — Thief? Morganne repeats, almost amused. I prefer "collector". — ... — But yes, it's me. And you're right on time. I haven't had a taste of the Incarnations of fire and ice yet. Isidora, still on her concrete block, leans toward her bag of chips and crunches a handful with renewed interest. — Oh. Company's coming. The crack closed behind them with a sharp snap. Void emerges a second later, his silhouette gradually taking shape through his own fog, right behind Ignis and Glacius. The three Incarnations find themselves lined up facing Morganne. On the other side of the battlefield, 81 still holds his two blades, Agent 47 his weapon, Lucifer breathes behind his ruined wall. Two camps. A single enemy. — ... Ignis turns his head toward 81. His flames crackle a little louder. — The Godslayer. — Ignis. — Akuma told me to push you aside if you got in the way. — Yeah. And? Ignis glances at Morganne, whose golden blood has just sealed over the last gash. A sneer twists his mouth. — ...We'll settle this later. — Works for me, 81 answers, without lowering his swords. Glacius takes a step. The frost cracks under his boot. — She has the Assimilated's chaos. If you hit her, she regenerates. — We noticed, thanks, 81 grinds out. "Confirmation," Reaper cuts in, in Agent 47's earpiece. "Temporary alliance between five high-ranking fighters. Recalculating probability of victory..." — And? "...I'd rather observe before giving a number." — Encouraging, 47 breathes. Morganne looks at all of them, one by one, the golden sphere crackling in her palm. Her smile doesn't falter. — Five against one. How flattering. On her concrete block, Isidora swallows a handful of chips without taking her eyes off the scene. She chews slowly, tilts her head, narrows her eyes. — Oh yeah, so that's her. — Isidora, Lucifer hisses. — No but look at her. The helmet, the pose, the little smile of a chick who thinks she's above everyone. She raises her bag of chips in Morganne's direction. — That's the new bitch of the universe, you can tell right away. — ... Morganne blinks. Her smile freezes for half a second. — Excuse me? — Nothing, nothing, carry on, I'm just here in my corner. — ISIDORA, EITHER HELP OR SHUT YOUR MOUTH, 81 yells. — I'M FILMING. — YOU'RE NOT FILMING, YOU DON'T EVEN HAVE YOUR PHONE IN YOUR HAND! Isidora looks down. The phone is indeed propped against her knee. She shrugs. — Oh. Yeah. Sorry. Void doesn't bother turning his head toward her. His fog stretches over the ground, creeps up to Morganne's feet, traces barely visible shapes around her. — Shall we begin? — With pleasure, Ignis answers. A blast of flames. An icy breath. A wave of hallucinations sweeping over the battlefield. Three attacks striking at the same time, a curtain of opposing colors swallowing Morganne in one go. — Now! 81 shouts. He charges through the cloud of heat and frost. 47 fires, three engraved bullets whistling into the fog. Lucifer leaves his cover, his lance of shadows extended once more. At the heart of the chaos, a golden silhouette bursts out laughing. — Finally, a show! The cloud of flames, frost and hallucinations tears apart all at once, like a curtain ripped down. Morganne steps out of it unharmed, the golden sphere still calm in the hollow of her palm. Her armor doesn't have a scratch. — ... — She didn't take anything, Lucifer breathes. — Again, 81 shouts. He charges. Ignis follows him, flames roaring on his arms. Glacius closes off the left flank, frost racing over the rubble. An ice lance, a blazing fist, two blades. The three assaults converge in the same second. Morganne opens her hand. A golden wave sweeps all three of them away. Ignis is hurled against a pillar, 81 goes through a wall, Glacius slides ten meters, the frost exploding around him. — ... She hasn't moved a single step. — This is KJ's Incarnations? she asks, almost disappointed. I expected better. Void unleashes a wave of hallucinations. The ground becomes an ocean, the sky fills with screaming faces. Morganne watches them go by for a few seconds, then blows on them like dust. The scenery dissolves. — Illusions, not really my thing. I've seen much prettier ones. — ... — Agent 47, shoot, 81 orders as he gets back up, his lip split. Three engraved bullets. One hits the throat, another the side. Golden blood spurts, seals over. Morganne doesn't even blink. "Regeneration confirmed," Reaper murmurs. "Every bit of damage is rewritten before it exists." — Then we hit her so hard she doesn't have time to heal, Ignis growls as he gets back on his feet, his shoulder smoking. — Try it, Morganne invites. He tries. A column of fire hot enough to melt a planet. She walks through it. The flames lick her golden armor like a caress, and when they die down, she's still there, her smile a little wider. — ... Glacius follows up with a coffin of absolute ice. Morganne shatters it with her fingertip. — Okay, that's enough. She raises her hand. A deluge of golden projectiles rains down on the whole battlefield. Lucifer dives behind a pillar, which collapses. 47 rolls aside, a bullet grazing his ear. Ignis takes it full-on, screams, his flames flickering. Glacius raises a wall of ice, which shatters on the third impact. When the dust settles, they're all on their knees or sprawled out — except 81, still standing, his blades crossed in front of him, blood running from his brow. — ... — You're holding up well, Godslayer, Morganne admits. But you can't touch me. — Watch me. — I'm watching. He throws himself at her once again. She dodges with a sidestep, and her green hand brushes his side. 81 feels something tear away inside him, an icy burn that has nothing physical about it, and he leaps back, panting. — Don't let her touch you with the green hand! Aravos yells, leaning against his pillar. — Thanks for the advice! 81 spits. On her concrete block, Isidora crunches a chip. — They're doing pretty well, right? — ISIDORA, Lucifer yells, sprawled on the ground. WE'RE GETTING OUR ASSES KICKED! — Yeah, but with style. Morganne laughs. Five Incarnations and the Godslayer, and not a single lasting scratch. — You see? Chaos is magnificent. It never lets me down. She takes a step toward 81, the golden sphere growing in her palm. — And now, if you don't mind, I'll take what I fancy. Ignis gets up first. His shoulder is still smoking, his flames roaring louder than ever, and the ground beginning to melt beneath his feet. — She wants fire? — Ignis, wait... — She's gonna get it. He doesn't listen. His arms blaze with a blinding white, and the temperature suddenly soars, far beyond what any ordinary body could bear. The rubble vaporizes. The sky wrinkles. Glacius takes a step back despite himself, the frost melting on his shoulders. — Hell Burn. The Incarnation of fire hurls himself at Morganne at a speed that tears the air. His fist goes through the golden sphere, burns it, devours it, and slams full-force into the Eternal Fairy's armor. — ... Morganne steps back. One step. Just one. — Oh. She looks down at the spot where the blow landed. The golden armor has turned red, and a trail of heat runs along her ribs. — Now that's something serious. — You see? Ignis roars, his flames rising yet another notch. You can burn! — I can, yes. Morganne's smile widens. — And that's exactly why I wanted you. Her green hand shoots out. Ignis sees it coming, tries to dodge, but the golden wave she sent ahead of it catches him at the knee. He loses his balance for half a second. Half a second is enough. — Ignis! 81 lunges, both blades forward. Too late. The green palm lands on the forehead of the Incarnation of fire and pins him to the ground. — ... — No... NO... Ignis's flames flicker. Then they twist, stretch, leave his body one by one and flow toward Morganne's hand like a river running backward. His scream breaks off midway. His skin empties of all heat, his veins of all light. — ... Something very ancient goes out inside him. Ignis's body doesn't remain. It sags, cracks, and crumbles into cold ashes that the wind immediately scatters over the rubble. — ... No one moves. Morganne slowly straightens up, eyes closed. Golden flames dance along her arms, climb up to her shoulders, wrap around her sphere, which grows with every second. The temperature around her exceeds anything matter can withstand. — Mmh... She opens her eyes again. Her green irises shine with an orange glow. — So this is what the hottest fire in the universe is worth. — ... — Thanks for the gift, Ignis. I'll put it to good use. Glacius has stayed frozen, the ice lance still raised, his face devoid of expression. But his breathing has changed. Shorter. More ragged. — He's dead. — ... — He's really dead. "Recalculating," Reaper murmurs in Agent 47's earpiece. "The alliance's probability of victory: in free fall. Morganne now has two Higher Incarnations in her arsenal." — Two, 47 repeats, without taking his eyes off Morganne. "And the first of the two keeps regenerating her." Lucifer straightens up behind his pillar, his face ashen. — She just absorbed a fire that can turn stars to dust... Void steps back. His fog retracts around him, as if he were trying to hide. — ...Akuma was right, he breathes, almost under his breath. She shouldn't exist. On her concrete block, Isidora has stopped chewing. Just for a moment. She watches Ignis's ashes roll across the ground, the bag of chips halfway up in her hand. — ... Then she shrugs and grabs another handful. — Oh. He's dead. Okay. — ISIDORA! 81 yells without turning around. — What? I didn't say anything mean. — A GUY JUST DIED IN FRONT OF YOU! — Yeah, and I saw. He played it wrong, that's all. Honestly, charging headfirst at a chick who regenerates wasn't smart. Morganne turns her head toward her. Her golden flames crackle a little louder. — ...You still haven't answered me. — Answered what? — You're the only one who isn't trembling. — Well yeah. Isidora swallows her chip, wipes her fingers on her cloak. — I'm starving and I don't feel like getting up. You're bothering me. Morganne's smile freezes. This time, it doesn't come back right away. — ... She slowly closes her hand, and the flames surrounding her wrap around her fist. — Next. Her eyes settle on Glacius.

codex-ts1-c1.title: Where Was That Damn Incarnation?
codex-ts1-c1.html:
The Assimilated was crossing the layers of the multiverse at blinding speed, each dimensional jump leaving behind fragments of entire realities collapsing in on themselves, whole universes reduced to cosmic dust by the mere shockwave of his passage.

— ...

His body, still marked by the wounds inflicted by 81 and Agent 47, was struggling more and more to hold together enough to keep making these endless crossings. Each jump cost him more, his chaotic domain flickering dangerously with every new destination.

He finally landed on an isolated planet, a sterile, silent world, perfectly suited to resting far from prying eyes.

— ...

He collapsed rather than sat down, his back against a massive rock, his labored breathing betraying the true extent of his exhaustion.

— Just... a few moments. Before heading back to the Palace.

He closed his eyes, trying to gather what strength he had left.

But something was off. A presence. Discreet, but undeniable — the nagging feeling of being watched ever since he had arrived on this planet.

— ...

He sat up abruptly, his golden gaze sweeping the surroundings, every muscle in his body instantly tensing.

— I know you're there.

At first, only silence answered him, broken solely by the sterile wind sweeping the planet's dusty surface.

Then a voice — female, drawling, loaded with undisguised mockery — rang out from the surrounding darkness.

— That's KJ's champion? Tell me it's a joke.

The Assimilated spun around sharply, frantically searching for the source of the voice.

— You're supposed to be the master of chaos. An uncontrollable, overpowered force.

A silhouette slowly began to materialize from the shadows, a cold, calculated elegance radiating from every one of its movements.

— And you're sleeping like a little bitch in a doghouse.

— ...

The Assimilated, despite his obvious exhaustion, proudly lifted his head, a flickering but still present aura of chaos forming around him again.

— Who are you.

A cruel smile spread across the face of the finally revealed silhouette, an ancient, fearsome power radiating from her whole being despite her deceptively delicate appearance.

— Someone who's going to take advantage of your current weakness to take what really interests me.

Morganne finally revealed herself completely, her figure clad in golden armor with sharp, almost royal lines — a helmet adorned with slender spikes framing a face with piercing green eyes, a sphere of golden energy crackling softly in the hollow of her palm.

— ...

The Assimilated, despite his exhaustion, got all the way up, his golden gaze quickly analyzing this imposing figure, the entire armor seeming to radiate an ancient, perfectly controlled power.

— I don't know you.

— Of course not, Morganne replied, a cold smile forming beneath her golden mask. I don't really hang out with KJ's lackeys.

— ...

— But you, she went on, stepping forward slowly and deliberately, the energy sphere crackling a little louder in her hand, you interest me. Chaos incarnate, barely able to stand after a simple fight.

The Assimilated clenched his fists, wounded pride piercing through his exhaustion.

— It wasn't a simple fight.

— Whatever, Morganne cut in, her drawling voice loaded with total contempt. What interests me is what you represent right now: a weakened source of power, unable to defend itself properly.

— ...

— And I, she added, her smile widening, just love collecting finds like that.

The Assimilated, instinctively sensing the real danger this woman posed, tried despite his critical state to gather the last remnants of his chaotic domain.

— You don't even know who you're talking to.

— Oh, but I do, Morganne replied, her energy sphere suddenly growing, an aura of raw, ancient power unfolding all around her. I know exactly who I'm talking to. A Higher Incarnation of Chaos, humiliated, drained of his strength, alone on some godforsaken planet.

She finally stopped, a few meters from him, her piercing green gaze plunging straight into his.

— The perfect moment to absorb a little more power before I deal with my dear brother.

— ...

The Assimilated, despite the growing terror he was desperately trying to hide, proudly raised his head, a last ounce of defiance crossing his golden gaze.

— You'll have to kill me for that.

Morganne tilted her head slightly, a crystalline, icy laugh escaping her.

— Count on it.

The Assimilated lunged forward despite his critical state, his flickering chaotic domain crackling around his clenched fists.

— ...

Morganne, with no visible effort, simply raised her hand, a rain of golden projectiles instantly bursting from her palm, each one slicing through the air with surgical precision.

Normally, these projectiles would have been no more than a minor nuisance — his domain would have absorbed, deflected, cancelled the slightest trace of their impact. But today, each projectile found its target with disconcerting ease, his already battered body taking every hit with very real pain.

— ...

He staggered back violently, several golden gashes opening along his torso, his chaotic domain visibly struggling to re-form properly around him.

— Well, well, Morganne observed, her drawling voice tinged with cruel amusement. Looks like your power isn't working as well as usual.

— ...

The Assimilated grimaced, still attempting a new offensive, a wave of chaotic distortion bursting from his hands — but the effect, usually devastating, turned out surprisingly weak, barely enough to push Morganne back slightly rather than destroy her completely.

— That's it? she asked, effortlessly dodging the rest of the attack, her smile never faltering.

— I... I took a hard fight, the Assimilated managed, his breathing more and more labored.

— I know. And that's exactly why I'm here.

She stepped forward again, a new volley of golden projectiles bursting out all at once, this time more numerous, faster.

The Assimilated tried to defend himself, his unstable domain creating barely enough distortion to deflect part of the attacks — but several projectiles found their way through, sinking painfully into his shoulder, his thigh, his already battered side.

— ...

He half collapsed onto one knee, breath wheezing, his golden gaze raised toward Morganne with a growing worry he could no longer hide.

— You really don't stand a chance in this state, she noted, slowly approaching, her golden energy sphere still crackling in her hand, ready to deliver the final blow.

Morganne slowly came closer, her free hand — this one a luminous green, a different energy crackling through her fingers — resting gently on the forehead of the Assimilated, still collapsed on his knees before her.

— ...

— Shh, she murmured, almost with a perverse gentleness. It'll only take a moment.

The Assimilated, too weak to break free, immediately felt something give way inside him — not a simple physical wound, but something much deeper, much more fundamental.

— ...

His very soul began to dissolve, gradually drawn out through Morganne's green palm, his chaotic powers following the same path, torn straight from his essence.

— ...No...

— Yes, she simply replied, her smile never wavering, the energy continuing to flow from him to her, an uninterrupted stream of raw power.

The Assimilated's body began to literally empty out, his skin losing its usual tint, his red and black tattoos gradually fading, every scrap of life force leaving his physical shell for good.

— ...

A last breath escaped him, a last golden gaze rising toward Morganne, filled with pure terror and total incomprehension.

Then nothing.

His body collapsed completely to the ground, inert, drained of all life force, all soul, all power — the Higher Incarnation of Chaos, a cosmic terror who had stood up to 81 and Agent 47 combined, reduced to a mere husk on a sterile, forgotten planet.

— ...

Morganne straightened up, examining her own hand, now charged with new power, a cold satisfaction crossing her face.

— Chaos in person. Beaten so easily.

She cast one last contemptuous glance at the Assimilated's lifeless body before turning away completely, her attention already on her next target.

— Now. My dear brother.

The Assimilated's lifeless body suddenly began to tremble, a blinding light radiating from within, an unbearable pressure building up in barely a few seconds.

— ...

Morganne, already walking away, stopped dead, turning around just in time to see the corpse implode on itself, then instantly explode in a blast of colossal power, a true miniature supernova completely ravaging the sterile planet around them.

— ...

The shockwave swept away everything in its path, the planet's entire surface breaking apart, rock fragments hurled at dizzying speeds into the void of space.

Morganne, protected by an instinctive golden aura, took the explosion without the slightest damage, her expression remaining perfectly impassive despite the scale of the cataclysm.

— Interesting, she simply commented, watching the last remnants of the planet scatter around her. One last residual discharge. Typical of chaos, even in death.

She was finally about to leave, her next target clearly set — but a sudden distortion in space caught her attention, a familiar silhouette materializing a few meters away from her.

— ...

Aravos, still marked by his own recent fight against 81, his entire body betraying deep exhaustion, froze instantly at the sight of his sister.

— ...

An icy silence settled between them, the debris of the destroyed planet still slowly floating all around, lit by the last echoes of the cosmic explosion.

— Morganne, he finally said, his voice tinged with an ancient hatred and poorly hidden terror.

She slowly turned her head toward him, a cruel, satisfied smile spreading across her face.

— Well, well. What a coincidence. I was just about to come pay you a little visit, dear brother.

Aravos clenched his fists, every part of his body, still aching from his disastrous fight against 81, protesting against the effort he was about to make.

— ...

Morganne, facing him, stayed perfectly relaxed, her golden energy sphere crackling softly in her palm, total confidence radiating from every one of her gestures.

— You know why I'm here, she said simply.

— I know, Aravos answered, his deep voice loaded with cold resolve. How long.

— Ever since you decided to hide like a coward after your daughter's death instead of facing me directly.

— ...

A tense silence settled in, the debris of the destroyed planet still floating all around them, lit by the faint glow of the surrounding stars.

— She laughed, Aravos finally managed, a contained rage piercing through every word. She laughed at her death.

— She deserved what happened to her, Morganne retorted, without the slightest trace of remorse. She was weak. Like you.

— ...

This time, Aravos didn't wait any longer.

He charged first, a wave of cosmic energy instantly bursting from his whole being, the accumulated power of the Cosmos and the greatest stars concentrating into a devastating assault.

— ...

Morganne, barely surprised, simply raised her hand, her own golden energy materializing into an instant shield, absorbing most of the blow with no visible effort.

— That's all you've got? she sneered, her smile never wavering.

Aravos, despite his lingering exhaustion, immediately followed up with a second attack, more focused, more precise, a miniature star forming between his hands before being hurled straight at his sister.

— ...

This time Morganne dodged the projectile with a fluid, almost nonchalant movement, her piercing green gaze never leaving her brother.

— You're tired, she observed, slowly moving forward, her energy sphere gradually growing. Your fight against the Godslayer drained your strength.

— ...

— And I, she added, have just absorbed the entirety of the powers of a Higher Incarnation of Chaos.

Aravos, feeling the chilling truth of that remark, still proudly raised his head, a desperate determination crossing his gaze.

— Then we might as well finish this now.

— With pleasure, Morganne answered, finally charging in turn, the fight between brother and sister truly beginning amid the floating wreckage of the destroyed planet.

Aravos struck a blow of colossal power, concentrating the last remnants of his cosmic energy into one single desperate assault — but Morganne, barely shaken, took the impact with disconcerting ease, her golden aura absorbing most of the shock.

— ...

— That's really all you've got, she sighed, almost disappointed, her smile never fading.

Aravos stepped back, every part of his body screaming with fatigue, his cosmic energy dangerously depleted after an already grueling fight against 81 barely a few hours earlier.

— ...

He understood instantly, with chilling clarity, that he no longer stood any chance. His sister, already far superior to him under normal circumstances, had just absorbed the entire power of a Higher Incarnation of Chaos. Continuing this fight meant dying, plain and simple.

— ...

He backed away further, desperately searching for a solution, his mind racing frantically despite the crushing exhaustion weighing on him.

Only one option took shape, humiliating as it was.

— ...

Gritting his teeth, swallowing a thousand-year-old pride, Aravos hastily opened a dimensional rift, his last ounce of energy concentrated in this final escape attempt.

— You can't run forever, Morganne shouted, already lunging to stop him from escaping.

— I know, he simply answered, diving into the rift just before she could reach him, the crack closing instantly behind him.

— ...

On the other side, Aravos reappeared abruptly, almost collapsing to the ground, his whole body trembling from the effort. He painfully straightened up, his gaze sweeping his surroundings to get his bearings.

He knew exactly where he had to go. The most unlikely place, the most painful for his pride — but the only one that offered a real chance of survival against what his sister had become.

— ...

He closed his eyes for a moment, a bitter resolve crossing his face.

— 81.

Chaos incarnate, barely able to stand after a simple fight. The Assimilated clenched his fists, wounded pride piercing through his exhaustion. — It wasn't a simple fight. — Whatever, Morganne cut in, her drawling voice loaded with total contempt. What interests me is what you represent right now: a weakened source of power, unable to defend itself properly. — ... — And I, she added, her smile widening, just love collecting finds like that. The Assimilated, instinctively sensing the real danger this woman posed, tried despite his critical state to gather the last remnants of his chaotic domain. — You don't even know who you're talking to. — Oh, but I do, Morganne replied, her energy sphere suddenly growing, an aura of raw, ancient power unfolding all around her. I know exactly who I'm talking to. A Higher Incarnation of Chaos, humiliated, drained of his strength, alone on some godforsaken planet. She finally stopped, a few meters from him, her piercing green gaze plunging straight into his. — The perfect moment to absorb a little more power before I deal with my dear brother. — ... The Assimilated, despite the growing terror he was desperately trying to hide, proudly raised his head, a last ounce of defiance crossing his golden gaze. — You'll have to kill me for that. Morganne tilted her head slightly, a crystalline, icy laugh escaping her. — Count on it. The Assimilated lunged forward despite his critical state, his flickering chaotic domain crackling around his clenched fists. — ... Morganne, with no visible effort, simply raised her hand, a rain of golden projectiles instantly bursting from her palm, each one slicing through the air with surgical precision. Normally, these projectiles would have been no more than a minor nuisance — his domain would have absorbed, deflected, cancelled the slightest trace of their impact. But today, each projectile found its target with disconcerting ease, his already battered body taking every hit with very real pain. — ... He staggered back violently, several golden gashes opening along his torso, his chaotic domain visibly struggling to re-form properly around him. — Well, well, Morganne observed, her drawling voice tinged with cruel amusement. Looks like your power isn't working as well as usual. — ... The Assimilated grimaced, still attempting a new offensive, a wave of chaotic distortion bursting from his hands — but the effect, usually devastating, turned out surprisingly weak, barely enough to push Morganne back slightly rather than destroy her completely. — That's it? she asked, effortlessly dodging the rest of the attack, her smile never faltering. — I... I took a hard fight, the Assimilated managed, his breathing more and more labored. — I know. And that's exactly why I'm here. She stepped forward again, a new volley of golden projectiles bursting out all at once, this time more numerous, faster. The Assimilated tried to defend himself, his unstable domain creating barely enough distortion to deflect part of the attacks — but several projectiles found their way through, sinking painfully into his shoulder, his thigh, his already battered side. — ... He half collapsed onto one knee, breath wheezing, his golden gaze raised toward Morganne with a growing worry he could no longer hide. — You really don't stand a chance in this state, she noted, slowly approaching, her golden energy sphere still crackling in her hand, ready to deliver the final blow. Morganne slowly came closer, her free hand — this one a luminous green, a different energy crackling through her fingers — resting gently on the forehead of the Assimilated, still collapsed on his knees before her. — ... — Shh, she murmured, almost with a perverse gentleness. It'll only take a moment. The Assimilated, too weak to break free, immediately felt something give way inside him — not a simple physical wound, but something much deeper, much more fundamental. — ... His very soul began to dissolve, gradually drawn out through Morganne's green palm, his chaotic powers following the same path, torn straight from his essence. — ...No... — Yes, she simply replied, her smile never wavering, the energy continuing to flow from him to her, an uninterrupted stream of raw power. The Assimilated's body began to literally empty out, his skin losing its usual tint, his red and black tattoos gradually fading, every scrap of life force leaving his physical shell for good. — ... A last breath escaped him, a last golden gaze rising toward Morganne, filled with pure terror and total incomprehension. Then nothing. His body collapsed completely to the ground, inert, drained of all life force, all soul, all power — the Higher Incarnation of Chaos, a cosmic terror who had stood up to 81 and Agent 47 combined, reduced to a mere husk on a sterile, forgotten planet. — ... Morganne straightened up, examining her own hand, now charged with new power, a cold satisfaction crossing her face. — Chaos in person. Beaten so easily. She cast one last contemptuous glance at the Assimilated's lifeless body before turning away completely, her attention already on her next target. — Now. My dear brother. The Assimilated's lifeless body suddenly began to tremble, a blinding light radiating from within, an unbearable pressure building up in barely a few seconds. — ... Morganne, already walking away, stopped dead, turning around just in time to see the corpse implode on itself, then instantly explode in a blast of colossal power, a true miniature supernova completely ravaging the sterile planet around them. — ... The shockwave swept away everything in its path, the planet's entire surface breaking apart, rock fragments hurled at dizzying speeds into the void of space. Morganne, protected by an instinctive golden aura, took the explosion without the slightest damage, her expression remaining perfectly impassive despite the scale of the cataclysm. — Interesting, she simply commented, watching the last remnants of the planet scatter around her. One last residual discharge. Typical of chaos, even in death. She was finally about to leave, her next target clearly set — but a sudden distortion in space caught her attention, a familiar silhouette materializing a few meters away from her. — ... Aravos, still marked by his own recent fight against 81, his entire body betraying deep exhaustion, froze instantly at the sight of his sister. — ... An icy silence settled between them, the debris of the destroyed planet still slowly floating all around, lit by the last echoes of the cosmic explosion. — Morganne, he finally said, his voice tinged with an ancient hatred and poorly hidden terror. She slowly turned her head toward him, a cruel, satisfied smile spreading across her face. — Well, well. What a coincidence. I was just about to come pay you a little visit, dear brother. Aravos clenched his fists, every part of his body, still aching from his disastrous fight against 81, protesting against the effort he was about to make. — ... Morganne, facing him, stayed perfectly relaxed, her golden energy sphere crackling softly in her palm, total confidence radiating from every one of her gestures. — You know why I'm here, she said simply. — I know, Aravos answered, his deep voice loaded with cold resolve. How long. — Ever since you decided to hide like a coward after your daughter's death instead of facing me directly. — ... A tense silence settled in, the debris of the destroyed planet still floating all around them, lit by the faint glow of the surrounding stars. — She laughed, Aravos finally managed, a contained rage piercing through every word. She laughed at her death. — She deserved what happened to her, Morganne retorted, without the slightest trace of remorse. She was weak. Like you. — ... This time, Aravos didn't wait any longer. He charged first, a wave of cosmic energy instantly bursting from his whole being, the accumulated power of the Cosmos and the greatest stars concentrating into a devastating assault. — ... Morganne, barely surprised, simply raised her hand, her own golden energy materializing into an instant shield, absorbing most of the blow with no visible effort. — That's all you've got? she sneered, her smile never wavering. Aravos, despite his lingering exhaustion, immediately followed up with a second attack, more focused, more precise, a miniature star forming between his hands before being hurled straight at his sister. — ... This time Morganne dodged the projectile with a fluid, almost nonchalant movement, her piercing green gaze never leaving her brother. — You're tired, she observed, slowly moving forward, her energy sphere gradually growing. Your fight against the Godslayer drained your strength. — ... — And I, she added, have just absorbed the entirety of the powers of a Higher Incarnation of Chaos. Aravos, feeling the chilling truth of that remark, still proudly raised his head, a desperate determination crossing his gaze. — Then we might as well finish this now. — With pleasure, Morganne answered, finally charging in turn, the fight between brother and sister truly beginning amid the floating wreckage of the destroyed planet. Aravos struck a blow of colossal power, concentrating the last remnants of his cosmic energy into one single desperate assault — but Morganne, barely shaken, took the impact with disconcerting ease, her golden aura absorbing most of the shock. — ... — That's really all you've got, she sighed, almost disappointed, her smile never fading. Aravos stepped back, every part of his body screaming with fatigue, his cosmic energy dangerously depleted after an already grueling fight against 81 barely a few hours earlier. — ... He understood instantly, with chilling clarity, that he no longer stood any chance. His sister, already far superior to him under normal circumstances, had just absorbed the entire power of a Higher Incarnation of Chaos. Continuing this fight meant dying, plain and simple. — ... He backed away further, desperately searching for a solution, his mind racing frantically despite the crushing exhaustion weighing on him. Only one option took shape, humiliating as it was. — ... Gritting his teeth, swallowing a thousand-year-old pride, Aravos hastily opened a dimensional rift, his last ounce of energy concentrated in this final escape attempt. — You can't run forever, Morganne shouted, already lunging to stop him from escaping. — I know, he simply answered, diving into the rift just before she could reach him, the crack closing instantly behind him. — ... On the other side, Aravos reappeared abruptly, almost collapsing to the ground, his whole body trembling from the effort. He painfully straightened up, his gaze sweeping his surroundings to get his bearings. He knew exactly where he had to go. The most unlikely place, the most painful for his pride — but the only one that offered a real chance of survival against what his sister had become. — ... He closed his eyes for a moment, a bitter resolve crossing his face. — 81.

qualdi-t1-c1.title: Chapter 1 — Getting Down to Business
qualdi-t1-c1.html:
Bullets whistled down the alley.

Two members of the Chimamire clan were running flat out, a Toride squad right on their heels. A burst of gunfire blew up a jar right next to them.

"Left! Go left!"

They turned, then turned again, and ran straight into a wall. A dead end.

The first one flattened himself against the stone.

"Shit, we're trapped! Give me the gun!"

The second one tossed him his submachine gun.

"Here, take it and spray anything that moves and wants you dead!"

He caught it in midair, dove behind a pile of crates and opened fire just as the Toride soldiers came around the corner. One soldier went down. The others threw themselves into cover.

"Contact! Dead end, ten o'clock!" a voice shouted. "They're cornered!"

The return fire came instantly. The crates exploded into splinters one by one.

"I'm almost out!" the first one yelled.

"I know, I know!"

The second one looked at the wall behind them, then at the mouth of the alley. The soldiers were advancing, covering one another.

"Okay… we're gonna have to improvise."

The shooting started up again, harder than before.

The first one rose behind the crates and emptied his magazine toward the mouth of the alley. A Toride soldier collapsed. Then another.

"Yeah! Come on, you dogs!"

But around the corner, more black helmets appeared. Four. Then six. Then ten.

"How many of them are there, damn it?!"

"Too many! Reload, reload!"

The second one tossed him a magazine. The first one slammed it in, raised the gun to his shoulder…

A bullet hit him square in the chest.

He took one step back and looked at the hole in his leather vest, as if he didn't understand. The gun slipped from his hands.

"No… no, no, no!"

The second one threw himself on him and dragged him behind what was left of the crates. He pressed both hands on the wound. The blood ran between his fingers, warm, far too fast.

"Stay with me! Stay with me, you hear me?!"

The first one opened his mouth. Nothing came out. His eyes stayed fixed on the blue sky of the Anarchy, then stopped moving.

The second one stayed still for a second. Just one.

"Cease fire!" a voice called from the Toride side. "There's one left! We want him alive!"

He picked up his partner's gun, held it tight against him and looked around. The wall behind. The soldiers in front. A broken window, two meters up, off to the side.

"Alive, huh…"

He fired a burst toward the mouth of the alley. The soldiers dove for cover. In the same second, he leapt onto a crate, grabbed the window ledge and hauled himself inside. Shards of glass sliced into his arms.

"He's going through the window! Surround the building!"

He landed in a dark room that smelled of dust and oil. He didn't stop. He crossed the hallway, tore down a staircase, smashed open a door with his shoulder. Behind him, boots were already climbing the stairs.

He ran, lungs on fire, the gun in one hand, the other pressed against his belt.

He could think of only one thing: getting back to Akasuna.

He kicked open a door.

A whole family was sitting at the table. The father, the mother, three kids, bowls of soup in their hands. Every head turned at the same time.

"Sorry!" he shouted as he crossed the room.

He knocked over a chair, jumped over the table and left through the back door. Behind him, the Toride soldiers burst into the kitchen.

"Which way did he go?!"

The father pointed his spoon at the back door, without even getting up.

The fugitive was already in the house next door. He charged down a hallway, turned and fired a blind burst behind him. A vase exploded, a painting fell, and a soldier hit the floor.

"He's shooting! He's shooting!"

"Of course he's shooting, move!"

Another door. Locked. He smashed it open with his shoulder and came face to face with an old man in his underwear, shaving in front of a mirror.

"Oh, is the gunfire for you again?" the old man sighed.

"Sorry, old timer!"

He opened the window, jumped onto the neighboring roof and landed heavily in a courtyard full of drying laundry. The sheets wrapped around him. He thrashed and swore, tore everything off and ran on, a white sheet still hanging from his shoulder.

Bullets rained down from the roof. The clotheslines snapped. A chicken took off screaming.

He turned, raised the gun and fired. The soldier on the roof pulled back into cover.

"He's in the courtyard! Cut off his exit!"

He crossed a carpet shop, knocking over two entire piles. He smashed through the back door, burst out into another alley and felt the magazine click empty.

Out of bullets.

He threw the gun away, pulled the pistol from his belt and started running again. In the distance, above the rooftops, the tall red towers of Akasuna were already in sight.

Three more streets.

Maybe four.

Behind him, the Toride boots weren't slowing down.

He reached the end of the last alley, and the city stopped all at once.

In front of him there was nothing but desert. Red dunes as far as the eye could see, and the sun crushing everything.

He didn't think. He ran.

His boots sank into the sand with every step. The sheet still hanging from his shoulder snapped in the hot wind. Behind him, the Toride soldiers were coming out of the city one after another.

"He's heading into the desert!"

"After him! Don't lose him!"

Five. Ten. Fifteen. Twenty black helmets advancing in a line across the sand, rifles raised.

He turned and fired two pistol rounds. Neither hit anyone. The soldiers didn't even bother to duck.

"Stop!" one of them shouted. "You won't get anywhere! There's nothing in this desert!"

"There's less of you, at least!" he yelled without slowing down.

He scrambled up a dune on all fours, the burning sand under his hands, and half rolled down the other side. He got up, spat out sand and kept going.

His legs were starting to shake. His throat was as dry as the desert itself. The blood from the cuts on his arms had dried into red crusts mixed with dust.

Behind him, the Toride soldiers weren't running. They were walking, at a steady pace, in formation. They didn't need to run.

The desert would end up stopping him for them.

"Come on… come on…" he panted, gripping his pistol. "Akasuna… it's not far… it's not far…"

He looked ahead. The red towers of Akasuna shimmered in the distance through the heat.

They didn't seem to be getting any closer.

He pushed his legs harder. Faster. Even faster.

The sand flew around him. His heart pounded so hard he could hear it in his ears. He wasn't looking back anymore. He was only looking at the red towers.

He didn't hear the footsteps closing in behind him.

A Toride soldier had broken away from the line. Younger, faster than the others, he had left his rifle with a colleague and run with everything he had too.

He leapt.

The impact threw the fugitive face first into the sand. The pistol flew out of his hand and slid a meter away. He thrashed, kicked, tried to turn over, but the soldier crushed his back with a knee and twisted his arm behind him.

"Don't move! Don't move!"

"Get off me! Get off me, you bastard!"

"It's over, buddy. It's over."

A metallic click. The cold of a handcuff around one wrist. Then the other.

The fugitive stopped moving. He lay there, cheek against the burning sand, out of breath, eyes fixed on the red towers of Akasuna.

They were still just as far away.

A second soldier came jogging up, bent down and picked the pistol up from the sand. He looked it over, emptied it and slipped the bullets into his pocket.

"Nice run," he said. "Really. We almost could've let you win."

The other eighteen were coming up behind, in no hurry.

The soldier who had tackled him pulled him up by the collar and forced him onto his knees. The fugitive spat out sand and looked up at them. Twenty black helmets. Twenty rifles. And the sun of the Anarchy above, giving no one any favors.

"So," the soldier said, wiping the sweat under his helmet. "You and me are gonna have a long talk."

The soldier raised a hand to his radio.

"This is unit three. Suspect apprehended. Requesting a vehicle at our position, we…"

He stopped.

At the top of the dune, facing them, silhouettes had just appeared. About ten. Red scarves, leather jackets, weapons in hand. On their armbands, the same drop of blood.

"Contact! Dune, twelve o'clock!"

The twenty Toride rifles rose in a single movement. The clan mercenaries didn't move. They weren't aiming at anyone. They were waiting.

Then, without a word, they stepped aside.

Someone was coming down the dune behind them.

He walked slowly, unhurried, as if the sand didn't bother him. A raised hood hid his face in shadow. A cape of black feathers covered his shoulders, and from his belt hung vials, pouches and a dagger. In his right hand he held a tall staff topped with a red orb that glowed faintly, like a beating heart.

The soldier holding the radio let it drop against his vest.

No one in unit three needed to be told who this was.

The man stopped a few meters from them. He glanced briefly at the prisoner kneeling in the sand, then raised his head toward the soldiers.

"You have no business here, soldier. This is my territory."

His voice was calm. Cold. Without anger.

The soldier in command of the unit took a step forward. His hand trembled slightly on the grip of his rifle, but his voice held.

"Your man stole, wrecked the place and killed a soldier. It would be worrying if we'd let him get away with that, don't you think?"

Crimson didn't answer right away.

The red orb pulsed once. Then a second time.

The soldier felt something strange. A throbbing in his temples, stronger than usual. A heat rising in his veins. Next to him, one of his men raised a hand to his nose. His fingers came back red.

"You will leave my territory," said Crimson, "or I will drain every drop of blood from your miserable carcass."

Silence fell over the desert.

Twenty rifles. About ten mercenaries. A single hooded man.

And yet, in unit three, everyone knew perfectly well which side had the advantage.

The soldier didn't take his eyes off Crimson. Slowly, very slowly, he raised the radio back to his mouth.

"Unit three to the Junta. Critical situation. The leader of the Chimamire clan is on site. I repeat, Crimson is on site. Requesting authorization to… to… Awaiting your orders."

Static.

Nothing.

The seconds stretched on. A drop of sweat ran down under the soldier's helmet. The prisoner, still on his knees, gave a little smile. Crimson didn't move a millimeter.

Then the radio crackled.

"Good day to you, chief of the Bandit Republic."

A deep voice, hoarse, calm. The voice of an old man who had seen too many battlefields to get worked up over the phone.

General Gérard Eldrath himself.

Crimson turned his head slightly toward the radio.

"General Gérard. I don't think you know who you're dealing with."

Behind the unit leader, a young soldier leaned toward the man next to him and whispered:

"The general's gonna send in the army. He won't be laughing then."

His neighbor didn't answer. Blood was still running from his nose.

The radio crackled again.

"Take back your man, Crimson, if you let my soldiers leave."

Total silence.

The young soldier opened his mouth, closed it, then opened it again.

"Wait… what?"

The unit leader turned to him with a look that clearly meant: shut up.

Crimson stood still for a long moment. Then the red orb of his staff stopped pulsing. The soldiers felt the heat leave their veins all at once, like a hand loosening its grip.

"Take off his handcuffs," Crimson said simply.

The soldier who had tackled the fugitive looked at his leader. His leader looked at the radio. The radio said nothing more.

"… Do what he says."

The clink of the handcuffs echoed in the silence of the desert. The prisoner got up rubbing his wrists, scraped a little dignity together from the sand and rejoined the clan mercenaries without looking back.

As he passed the young soldier, he gave him a wink.

"Nice run, huh?"

The Toride vehicle arrived a few minutes later, in a cloud of red dust.

No one spoke while the soldiers climbed aboard. The twenty black helmets crammed into the back, rifles between their knees, without taking their eyes off the dune where the Chimamire clan still stood.

The engine roared. The vehicle turned around and drove off toward the border.

In the back, the young soldier couldn't hold it in anymore.

"I don't get it."

"Shut up," his neighbor muttered, a blood-soaked handkerchief under his nose.

"No, seriously. That's Crimson. The most wanted criminal in the world. He was right there, five meters from us, and the general… he just lets him go? Like that?"

"Did you see what he did to us without even moving? What did you want, for us to shoot him?"

"I don't know! Send in the army! Tanks! A bomb! Anything!"

The unit leader, sitting up front, didn't turn around.

"The general made his decision," he said. "He saved twenty lives today. Period."

The young soldier opened his mouth, then closed it. Through the rear window he watched the clan silhouettes shrinking at the top of the dune.

"Still," he muttered. "It's weird."

No one answered him.

On the dune, Crimson watched the vehicle disappear over the horizon. He stayed still until the sound of the engine had completely died away.

The clan member who had just been freed came over, head down.

"Boss… thank you. I…"

"Your partner is dead."

It wasn't a question. The fugitive lowered his head even further.

"Yes, boss."

Crimson said nothing more. He turned and began to climb back up the dune, staff in hand, his cape of black feathers quivering in the hot wind. The mercenaries followed him without a word.

Behind them, the wind was already erasing the footprints in the sand.

Requesting a vehicle at our position, we…" He stopped. At the top of the dune, facing them, silhouettes had just appeared. About ten. Red scarves, leather jackets, weapons in hand. On their armbands, the same drop of blood. "Contact! Dune, twelve o'clock!" The twenty Toride rifles rose in a single movement. The clan mercenaries didn't move. They weren't aiming at anyone. They were waiting. Then, without a word, they stepped aside. Someone was coming down the dune behind them. He walked slowly, unhurried, as if the sand didn't bother him. A raised hood hid his face in shadow. A cape of black feathers covered his shoulders, and from his belt hung vials, pouches and a dagger. In his right hand he held a tall staff topped with a red orb that glowed faintly, like a beating heart. The soldier holding the radio let it drop against his vest. No one in unit three needed to be told who this was. The man stopped a few meters from them. He glanced briefly at the prisoner kneeling in the sand, then raised his head toward the soldiers. "You have no business here, soldier. This is my territory." His voice was calm. Cold. Without anger. The soldier in command of the unit took a step forward. His hand trembled slightly on the grip of his rifle, but his voice held. "Your man stole, wrecked the place and killed a soldier. It would be worrying if we'd let him get away with that, don't you think?" Crimson didn't answer right away. The red orb pulsed once. Then a second time. The soldier felt something strange. A throbbing in his temples, stronger than usual. A heat rising in his veins. Next to him, one of his men raised a hand to his nose. His fingers came back red. "You will leave my territory," said Crimson, "or I will drain every drop of blood from your miserable carcass." Silence fell over the desert. Twenty rifles. About ten mercenaries. A single hooded man. And yet, in unit three, everyone knew perfectly well which side had the advantage. The soldier didn't take his eyes off Crimson. Slowly, very slowly, he raised the radio back to his mouth. "Unit three to the Junta. Critical situation. The leader of the Chimamire clan is on site. I repeat, Crimson is on site. Requesting authorization to… to… Awaiting your orders." Static. Nothing. The seconds stretched on. A drop of sweat ran down under the soldier's helmet. The prisoner, still on his knees, gave a little smile. Crimson didn't move a millimeter. Then the radio crackled. "Good day to you, chief of the Bandit Republic." A deep voice, hoarse, calm. The voice of an old man who had seen too many battlefields to get worked up over the phone. General Gérard Eldrath himself. Crimson turned his head slightly toward the radio. "General Gérard. I don't think you know who you're dealing with." Behind the unit leader, a young soldier leaned toward the man next to him and whispered: "The general's gonna send in the army. He won't be laughing then." His neighbor didn't answer. Blood was still running from his nose. The radio crackled again. "Take back your man, Crimson, if you let my soldiers leave." Total silence. The young soldier opened his mouth, closed it, then opened it again. "Wait… what?" The unit leader turned to him with a look that clearly meant: shut up . Crimson stood still for a long moment. Then the red orb of his staff stopped pulsing. The soldiers felt the heat leave their veins all at once, like a hand loosening its grip. "Take off his handcuffs," Crimson said simply. The soldier who had tackled the fugitive looked at his leader. His leader looked at the radio. The radio said nothing more. "… Do what he says." The clink of the handcuffs echoed in the silence of the desert. The prisoner got up rubbing his wrists, scraped a little dignity together from the sand and rejoined the clan mercenaries without looking back. As he passed the young soldier, he gave him a wink. "Nice run, huh?" The Toride vehicle arrived a few minutes later, in a cloud of red dust. No one spoke while the soldiers climbed aboard. The twenty black helmets crammed into the back, rifles between their knees, without taking their eyes off the dune where the Chimamire clan still stood. The engine roared. The vehicle turned around and drove off toward the border. In the back, the young soldier couldn't hold it in anymore. "I don't get it." "Shut up," his neighbor muttered, a blood-soaked handkerchief under his nose. "No, seriously. That's Crimson. The most wanted criminal in the world. He was right there, five meters from us, and the general… he just lets him go? Like that?" "Did you see what he did to us without even moving? What did you want, for us to shoot him?" "I don't know! Send in the army! Tanks! A bomb! Anything!" The unit leader, sitting up front, didn't turn around. "The general made his decision," he said. "He saved twenty lives today. Period." The young soldier opened his mouth, then closed it. Through the rear window he watched the clan silhouettes shrinking at the top of the dune. "Still," he muttered. "It's weird." No one answered him. On the dune, Crimson watched the vehicle disappear over the horizon. He stayed still until the sound of the engine had completely died away. The clan member who had just been freed came over, head down. "Boss… thank you. I…" "Your partner is dead." It wasn't a question. The fugitive lowered his head even further. "Yes, boss." Crimson said nothing more. He turned and began to climb back up the dune, staff in hand, his cape of black feathers quivering in the hot wind. The mercenaries followed him without a word. Behind them, the wind was already erasing the footprints in the sand.
